Therefore, it can rescue the drowning populace from the currents of transmigration,
and pull out deeply rooted karma from endless kalpas.
It far opens the paths of the Three Vehicles,
and widely establishes the road for humans and devas.
Furthermore, when great bodhisattvas practice,
they prioritize the pāramitā of dāna (giving).
When they establish their ultimate doctrine,
they begin with pagodas and monasteries.
Giving leads to recompense;
it is not a futile expense.
Benefiting leads to merit;
how can it be called doing nothing?
Moreover, as subtle principles gradually diminish,
extravagance and luxury become rampant.
The fault lies in the minds of people;
how does it concern the sagely concern?
Thus, the lofty hall Bólíang and the jade seal [of the emperor]
were not the intentions of Yáo and Shùn.
Luxurious residences and sumptuous food
were certainly not the will of Śākyamuni.
Now, the Great Zhōu governs the world, and its pure customs spread afar.
It upholds the moral order throughout the six directions,
and spreads the net of virtue across the eight wastes.
There are no men who strike the waves in rivers [to protest],
nor scholars who hide in valleys [due to discontent].
All four classes of people are at peace in their occupations,
and all officials diligently fulfill their duties.
Fine grains accumulate in the central fields,
and granaries are piled high until they decay.
We are about to sing praises of great peace by striking the ground,
and pat our bellies while observing the flourishing transformation.
My child, why are you constrained by baseless worries and impoverished thoughts?
The ancients sighed, saying:
‘Talent is indeed hard to come by.’
It is true!
Among Kǒng Mén’s three thousand disciples and the outstanding talents within the four seas,
those selected for the four sections did not exceed ten.
Among them, Bó Niú suffered a serious illness;
Huí Yě died young;
Shāng Yě was stingy;
Cì Yě was a merchant;
Qiú Yě accumulated wealth;
Yóu Yě was fierce and obstinate.
Yet, the whole world revered and supported them
as the paragon of human ethics,
and admired their noble conduct
as models for officials.
For a hundred generations, people cherished their enduring influence,
and for a thousand years, they looked up to their glorious deeds.
As for śramaṇas who bitterly resist worldly restraints,
their hair and skin, though trivial, are valued by worldly people,
but śramaṇas discard them like worn-out sandals.
Fame, position, wealth, and beauty are what sentient beings cling to,
but śramaṇas regard them as chaff.
This is to endure what others cannot endure,
and to abandon what others cannot abandon.
They can be called bridges to transcend the world,
and excellent paths for propagating the Dharma.
Recording their sincerity in renouncing the mundane
is sufficient to offset the four offerings.
Collecting their noble deeds
can repay the four kindnesses.
How much more so for those who excel beyond this?
Even Kūnlún Mountain, rich in jade,
still has pebbles and sand.
The floating water [of the Jīnshā River], abundant in gold,
how could it be without earth and stone?
Among śramaṇas, many truly observe meditation and precepts,
but it is not without three or five who fall short of the precepts.
It is proper to reject people because of the Way,
but one should not reject the Way because of people.
My child, why do you, upon seeing this, forsake Buddhism?
Therefore, the Sūtra says:
‘Rely on the Dharma, not on the person.
Rely on wisdom, not on consciousness.’
One must not, upon seeing the actions of Zhòu and Zhí, disregard the paths of Yáo and Kǒng.
Nor should one, upon observing the deeds of Devadatta, forget the wisdom of Mañjuśrī.
Now I shall briefly explain the gist to you.
The Three Vehicles all lead out of saṃsāra,
yet their profound journeys have shallow and deep aspects.
The Nine Schools all enlighten the world,
but how can their profundity be without general and specific meanings?
The Confucian Classics say:
‘Filial piety is the root of virtue,
the source from which teachings arise.’
Since it is called the root of virtue,
its Way is higher than the traces of benevolence and righteousness.
As the source of teachings,
the ancient classics are thereby propagated.
Thus, they lead to the same destination by different paths,
and share one goal with a hundred considerations.
Filial piety and compassion are the general principles;
why are you confused, my child?
The Confucian system is the overarching one;
why do you doubt it, my child?”
Thereupon, the young lad smiled pleasantly and said:
“Upon the construction of Bólíang,
one realizes the narrowness and meagerness of a thatched hut.
Looking up at the ever-high sun and moon,
how can hills and mounds be compared?
Beholding the vastness of the true Dharma,
one realizes that worldly teachings are superficial.
Searching the true discourses of the Two Canons,
I understand the deceitful absurdities of the Three Zhāngs.
The Buddha was born in the Western Regions, his form and demeanor unseen,
but his teachings flowed to the Eastern Land, allowing us to hear their lingering sounds.
Yet, his divine traces are vast and distant, his principles defy description,
and cause and effect are utterly remote, beyond words.
Now, with my shallow mind, I have been privileged to hear profound discussions,
and my doubts and stagnation have melted away like spring ice.
Only now do I realize that the vast Buddhist canon encompasses the Two Truths,
and the solid Confucian school comprises the Nine Schools.
Truly, this transcends ordinary discourse and cannot be adequately praised!
I am indeed not intelligent;
I respectfully accept your excellent instruction.”
Your subject, Zhēn Luán, respectfully presents this memorial.
By imperial edict, I am commanded to make a detailed comparison of Buddhism and Daoism,
to determine their precedence, depth, similarities, and differences.
Your subject, not weighing his own inadequacies,
has carefully recorded the findings to present.
Your subject humbly submits that the teachings of the Buddha and Dào differ in their paths.
Their manifestations, concealment, and transformations are also distinct.
Their profound subtlety and mystery are not easy to detail and measure.
Furthermore, in a direct comparison,
Buddhism takes causality (因緣) as its core principle,
while Daoism regards natural spontaneity (自然) as its meaning.
Natural spontaneity means achieving without action.
Causality means attaining through accumulated practice.
Adhering to one's foundation, affairs become tranquil and principles harmonious.
Deviating from the core principle, intentions become perverse and teachings false.
When principles are harmonious, beginning and end are as one.
When teachings are false, nothing is beyond limits.
Considering Lǎozi’s five thousand characters, both the diction and meaning are magnificent.
Truly, it is highly estimable.
It is rich in the principles for self-cultivation, governing the state, and ruling the people.
Therefore, Daoism possesses methods of talismans, incantations, and curses.
Buddhism forbids strange powers, violence, and actions that go against compassion.
When compared to each other,
this causes people to doubt their righteousness.
How can this be the intention of the Great Dào, which is natural, void, tranquil, and non-active?
Perhaps it is because later generations deviated from the original and wantonly fabricated interpretations.
Moreover, Daoist methods regard achieving immortality as becoming a god.
Consequently, they deceive and subtly benefit themselves at present.
In the past, Xú Fú deceived and sought to establish a state among the barbarians (夷丹).
Wénchéng and Wǔlì practiced sorcery and deception in the Hàn era.
The Sān Zhāng (three Zhāngs) spread deceit in Xīliáng.
Sūn Ēn caused disturbances in Dōngyuè.
These great pests have been falsely accused throughout history.
When they are used to guide government, government often becomes perverse.
When they are used to lead the people, the people often become deluded.
Examining their scriptures, chapter after chapter contradicts itself.
Discussing their principles, they have no merit from beginning to end.
In ancient times, Xíng Fù (行父) was such a person:
When he saw someone respectful towards his ruler,
he respected them as a filial son caring for his parents.
When he saw someone disrespectful towards his ruler,
he detested them as a hawk or falcon pursuing small birds.
Xūanní (孔子) said:
"A noble person serving his superior,
when advancing, thinks of exerting loyalty; when retreating, thinks of rectifying faults.
He will follow the good and rectify the evil.
Thus, superiors and subordinates can be close to each other."
The Chūnqiū Zhuàn (春秋傳) says:
"When the ruler says something is permissible, but there is a flaw,
the subject should offer what is permissible to remove the flaw."
What kind of person is your subject?
By imperial edict, I am asked, how dare I not answer truthfully?
The two scrolls of the Dàodé Jīng (道德經) can be considered the core of the scholarly forest.
As for what is doubtful or erroneous, please consider removing the extreme parts and revising them.
The Five Thousand Characters (五千文) says:
"When a superior scholar hears of the Dào, he diligently practices it.
When an average scholar hears of the Dào, he seems to retain and yet to lose it.
When an inferior scholar hears of the Dào, he laughs loudly at it.
If he doesn't laugh, it cannot be called the Dào."
Your subject, adopting the view of an inferior scholar, has therefore written three scrolls of Xiàodào Lùn (笑道論), totaling thirty-six articles.
The three scrolls mock the name Sān Dòng (三洞).
The thirty-six articles mock the fact that their scriptures have thirty-six sections.
I present this with sweat and trembling, my heart and soul losing their composure.
Respectfully submitted.
The 15th day of the second month, the fifth year of Tiānhé of the Great Zhōu.
Zhēn Luán, former Cènglì and founding Earl of Mùjí County, your subject, respectfully presents this.
1. Tàishàng Dàojūn (太上道君) created heaven and earth.
The earliest records call him Lǎozi.
It says that when the virtue of King Yōu of Zhōu declined,
Lǎozi wished to cross the pass westward.
He arranged with Yǐn Xǐ to meet three years later in the Qīngyáng Gān (青羊肝) market in Cháng'ān.
Lǎozi was then born from the Empress's womb.
At the appointed time, Yǐn Xǐ saw someone selling Qīngyáng Gān.
He then inquired and saw Lǎozi rise from his mother's arms,
with white hair and beard, sixteen feet tall.
He wore a heavenly crown and held a golden staff.
He led Yǐn Xǐ to convert the Hú (胡).
He then hid in Shǒuyáng Shān (首陽山).
Purple clouds covered him.
The Hú king suspected sorcery.
He boiled him in a cauldron, but it did not get hot.
Lǎo Jūn (老君) became greatly enraged and struck the Hú king dead.
His seven sons and a portion of the people also died.
The king then submitted and commanded his people to be converted.
They shaved their heads, refrained from marriage, and received two hundred and fifty precepts.
They made images of Wú Xíng (吾形) and worshipped them with incense.
Lǎozi then transformed his body:
his left eye became the sun, his right eye the moon.
His head became Kūnlún Shān (崑崙山), his hair the stars.
His bones became dragons, his flesh beasts, his intestines snakes.
His belly became the sea.
His fingers became the Five Sacred Mountains (五嶽).
His hair became grass and trees.
His heart became the Huágài (華蓋) canopy.
Even his two kidneys combined became the true essence of parents.
Your subject, Luán, laughs and says:
The Hàn Shū (漢書) says:
"Cháng'ān was originally named Xiányáng.
When Emperor Gāozǔ of Hàn pacified the world, he planned to make Luòyì his capital.
Due to Lóu Jìng’s admonition, he sighed and said:
'I shall make Cháng'ān here.'
Thus, it was named."
How could Lǎozi have known about Cháng'ān before King Yōu existed,
and arranged a meeting with Yǐn Xǐ there?
Furthermore, the Sāntiān Zhèngfǎ Hùndùn Jīng (三天正法混沌經) says:
"At the beginning of chaos (混沌),
the clear qi became heaven, and the turbid qi became earth.
Then the forms of the Seven Luminaries and myriad phenomena came into being long ago."
How could Lǎozi only transform into the sun, moon, mountains, and rivers after converting the Hú?
If so, then before King Yōu,
heaven and earth, and all things, had not yet been born.
How then do Daoist scriptures speak of the Sān Huáng (三皇), Wǔ Dì (五帝), and Sān Wáng (三王)?
Therefore, heaven and earth would have originated from King Yōu.
Moreover, the Zào Tiāndì Jì (造天地記) says:
"Kūnlún Shān is four thousand eight hundred li high.
Above it are Yùjīng Shān (玉京山) and Dàluó Shān (大羅山).
Each is four thousand eight hundred li high.
The three mountains combined are fourteen thousand four hundred li high."
The Guǎngshuō Pǐn (廣說品) also says:
"Heaven and earth are separated by one hundred thousand five thousand li."
It calculates that Zǐwēi Gōng (紫微宮) is above five hundred million layers of heaven.
This means it is millions of li higher than Kūnlún Shān.
Yet Lǎo Jūn's heart is the Huágài canopy,
his liver is the Qīngdì Gōng (青帝宮),
his spleen is the Zǐwēi Gōng,
and his head is Kūnlún Shān.
I do not know what crime Lǎo Jūn committed to be standing upside down on the earth,
with his head below and liver above.
Is it because he is upside down that his view is also inverted?
Taking Cháng'ān as the year he crossed the pass,
and King Yōu as the age of creation,
if this is used to convert beings,
how can it be accepted?
The Dàodé Jīng Xù (道德經序) says:
"Lǎozi, in the first year of Shànghuáng (上皇), the dingmao year,
descended to be the Master of Zhōu.
In the first year of Wújí (無極), the guichou year, he left Zhōu and crossed the pass."
Laughing, I say:
"Ancient emperors and kings had no reign titles for their years.
It was not until Emperor Wǔ of Hàn that the first 'Jiànyuán' (建元) was created.
Later kings followed this, continuing to this day.
Shànghuáng is a wild fabrication, deeply laughable."
Moreover, the Wénshǐ Zhuàn (文始傳) says:
"Lǎozi, since the Sān Huáng,
served as the National Master (國師) in every generation and converted the Hú."
It also says that during Tāng's time, he was Xīshòu Zǐ (錫壽子).
In early Zhōu, he was Guōshú Zǐ (郭叔子).
Since he was a National Master, he should have transmitted classic texts.
Why is he not mentioned?
Why are only people like Yī Yǐn, Fù Yuè, Lǚ Wàng, Kāng Shào listed?
As for Fù Yuè,
only Lǎozi is noted as the Zhùxià Shǐ (柱下史).
Daoists note him as the Master of Zhōu.
This means he was a civil official.
How could historical records not mention this?
Moreover, the first year of Shànghuáng was a dingmao year.
Calculating the Jī (姬) dynasty, it lasted over seven hundred years.
No title of Shànghuáng has ever been heard of.
All historical records indicate that
Lǎozi crossed the pass during King Jǐng's time.
Kǒng Qiū died in the sixteenth year of Duke Āi of Lǔ,
which was during King Jìng's time.
King Jìng was the son of King Jǐng.
King Jǐng was more than ten generations after King Yōu.
This means Kǒng and Lǎo were contemporaries.
Yet the Huàhú Jīng (化胡經) says:
"On the day of King Yōu, he crossed the pass."
It doesn't mention him ever returning.
How could he have met Kǒngzǐ?
The Huàhú Jīng also says:
"He was the Zhōu Zhùshǐ for seven hundred years."
From the beginning of Zhōu to King Yōu,
there were only over three hundred years.
How could such a fabrication be made?
However, the years of Shànghuáng and Wújí are fictitious Daoist names.
Therefore, the Língbǎo (靈寶) says:
"In the first year of Shànghuáng, I saved people for half a kalpa."
At that time, human lifespans were eighteen thousand years.
How could a title from half a kalpa ago be adopted for recent times?
This is utterly laughable!
Moreover, Shànghuáng and Wújí are both ignorant fabrications.
The authors, wishing to divinize their techniques,
still added reign titles to dates,
hoping to find believers to follow them.
It also says:
generation after generation serving as national preceptors.
Gě Hóng's 葛洪 *Shénxiān Xù* 神仙序 already fully explains what is considered strange.
When the sage emerged, his priority was to rescue and assist.
Yet Xià Jié 夏桀 oppressed and tormented the common people.
Chéng Tāng 成湯 and Wǔ Dīng 武丁 yearned for worthy men.
Why did Lǎo Zǐ 老子 not assist worthy rulers nor instruct tyrannical governments?
He merely cultivated himself and preserved his nature.
When he was approaching one hundred years of age,
knowing his death was nigh, he secretly journeyed west.
He exclusively instructed Yǐn Xǐ 尹喜 to read and recite,
but did not encourage him to transmit it to others.
He died in Guānzhōng 關中, and his tomb is still there.
Qín Yì 秦佚 mourned him, crying out three times before departing.
Scrutinizing earlier transmissions and later wild theories,
though they claim to venerate,
they actually insult the Dào 道.
The *Tàishàng Sān Yuán Pǐn* 太上三元品 says:
In the first grade of the Upper Primal (Shàngyuán Yī Pǐn 上元一品), the primal energy of the celestial palace first condensed.
The Three Luminaries opened brightly, and the green and yellow energies established the three palaces of the Upper Primal.
The first palace is named Xuándū Yuányáng Qībǎo Zǐwēi Gōng 玄都元陽七寶紫微宮.
Therein exists the Primal Yang energy of the Green Primal (Qīngyuán Shǐyáng zhī Qì 青元始陽之氣),

which governs all the Supreme Perfected (Shàngzhēn 上真), the Natural Jade Palaces (Zìrán Yù Gōng 自然玉宮), the Numinous Treasure Supreme Emperors (Língbǎo Shànghuáng 靈寶上皇), the various Heavenly Emperors and Kings (Zhū Tiāndìwáng 諸天帝王), and the Supreme Sages and Great Spirits (Shàngshèng Dàshén 上聖大神).
Their palaces are all composed of five hundred fifty-five thousand five hundred fifty-five myriad layers of green yang energy.
Within them, the divine immortals, officials, and populace each have five hundred fifty-five thousand, and so on, up to the aforementioned myriad layers.
All are formed by the condensation of the natural green primal energy.
The layers, officials, and populace of the Nine Palaces (Jiǔ Gōng 九宮) are all identical to those of Zǐwēi 紫微.
Your servant laughs and says:
The *Sāntiān Zhèngfǎ Jīng* 三天正法經 says:
Before the heavenly light was bright and the accumulated mists were clear,
after more than seven thousand kalpas, the Dark Scenery (Xuánjǐng 玄景) first separated.
Nine energies existed.
Each energy was separated by ninety-nine thousand nine hundred ninety *lǐ* 里.
The green energy ascended and cleared, while the turbid mixed energies descended.
And the Nine Heaven True Kings (Jiǔtiān Zhēnwáng 九天真王) and the Primordial Heaven King (Yuánshǐ Tiānwáng 元始天王) were born within the nine energies.
The energies condensed and took form.
Then there were the Emperors of the Nine Perfected (Jiǔzhēn zhī Dì 九真之帝).
All were formed by the condensation of the clear energy of the nine heavens into the positions of the Nine Universes (Jiǔyǔ 九宇).
The Three Primal Ladies (Sānyuán Fūrén 三元夫人) were born from the energies and resided in the Dòngfáng Gōng 洞房宮, attended by three thousand Jade Boys (Yùtóng 玉童) and Jade Girls (Yùnǚ 玉女) each.
Taking heaven as father and energy as mother,
they gave birth to the Lords of the Three Primal (Sānyuán zhī Jūn 三元之君).
Also, the *Língbǎo Zuì Gēn Pǐn* 靈寶罪根品 says:
The Supreme Dào Lord (Tàishàng Dàojūn 太上道君) bowed to the Primordial Heaven Honored (Yuánshǐ Tiānzūn 元始天尊) and inquired about the Dharma of the Ten Virtues (Shí Shàn 十善), etc.
Thereupon, the Heaven Honored commanded the divine immortals to gather and each explain the causal conditions.
Saints as numerous as the sands of the Ganges had attained the Dào 道 and become Tathāgatas.
Those who had not yet attained it were also as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
Also, the *Yuánshǐ Chuán* 元始傳 says:
Heaven corresponds to hell.
The good ascend to heaven, the wicked enter hell.
If we reason based on this explanation, it is not so.
Why? The Primordial Heaven King (Yuánshǐ Tiānwáng 元始天王), the Supreme Dào Lord (Tàishàng Dàojūn 太上道君), and all the heavenly divine beings (Zhū Tiān Shénrén 諸天神人)
were originally formed by the condensation and transformation of the natural clear primal energy.
They were not formed by cultivating precepts.
Since they were not originally formed by upholding precepts,
how can they expect me to exclusively practice good deeds and hope to attain that state?
Also, the *Dùrén Běnháng Jīng* 度人本行經 says:
The Supreme Dào Lord (Tàishàng Dàojūn 太上道君) said:
“In immeasurable kalpas, I have saved countless beings.”
The Primordial Heaven Honored (Yuánshǐ Tiānzūn 元始天zun) bestowed upon me the title of Tàishàng 太上
due to my merits in this causal connection.
Inferring from this, there are doubts.
For example, the *Yǒuwú Shēngchéng Pǐn* 有無生成品 says:
“Emptiness is the mother of all things,
the Dào 道 is the father of all things.”
This implies that the Dào 道 existed first, and then sentient beings came into existence.
However, this is the father of the Dào 道,
not something created by sentient beings.
Since the Dào 道 is like this,
why do sentient beings need to cultivate goodness to create it?
Moreover, the Dào 道 gives birth to all things.
The beginning of the creation of things is therefore the origin.
Since I was originally born and had no accumulated defilements,
how can there be the distinction of suffering and joy in the six paths and four births?
This is also impossible.
It also says:
“The divine consciousness of sentient beings inherently exists from the beginning,
not born of the Dào 道.”
If the Dào 道 can give birth to all things,
is not divine consciousness also a thing?
This is also impossible.
The *Sāntiān Zhèngfǎ Jīng* 三天正法經 says:
Once the nine energies separated,

the Nine True Heavenly Kings (Jiǔzhēn Tiānwáng 九真天王), down to the Three Primal Ladies (Sānyuán Fūrén 三元夫人), the Lords of the Three Primal (Sānyuán zhī Jūn 三元之君), and the Supreme Dào Lord (Tàishàng Dàojūn 太上道君), took form.
When the Emperor (Huángdì 皇帝) first established the common people, he formed figures from earth in the wilderness.
After three years, they could speak.
Each resided in a different region.
Thus there were Cāng 秦, Yí 夷, and Qiāng 羌 (peoples).
The five emotions converged with virtue, and the five laws were natural.
They received the energy of the Supreme Perfected (Shàngzhēn 上真) and thus became human.
Your servant laughs and says:
The good and evil karma and their retributions in the *Sānyuán Pǐn* 三元品 all originate from one's own self.
Also, the *Yuánshǐ Chuán* 元始傳 says:
If one is licentious, thieving, and unfilial,
upon death, one enters hell to suffer the five torments and eight difficulties.
Later, one is reborn among the six types of livestock and barbarians.
Inferring from this,
the contradictions are too great.
Furthermore, on the day the Emperor's (Huángdì 皇帝) earth figures were made,
it took three years for the energy of the Supreme Perfected (Shàngzhēn 上真) to enter before they could speak.
This energy of the Upper Clarity (Shàngqīng 上清) has the same origin as the Supreme (Tàishàng 太上).
If there was no good or evil before,
why would it enter the earth figures
and immediately fall into the eight difficulties, becoming barbarians?
These earth figures
also had no cause beforehand.
How could there be distinctions between central and peripheral (civilized and barbarian) after their creation?
Moreover, was the energy of the Supreme Perfected (Shàngzhēn 上真) foolish or intelligent?
If it was foolish,
it should not have been able to speak after entering the earth.
If it was intelligent,
it should have recognized the five torments and eight difficulties.
How could it not delight in goodness and joy, but rather desire suffering and difficulty?
Inferring from all these points,
it is deeply laughable.
The *Wénshǐ Chuán* 文始傳 says:
Lǎo Zǐ 老子, in the first year of the Supreme Emperor (Shànghuáng Yuánnián 上皇元年), descended to become the preceptor of Zhōu 周.
In the first year of Wújí 無極, he rode a blue ox in a thin-board carriage across the pass.
He explained the five thousand characters to Yǐn Xǐ 尹喜, saying:
“I roam between heaven and earth.
You have not yet attained the Dào 道,
so you cannot follow me.
You must recite the five thousand characters ten thousand times.
Your ears will hear thoroughly, your eyes will see thoroughly,
your body will be able to fly, achieving the six supernatural powers and reaching everywhere.
We shall meet in Chéngdū 成都.”
Yǐn Xǐ 尹喜 followed his words and achieved this.
When he visited and met him,
he arrived in the mountains of Jìbīn 罽賓 and Tántè 檀特.
There, when the king tried to burn and sink him with fire and water,
Lǎo Zǐ 老子 sat in a lotus flower and recited scriptures as before.
The king pleaded for mercy and repented.
Lǎo Zǐ 老子 then designated Yǐn Xǐ 尹喜 as his teacher.
He said to the king:
“My teacher is called the Fó 佛 (Buddha).
Buddha's work is supreme.
The Dào 道 king followed him and was converted.
Men and women shaved their heads and did not marry wives.
This supreme Dào 道 relies on the awe-inspiring power of the Fó 佛.
He appointed Yǐn Xǐ 尹喜 as the Fó 佛 of the kingdom of Jìbīn 罽賓,
named Míngguāng Rútóng 明光儒童.”
Chén xiào yuē:
Guǎngshuō Pǐn yún:
Shǐ Lǎo guówáng wén Tiānzūn shuōfǎ,
yǔ qīzi jù dé Xūtuóhuán guǒ.
Qīnghé Guówáng wén zhī yǔ qúnchén zào Tiānzūn suǒ,
jiē báirì shēngtiān.
Wáng wèi Fàntiān zhī shǒu,
hào Xuánzhōng Fǎshī.
Qī wénfǎ tóng fēi wèi Miàofàntiānwáng.
Hòu shēng Jìbīn hào Fèntuólì Wáng,
shāhài wú dào.
Xuánzhōng Fǎshī xū huàdù zhī.
Huàshēng Lǐ shì zhī tāi,
bāshí'èr nián pōu zuǒ yì,
shēng ér báishǒu.
Jīng sān yuè chéng báilù yǔ Yǐn Xǐ xīyóu yǐn Tántè.
Sān nián Fèntuólì Wáng liè jiàn biàn shāochén.
Lǎozi bù sǐ.
Wáng fú biàn tìfà gǎiyī,
xìng Shì míng Fǎ hào Shāmén.
Chéngguǒ wèi Shìjiāmóuní Fó.
Zhì Hàn shì fǎ liú Dōngqín.
Yòu Wénshǐ Chuán:
Lǎozi huà Hú tuī Yǐn Xǐ wéi shī ér huà Hú.
Xiāobīng Jīng yún:
Yǐn Xǐ tuī Lǎozi wéi shī yě.
Wénshǐ Chuán yún:
Wú shī hào Fó.
Fó shì wúshàng dào.
Yòu yún:
Wúshàng Dào chéng Fó wēishén wěi Yǐn Xǐ wéi Fó.
Tuī cǐ zhòng tú shī dì luàn yǐ.
Hé míngjiào zhī cún hū?
Yòu Huàhú Xiāobīng Jīng jiē yán:
Lǎozi huà Jìbīn shēn zì wèi Fó.
Guǎngshuō Pǐn:
Fèntuólì Wáng Lǎo zhī qī yě.
Dédào hào Shìjiāmóuní Fó,
jí Qín Hàn suǒ liú zhě.
Xuánmiào Piān yún:
Lǎozi rù Guān zhì Tiānzhú Wéiwèi Guó,
rù yú fūrén Qīngmiào kǒu zhōng.
Zhì hòunián sìyuè bārì pōu zuǒ yì ér shēng.
Jǔ shǒu yuē:
Tiānshàng tiānxià wéi wǒ wéi zūn.
Sānjiè jiē kǔ hé kělè zhě?
Xún Jìbīn yī guó nǎi yǒu wǔ Fó jù chū.
Yī shì Yǐn Xǐ hào Rútóng zhě.
Èr shì Lǎozi huà Jìbīn zhě.
Sān Lǎozi zhī qī Fèntuó Wáng hào Shìjiā zhě.
Sì Lǎozi zài Wéiwèi zuò Fó,
yì hào Shìjiā.
Wǔ Báijìng Wángzi Xīdá zuò Fó,
fù hào Shìjiā.
Àn Wénshǐ Chuán yún:
Wǔbǎi nián yī xián qiānnián yī shèng.
Jīn wǔ Fó bìng chū,
bù jué fán hū?
Ruò yán shèngrén néng fēnshēn huàwù,
shuōjīng yì bì duōfāng.
Hé wèi lǎohuà zé duō,
jīng wéi èr juǎn bù biàn?
Zhì yú Rútóng Yǐn Xǐ Fèntuó Fójīng,
wú wén yú jīn.
Dàn shì Báijìng Wángzi suǒ shuō.
Yǐ cǐ tuī zhī,
Lǎo Xǐ wèi Fó,
xūwàng kě pù.
Qiě Lǎo Jīng mìshuō bù xǔ rén wén.
Qiánhòu xiāng fān chéng yǒu yuǎnyì.
Rán Lǎo néng zuò Fó,
zhǐ shì yīrén dàoshì.
Bùzhī fèng Fó huò zhī shèn yǐ.
Rú fù wèi dàoshì,
qǐ yǐ dàorén zǐ wèi dàoshì?
Qǐ yǐ dàorén gù,
ér bù rèn qí fù hū?
Wǔliàn Jīng yún:
Mièdù zhě yòng sè zēng.
Tiānzi yī pǐ.
Gōng Wáng yī zhàng.
Shùmín wǔ chǐ.
Shàng jīn wǔ liǎng ér zuò yī lóng.
Shùmín yòng tiě wǔsè shí wǔ méi,
yǐ shū yù wén.
Tōngyè lù mái.
Shēn sān chǐ.
Nǚqīng Wén yuē:
Jiǔ zǔ yōuhún jí chū chángyè rù guāngmíng tiān,
gōng qí chú fàn sānshí'èr nián,
huán qí gù xíng ér gēng shēng yǐ.
Chén xiào yuē:
Sānyuán Pǐn zhōng tiāndì dàshuǐ Sāngōng Jiǔfǔ Jiǔgōng yìbǎi èrshí Cáo,
zuì fú gōngxíng,
kǎoguān shū zhī wú yǒu chācuò.
Shàn zhě yìshòu è zhě duósùn.
Qǐ yǒu bù yīn yèxíng zhí yòng wǔ chǐ zēng,
ér lìng jiǔ zǔ yōuhún rù guāngmíng tiān,
sānshí'èr nián huán gù xíng yé?
Bùrán zhī tán,
yú sī kějiàn.
Jì Wǔliàn zhī wén,
chū tiāndì wèi fēn zhī qián,
zhì jīn yì yìngyòng zhě,
zé sānshí'èr nián hòu chuān zhǒng ér chū yě.
Ěrmù suǒ zhī,
hé wèi Xīhuáng yǐ lái,
bù wén dàoshì sǐ shī jiǔ zǔ cóng dì chū zhě yé?
Bùrán zhī zhuàng,
yòu kě xiào yě.
Jīn jiāoyě gǔzhǒng,
yì yǒu xué kāi yān.
Fēi dàoshì zǔfù gēngshēng zhī chù hū?
Yì kě qǐchǐ.
Yǒu dàoshì zào Lǎo xiàng,
èr Púsà shì zhī.
Yī yuē Jīngāngzàng.
Èr yuē Guānshìyīn.
Yòu dàoshì fú huángbù pèi,
huò sì fú pā tōngshēn pī zhī.
Tōu Fósēng jiāshā fǎfú zhī xiàng.
Qí fú huáng pèi,
nǎi shì gǔ xián zhī yī,
héng bèi jiā qián liǎng dài zhě,
jīn xī xiāochú,
xuésēng fú xiàng.
Chén xiào yuē:
Àn Zhūtiān Nèiyīn Bāzì Wén yuē:
Fànxíng luò kōng jiǔ chóng tuī qián.
Tiānzhēn Huángrén.
Jiě yuē:
Fànxíng zhě,
Yuánshǐ Tiānzūn,
yú Lónghàn zhī shì hào yě.
Zhì Chìmíng nián,
hào Guānyīn yǐ.
Yòu àn Shǔ Jì yún:
Zhāng Líng bì nuè Qiū shè zhōng,
dé zhòuguǐ zhī shù.
Zì zào fúshū yǐ kuáng bǎixìng.
Wèi dàshé suǒ tūn.
Dìzǐ chǐ zhī,
yún báirì shēngtiān.
Líng zǐ Héng wèi Xìshī.
Héng zǐ Lǔ wèi Sìshī.
Yǐ zǔ yāofǎ huòluàn tiānxià.
Hàn Shū yún:
Liú Yān yǐ Lǔ wèi Dūyì Sīmǎ.
Suì shā Hànzhōng Tàishǒu Sū Gù,
biàn dé Hànzhōng.
Guǐdào huàrén.
Shí chuán huángyī dāng wáng.
Lǔ suì lìng qí bùzhòng gǎizhe huángyī jīnpèi,
dài Hàn zhī zhēng.
Zì ěr zhì jīn huáng fú bù jué.
Xiàng fú Shāmén.
Liáng kě bēi yě.
Qiě lìshēn zhī běn,
zhōngxiào wèi xiān.
Zǐ xiàng fù shì tiāndì bù lì.
Guānyīn jí wèi dàshì.
Lǎozi bù jí dàxián.
Ér lìng zǔfù lì shì zǐsūn shì bùxiào yě.
Yòu xí Zhāng Lǔ nìrén zhī fú,
shì bùzhōng yě.
Jì xié bùzhōng bùxiào,
hé zú zhǒng yān.
Lǎozi's Preface states:
The Way of Yīn and Yáng transforms into myriad things.
The Way is born in the east,
representing wood and Yáng.
The Buddha is born in the west,
representing metal and Yīn.
The Way is the father, the Buddha is the mother.
The Way is heaven, the Buddha is earth.
The Way gives life, the Buddha gives death; the Way is the cause, the Buddha is the condition.
Both Yīn and Yáng cannot be separated.
The Buddha is born of the Way.
Great Vehicle adherents of the Way of goodness
naturally have no origin of birth.
At the Buddhist assembly, they sit in a large circle,
following the square shape of the earth.
At the Daoist assembly, they sit in a small circle,
following the round shape of heaven.
Daoists do not engage in military service
because they are like women, having the Yīn qi.
Therefore, they are not subjected to military conscription.
Daoists who take up arms
know that Daoists do not bow to emperors or kings
(like women in deep chambers who do not interfere in politics).
Daoists who bow to emperors and governors
do so by engaging in politics as officials.
Daoists at assemblies who drink wine are without fault.
Buddhists at assemblies do not drink,
for women drinking wine commits one of the seven grounds for divorce.
Daoists at assemblies do not fast,
for they preside over life and must eat to live.
Buddhists at assemblies hold fasts,
for they preside over death and do not eat in death.
Also, like women who observe dietary restrictions.
Daoists sit alone,
like women who observe chastity.
Daoists gather and lodge together, so there is nothing to constrain them.
Your servant laughed and said:
The Wénshǐ Zhuàn says:
The Way is born in the East, wood, male.
The Buddha is born in the West, metal, female.
Now, if we analyze this using the Five Phases,
then metal can overcome wood.
Wood considers metal its official/demon (guānguǐ).
Metal considers wood its wife/wealth (qīcái).
Based on this, the Buddha is the Way's guānguǐ,
and the Way is the Buddha's qīcái.
It also says:
The Way giving birth to the Buddha is not logical.
How can Yīn and Yáng and the Five Phases have wood that gives birth to metal?
Therefore, it is known that the Way does not give birth to the Buddha.
Daoists sit in a large circle
because they are the officials of the Way.
Daoists sit in a small circle
because they are pressured by officials from above.
Daoists do not pay military tax
because they are of the royal lineage, hence exempt.
For ordinary Daoists, military tax is normal.
If the Daoist scriptures are like this,
then exemption from military tax would violate Daoist teachings.
Moreover, the Língbǎo Dàjiè says:
Daoists do not drink wine and do not associate with the powerful.
How can this great precept be violated?
The subsequent chaos
has no clear aim at all.
It also says:
Daoists consider fasting a dead ritual,
hence they do not fast.
Why not eat to their fill all day to nourish this body
and instead promote abstaining from grain and ingesting qi in pursuit of the art of longevity?
In the end, it cannot be seen through,
becoming a discussion of catching shadows.
It also says:
Daoists sleep alone, Daoists gather and lodge together.
According to this, uniting qi
and the Yellow Books cannot be arbitrary.
The Wénshǐ Zhuàn says:
Heaven is forty-nine thousand li away from Earth.
The sun and moon pass directly for three thousand li each,
circulating six thousand li.
Heaven and Earth are ninety million li apart at noon and midnight.
The four corners of mǎo and yǒu are also like turning shapes.
The Jìkǔ Jīng says:
Kūnlún Shān is fifteen thousand li high.
Your servant laughed and said:
According to the Jìkǔ Jīng,
Heaven and Earth are fifteen million li apart.
This completely differs
from the previous Wénshǐ.
The Wénshǐ Zhuàn says:
The sun and moon circulate six thousand li,
with a diameter of three thousand li.
According to the rule, the circumference should be nine thousand li.
Why is it only six thousand?
Furthermore, "Heaven is round and Earth is square" is a constant Daoist saying.
Now, if the four corners are equal to the square,
then Heaven and Earth would both be round.
The Huàhú Jīng says:
The upper limit of Buddhist law only reaches the Thirty-three Heavens,
not reaching the eighty-one heavens of Daoism.
It also says:
Kūn Shān has nine layers, each layer nine thousand li apart.
The mountain has four sides.
Each side has one heaven.
Thus, four times nine is thirty-six heavens.
The first layer is where Dìshì resides.
Now, Kūn Shān is calculated to be fifteen thousand li high,
and it has nine layers.
Each layer is nine thousand li high.
Then the total height would be eighty-one thousand li.
Why then is it said to be fifteen thousand li?
How greatly inconsistent!
Truly laughable.
The Wénshǐ Zhuàn says:
After myriad myriad myriad myriad years,
a great flood, and Kūnlún Shān flies and floats.
At that time, flying immortals welcome and take the Heavenly King and good people,
settling them on the mountain.
After another myriad myriad myriad years, a great fire arises.
At that time, saints fly to welcome the Heavenly King and people,
settling them on the mountain.
Your servant laughed and said:
The Jìkǔ Jīng says:
Heaven and Earth are burned in a kalpa, completely empty.
The clear qi becomes heaven, the turbid qi becomes earth.
Then Jùlíng and Húhài create mountains, rivers, sun, and moon as before.
Kūn Shān flying and floating might allow welcoming people and settling them on the mountain.
But if Heaven and Earth are entirely burned and the mountain is consumed by fire,
it cannot stand alone by itself.
How can the king and people be welcomed and settled on the mountain?
Moreover, the Dùrén Miàojīng says:
Above five hundred million layers of heavens is the Dàluó Heaven.
There is Yùjīng Shān,
which disasters cannot reach.
Considering Tàishàng's compassion,
why not welcome them to Yùjīng?
If he watches them die and does not welcome them,
that is not compassionate.
If he cannot welcome them,
that is deception.
Furthermore, the Dùrén Běnxíng Jīng says:
The Way states, "I follow the kalpas of life and death."
Yet, Dàshàng Dàojūn,
residing above Dàluó,
where disasters cannot reach,
still says he follows the kalpas of life and death.
How can other flying immortals
welcome and take the Heavenly King and good people,
settling them on the mountain to save them from death?
This is profoundly foolish
and laughable.
The Wǔfú Jīng says:
Zhōnghuáng Dàojūn said:
Heaven gives birth to myriad things, and humans are the most precious.
The human body encompasses Heaven and Earth, without anything it does not emulate.

It establishes an emperor, sets up three Excellencies, nine Ministers, twenty-seven Grand Masters, eighty-one Primary Officers, nine provinces, one hundred twenty commanderies, and one thousand two hundred counties.
The gallbladder is the emperor, the Great Dao Lord.
The spleen is the empress.
The heart is the Grand Commandant.
The left kidney is the Minister of Education.
The right kidney is the Minister of Works.
The eight spirits and the navel are sealed as the nine Ministers; the twelve stomach spirits and the three sanjiāo spirits
combine to form the twenty-seven Grand Masters.
The spirits of the four limbs are eighty-one Primary Officers,
totaling one hundred twenty,
to emulate the number of commanderies.
Also, the lungs are the Ministry of Personnel,
and the liver is the Imperial Secretariat.
Your servant laughed and said:
Checking the Daoist scriptures for names of provinces and counties,
the wording appears to be a recent production.
Ancient counties were large and commanderies small,
as seen in the Chūnqiū and Zhōushū Luògào.
Now, it is reversed, with commanderies larger than counties.
Is this not a Daoist scripture from before the Chūnqiū period?
It is deceitful, confusing, and erroneous, not worth reading,
and laughable.
The Huàhú Jīng says:
Lǎozi converted the Hú.
The king did not accept his teachings.
Lǎozi said:
"If the king does not believe,
I will go south to Tiānzhú to convert various nations.
My Way will greatly flourish.
From here south, none will be more revered than the Buddha."
The Hú king still did not believe and said:
"If you go south to convert Tiānzhú,
I shall bow my head and declare 'Nāmó Fó'."
Also, there was the Jiāyí Kingdom in the Liúshā Sài,
constantly plagued by bandits.
The Hú king was troubled by this.
He sent men to guard the fortress, who were constantly worried.
Thus, the men were called Yōupósài.
Women also feared being plundered by Jiāyí,
and were also worried about their husbands being trapped by the Yi.
Thus, they were called Yōupóyí.
Your humble servant smiled and said,
"What does 'Námó' mean?
This word means 'taking refuge in' or 'reverently bowing to.'
It also means 'save me.'
What does 'Yōupósài' mean?
This means 'pious male believer.'
'Yōupóyí'
means 'pious female believer.'
If we follow Lǎozǐ's words,
and the Buddha appeared in the south,
then one might say 'Námó Fó.'
If he appeared in the west,
could one then say 'Xīmó Fó'?
If it is said,
'A man guarding a pass can be named Yōusài,'
and 'a woman fearing her husband might be endangered can be named Yōuyí,'
then one wonders about 'pó.'
Could one then worry about one's grandmother?
Such interpretation based on individual characters
is ugly, clumsy, distressing, and humiliating,
truly laughable.
The Dòngshén Sānhuáng Jīng [Scripture of the Perfected Spirits of the Three Sovereigns]
refers to the Western Regions' immortals as 'Huángwén.'
This means the origin of written characters from bird tracks from before the Sānhuáng.
It also says,
'The Sānhuáng [Three Sovereigns]
are the most revered deities of the Sāndòng [Three Caverns],
the ancestral qi of the Great Existence.
The Tiānhuáng [Heavenly Sovereign] governs qi,
the Dìhuáng [Earthly Sovereign] governs spirit,
and the Rénhuáng [Human Sovereign] governs life.
The three combine to perfect virtue, and all things are transformed and born.'
Your humble servant smiled and said,
The Nánjí Zhēnrén Wènshì Pǐn [Chapter on the True Man of the South Pole Answering Questions] states,
'The Língbǎo Zhēnwén [True Script of the Numinous Treasure] in thirty-six scrolls
is located in the Xuántái Yùshì [Jade Chamber of the Mysterious Terrace] on Yùjīng Shān [Jade Capital Mountain].
Large characters of true script fill it.
When heaven and earth are destroyed and created ten thousand times over,
the true script alone shines brightly.'
This true script
is the script of the Sāndòng.
The Sānhuáng are the revered deities of the Sāndòng,
they certainly did not come after the Sāndòng.
At that time, there were no birds or beasts;
how can it be said to be the origin of bird tracks from before the Sānhuáng?
If Fúxī is considered one of the Sānhuáng,
then according to Huáinánzǐ,
'The Huángdì [Yellow Emperor] commanded Cāngjié to observe bird tracks and create characters.'
This would place it only in the time of the Huángdì.
How can it be said to be the origin of bird script from before the Sānhuáng?
The Huàhú Jīng [Scripture on the Conversion of the Barbarians] says,
Jiāyè Púsà [Kāśyapa Bodhisattva] said,
'Five hundred years after the Tathāgata's nirvāṇa,
I came to the east and imparted the Way to Hán Píngzǐ.
He ascended to heaven in broad daylight.
Two hundred years later,
I imparted the Way to Zhāng Líng.
Another two hundred years later,
I imparted the Way to Jiànpíngzǐ.
Another two hundred years later,
I imparted it to Wǔshì.
After that, in the late Hàn dynasty, the Way declined and was not followed.
In the seventh year, jiǎzǐ, of the Yǒngpíng reign of Hàn Míngdì [Emperor Ming of Han],
a star appeared in the west during the day. At night,
Míngdì dreamed of a divine being sixteen feet tall with a halo of light around his neck.
The next morning, he asked his ministers.
Fù Yì said,
'A crown prince of a Hú kingdom in the west achieved enlightenment and was named Fó.'
Míngdì then dispatched Zhāng Qiān and others.
They explored the source of the river [the Yellow River],
passed through thirty-six kingdoms, and reached Shèwèi [Śrāvastī].
The Buddha had already entered nirvāṇa.
They copied scriptures totaling six hundred thousand five thousand words.
They returned in the eighteenth year of Yǒngpíng.'
Your humble servant smiled and said,
"The Hànshū [Book of Han] says,
'Zhāng Líng was a person of the time of Hàn Shùndì [Emperor Shun of Han] in the Later Han dynasty.'
He studied as a sojourner in Shǔ.
He entered Hèmíng Shān [Crane's Cry Mountain] and was swallowed by a snake.
Counting Shùndì,
he was the seventh-generation grandson of Míngdì.
Logically, he could not have lived more than a hundred years before Míngdì.
It also says,
'Míngdì dispatched Zhāng Qiān to seek the source of the river.'
This is also a fabrication.
According to the Hànshū,
Zhāng Qiān was sent by Hàn Wǔdì [Emperor Wu of Han] of the Former Han dynasty to seek the source of the river.
How could Hàn Míngdì of the Later Han
send him again?
I wonder what kind of long-lived immortal Zhāng Qiān was,
serving as an envoy for generations?
What a hardship!
And how laughable is this fabricated citation!
The Zhūtiān Nèiyīn Dìsān Zōng Piāotiān Bāzì Wén [Eight-Character Text of the Third Chapter of Inner Sounds of All Heavens, Floating Heavens] says,
'Zéluò Jué Pútái Yuán Dàluó.'
The Qiān Tiān Zhēnhuáng Rén [True Human Sovereigns of a Thousand Heavens] explain:
'Zé is the name of a mountain in the heavens,
the dwelling place of many dragons. Luòjué is the inner name of a Dàojūn [Lord of the Dao].
Pútái is the hidden title of a Zhēnrén [Perfected Person].
The Jade Terrace is located on the sunny side of Zé Mountain.
Thirty thousand suns and moons illuminate its left and right.
The Arhat Moon Lady
caused great kalpic disaster.
The suns and moons of all heavens gather beneath the Jade Terrace.
The division of the Great Thousand Worlds,
the world changes, and the Great Thousand is completely altered.'
Your humble servant smiled and said,
"The Jìkǔ Jīng [Scripture for Relieving Suffering] says,
'After qián and kūn [heaven and earth] were completely altered, Jùlíng and Húhài were made to create mountains and rivers, and Xuánzhōng was made to create suns and moons.'
Thirty trillion lǐ south of Kūnshān [Kunlun Mountain], there is another Kūnshān.
In this sequence, there are a thousand Kūnshān,
called a Small Thousand World.
Another thousand Small Thousands
make a Middle Thousand World.
Another thousand Middle Thousands
make a Great Thousand World.
It is calculated that a Great Thousand World contains one hundred billion suns and moons.
Another scripture says,
'When a great kalpa occurs, heaven and earth change,
and no suns, moons, or stars remain.'
If they all gather, then one hundred billion would come.
Why do only three thousand arrive?
If the rest do not gather, is it because they are beyond the reach of the disaster,
or is it that their native realms are incomplete?
If they are indeed few,
even ordinary people on earth
are still illuminated by the sun and moon.
How could the more blessed beings in heaven
uniquely lack illumination?
Moreover, below the sun and moon
is the desire realm.
Lower beings are not called 'Dàluó Shàngjiè' [Great Net Upper Realm], which is beyond the reach of disaster.
If they do not come now,
is that reasonable?
I suppose that the creator of this scripture
only heard the name 'Great Thousand'
and was confused about the number of suns and moons.
Hence, it is as it is!
The Wénshǐ Zhuàn [Biography of Wénshǐ] says,
'Lǎozǐ and Yǐn Xǐ traveled in heaven,
entered the nine-layered Bái Mén Tiāndì [White Gate Heavenly Emperor] who bowed upon seeing Lǎo.
Lǎo ordered Xǐ to exchange courtesies with the Tiāndì.
Lǎozǐ said,
"Tàishàng is honorable and noble.
I will arrange a meeting for a specific day.
Tàishàng resides in the Qībǎo Gōng [Seven Treasures Palace] on Yùjīng Shān.
He is beyond all heavens,
silent, dark, pure, and distant."'
Your humble servant smiled and said,
"The Shénxiān Zhuàn [Biographies of Divine Immortals] says,
'Shěn Yì of Wújùn ascended to immortality in broad daylight.
Four hundred years later, he returned home
and recounted that
when he first ascended to heaven, he wished to see the Tiāndì.
The Tiāndì was too honorable to be seen.
So he first saw Tàishàng,
sitting in the main hall.
Several hundred men and women attended him.'
This description makes it clear
that Tàishàng is inferior to the Tiāndì.
The statement that Tàishàng is honorable, noble, and governs above all heavens is false.
Now, according to the Jiǔtiān Shēngshén Zhāng [Chapter on the Divine Births of the Nine Heavens],
Tàishàng resides in Xuándū Gōng [Palace of the Mysterious Capital].
His Yùqīng Gōng [Jade Purity Palace] is above Xuándū.
How can Héchóng Gōng [Palace of Crane Multiplicity] be above Yùqīng?
That would make it two levels higher than Xuándū.
Yet Lǎozǐ says,
'Tàishàng governs above all heavens.'
How mistaken this is!
The Huàhú Jīng says,
'During the time of the Sānhuáng practicing the Way, people did not die.
In ancient times,
heaven produced sweet dew and earth produced sweet spring water.
Eating and drinking these led to longevity.
In middle ancient times, heaven produced the five qi and earth produced the five flavors.
Eating these prolonged life.
In later ancient times, the world was meager; heaven produced wind and rain, and earth nurtured all beasts.
People hunted and ate them.
I grieved at this situation,
and therefore tasted the hundred grains to feed the common people.'
Thereupon, the Sānhuáng each offered five dòu of grain as a pledge,
requesting that their descendants for generations would not lack the five grains to sustain Shénzhōu."
Your humble servant smiled and said,
The Wǔfú Jīng 五符經 says:
"The Sānxiān Wáng 三仙王 reported to the Huángdì 皇帝:
The reason people live long
is that they do not eat the five grains."
The Dàyǒu Jīng 大有經 says:
"The five grains are the chisel that carves out life.
Eating the five grains shortens life.
This food entering the belly does not lead to long life.
If you wish not to die, have no feces in your intestines."
The Wǔfǔ Jīng 五府經 says:
"Huángjīng 黃精 is the qi 氣 of the three yang.
It ascends to the Tàiqīng Gōng 太清宮.
Eating it is sweet and delicious,
and it also prolongs life."
I do not understand why Lǎozǐ 老子 did not taste this,
but instead tasted the five grains that corrupt human intestines.
Furthermore, the Sānhuáng 三皇 were all divine beings.
Why did they not allow their descendants to reign in the land of immortality,
but instead, by means of five measures of grain, invited their descendants to reign in Shénzhōu 神州,
seeking the short life that carves out life and corrupts intestines? This is also laughable.
The Xuánmiào Nèipiān 玄妙內篇 says:
"Lǎozǐ 老子 entered the pass and went to Wéiwèi Guó 維衛國.
He entered the mouth of Qīngmiào Fūrén 清妙夫人.
Later, he was born by being cut from her left armpit.
After walking seven steps, he said:
'Above the heavens and below the heavens, only I am honored.'
Thereupon, the Buddhist dharma came into existence."
Your humble servant smiled and said,
The Huàhú Jīng 化胡經 says:
"When Lǎo 老 transformed the people of Jìbīn 罽賓, everyone revered the Buddha.
Lǎo 老 said:
'A hundred years from now,
there will be a true Buddha in the Dōushuài Tiān 兜率天.
He will take rebirth in the palace of Bájìng Wáng 白淨王 in Shèwèi 舍衛.
At that time, I
will also send Yǐn Xǐ 尹喜 to be reborn and follow the Buddha.
He will be known as Ānán 阿難,
and will compose the twelve divisions of scriptures.'
A hundred years after Lǎozǐ 老子 departed,
the king of Shèwèi Guó 舍衛國 indeed gave birth to a crown prince.
After six years of ascetic practice,
he achieved enlightenment and was called Buddha.
His name was Shìjiāmóuní 釋迦牟尼.
After forty-nine years, when he was about to enter Nirvāṇa 涅槃,
Lǎozǐ 老子 reappeared in the world, known as Jiāyè 迦葉.
Between the twin śāla trees,
he requested thirty-six questions from the Tathāgata for the great multitude.
Then the Buddha entered Nirvāṇa.
Jiāyè Púsà 迦葉菩薩 cremated the Buddha's body,
took the relicts, divided them among nations, and built stūpas.
Āyù Wáng 阿育王 also built eighty-four thousand stūpas."
Judging by these facts,
Lǎozǐ 老子 was originally not the Buddha.
If he were the Buddha,
how could he, in old age, burn his own old body and build a stūpa?
This is truly laughable.
Moreover, many of Lǎozǐ's 老子 scriptures say he became the Buddha,
or became a national preceptor.
How could all national preceptors in the world
and the Buddha necessarily rely on Bóyáng 伯陽?
To save people and transform customs,
must it require Lǐ Ěr 李耳?
If it is said that the Buddha cannot achieve it and must rely on the Daoist,
then from the beginning of qi 氣
there was only one Lǎozǐ 老子.
Were no other people allowed to comprehend the great Dao and become national preceptors?
This would mean Lǎo 老 was praising himself, saying "only I can do it."
Yet, the Buddhist scriptures state
that everyone, through their actions, can attain Buddhahood.
The Daoist scriptures do not describe this,
only referring to Lǎo Jūn 老君.
How is it that Buddhist teachings are so expansive,
while Daoist scriptures are so narrow?
Furthermore, these wild and baseless fabrications have no beginning or end.
The Shǔ Jì 蜀記 says
Zhāng Líng 張陵 was devoured by a snake,
yet it is recorded that he ascended to heaven in broad daylight.
The Hàn Shū 漢書 says
Liú Ān 劉安 was cut down by an axe,
yet it is said he achieved immortality. The Daoists falsely claim Lǎozǐ 老子 became the Buddha,
how can this not be strange?
They also composed the Tiāndì Jīng 天地經 which says:
"When he transformed the kings of the west,
Lǎozǐ 老子 transformed his body and departed.
His left eye became the sun,
his right eye became the moon."
However, the Xuánmiào Jīng 玄妙經 says:
"Lǎozǐ 老子 rode the essence of the sun into Qīngmiào's 清妙 mouth."
This would mean Lǎozǐ 老子 rode the essence of one eye into the mouth.
Considering that the Great Dao pervades the divine and is everywhere,
must it rely on a single essence to enter the womb?
If it must rely on essence,
and essence resides in the head,
then if he entered by way of the head,
both eyes would come along.
Now, to enter by riding one eye
would make the Great Dao one-sided.
This is also laughable.
Lǎozǐ's Huàhú Gē 老子化胡歌 says:
"When I was in Shèwèi 舍衛,
I instructed Gōután 瞿曇,
'You and Mahāsattva
bring scriptures to Dōng Qín 東秦.
Traverse the lands of Shénzhōu 神州,
until you reach the Eastern Sea.
Widely propagate the honored one's dharma,
teaching the deaf and ignorant people.
I grant you divine power,
to transform the Dao for a thousand years.
When the years are complete, you must return,
be careful not to cling to Dōng Qín 東秦.
Do not let the Tiāndì 天帝 be angry,
or Tàishàng 太上 will stamp his feet in rage!'"
Your humble servant smiled and said,
According to this, Gōután 瞿曇
is indeed Shìjiāmóuní 釋迦牟尼.
The Huàhú Jīng 化胡經 says:
"In the third year of Běnchū 本初, in the cyclical year bǐngchén 丙辰, of Zhōu Zhuāng's 周莊 reign,
Bájìng Wángzǐ 白淨王子 attained correct enlightenment,
and was named Fó Shìjiā 佛釋迦.
Lǎozǐ 老子, seeing his passing, feared people would grow lax,
so he descended again to Duōluó Jùluò 多羅聚落,
known as Jiāyè 迦葉.
He closely attended the Buddha,
cremated his body, took the bones,
and built stūpas, distributing them."
If, according to the text above,
Shìjiāmóuní 釋迦牟尼 had not yet been born,
he could not have been sent to the Eastern Lands in advance.
If he had already been born and achieved Buddhahood,
there would be no way
for him to receive Jiāyè's 迦葉 instructions and serve as his envoy for a thousand years.
How could a Bodhisattva, personally attending the Buddha, instruct the Buddha as an envoy?
Moreover, Zhōu Zhuāng's 周莊 reign
lasted only fifteen years.
The first year was yǐyǒu 乙酉, and there was no bǐngchén 丙辰 at all.
How could the era name Běnchū 本初 be so erroneous?
This is enough to make one cover one's ears.
Would it also make Tàishàng 太上 stamp his feet in rage?
The Dùrén Miàojīng 度人妙經 states:
"The demon kings of the three realms each have their incantations.
Recite them a hundred times, and your name will be recorded in Nángōng 南宮.
A thousand times, the demon kings will protect and welcome you.
Ten thousand times, you will ascend to the Great Void,
pass beyond the three realms, and become an immortal lord."
Furthermore, the Xuánzhōng Jīngjīng 玄中精經 says:
"Daoists receive precepts and talismans,
place them in the positions of the Five Sacred Mountains, set out wine and dried meat, and bow twice."
Your humble servant smiled and said,
The Guānshēn Dàjiè 觀身大誡 says:
"Those who study the Dao must not worship ghosts and spirits or bow to them."
Since they are demon kings of the realm of desire,
not yet having crossed all existences,
how can reciting their incantations a hundred times lead to being recorded in Nángōng 南宮?
Moreover, according to the methods of the Sān Zhāng 三張,
they sacrificed to the earth god and the stove god during the spring and autumn equinoxes.
During the winter and summer solstices, they performed sacrifices according to popular custom.
Military talismans, earth god contracts, and military generals engaged in battle.
There are no texts of prohibitions or admonitions.
These earth gods,
are they spirits or Dao?
If they are spirits,
Daoists should not bow.
If they are Dao,
no wine and dried meat should be offered.
How can one recite demon words with one's mouth and perform ritual sacrifices with one's body,
seeking to transcend the three realms?
Truly lamentable!
The Huàhú Jīng 化胡經 says: "The Buddha arose in the land of the Hu 胡.
The golden qi 氣 of the West is rigid and without礼 (lǐ).
The scholars of Shénzhōu 神州
imitate their rituals and build stūpas.
Everywhere they exclusively value the trivial and abandon the fundamental.
Their words are circuitous and do not accord with the subtle dharma.
They adorn and carve scriptures and images to deceive kings and ministers.
This leads to droughts and floods, and military conflicts throughout the land.
Within ten years, disasters will appear everywhere.
The five planets will lose their orbits, mountains and rivers will collapse and dry up.
The king's transformation is uneven, all due to the Buddha's disruption.
Emperors do not serve ancestral temples,
common people do not honor their ancestors.
Therefore, the spirits and Daoist qi 氣
cannot be rectified again."
Your humble servant smiled and said,
The Pǐn (品) chapter on the Root of Wisdom and Sin says,
Yuánshǐ Tiānzūn (元始天尊) said,
"During the first half-kalpa of the Yuánshǐ (元始) era,
I saved people and extended their lives for eighteen thousand years.
After I left, human hearts deteriorated, indulging in illicit sacrifices to evil gods,
killing living beings, praying, and harming each other.
They brought upon themselves early deaths and lives without a fixed lifespan."
Based on this,
if illicit sacrifices to evil gods make myriad deities rejoice,
and if one's qì (氣) aligns with the Dào (道), one should receive blessings.
How then would one's life be cut short and lifespan unfixed?
Furthermore, before the reign of Hàn Míngdì (漢明帝),
when Buddhist Dharma had not yet spread and the Dào (道) teachings were flourishing,
why were there frequent wars, successive droughts and floods,
blood rains, collapsing mountains, and continuous famines?
Moreover, there were Jie (桀) and Zhòu (紂) who roasted living beings.
Since Emperor Míng (明) onwards, Buddhist Dharma has been practiced for over five hundred years;
has there been any demonic disaster or tyrannical rule worse than before?
Comparing the present to the past,
who has been deceitful?
The facts are clear in historical records,
they cannot be concealed.
Though Luán (鸞) is mediocre and ignorant,
he has somewhat studied both teachings.
The Dào (道) teachings are humble and self-effacing,
feigning falsity to highlight the truth of Buddhism.
Buddhist Dharma is pure and righteous,
preserving reason to enlighten sentient beings.
If not for this understanding of the Dào (道),
then it would be ridiculously fatal.
Lǎozǐ's (老子) "One Hundred and Eighty Precepts of Strict Discipline" says,
"My precepts are extremely severe.
Speak them to a tree, and it will wither.
Speak them to an animal, and it will die."
Also, the Língbǎo Jīng (靈寶經) says,
"The Way of Xuán (玄) and Sù (素)
was cultivated by ancient people to extend their years and prolong their lives.
Modern people who cultivate it will shorten their years and diminish their lives."
Also, Dàoshì (道士) who receive the methods of the Three Generals' Prohibition and Suppression
can cause those they resent to become leprous, insane, or to die.
Also, the "Chapter on Saving Kings" says,
"From the east, Kāimíng (開明) beckons true deities whose bodies wear black turbans.
They have mysterious markings and are a hundred paces wide.
Their heads pierce the heavens, they feed on evil demons, and their mouths encompass mountains.
In the morning they eat five hundred, in the evening they devour three thousand, and fifty-five together they swallow."
Your humble servant smiled and said,
The Sān Yuán Dà Jiè (三元大誡) says, "Tiānzūn (天尊) preached the Ten Precepts, Ten Virtues, and other practices,
and countless people attained the Dào (道)."
The precepts say,
"Do not harbor evil thoughts.
Hearing the precepts and slandering them incurs sin."
Now, trees are insentient;
they do not worry about incurring sin or raising slander.
Why should they be cautioned to wither?
If they must wither and die,
then they are sentient.
If they are sentient,
they should awaken upon hearing the Dharma.
However, this is not logical.
Why use such words?
You know that modern people who cultivate these practices will shorten their lives, and disasters and poisons have already spread.
Is the Great Dào (大道) so tolerant as to allow this without restraint,
causing calamities to extend to future generations without redress?
Also, according to the methods of Sān Zhāng (三張), the "Fearful Ghost Rules" say,
"Wear the Tàijí Zhāng (太極章) on the left,
and the Kūn Wú Tiě (昆吾鐵) on the right.
Point at the sun, and it stops in the sky.
Aim at a ghost, and blood splatters a thousand li."
Also, making the Yellow God's Red Seal (黃神赤章) kills ghosts,
and the Vermilion Seal (朱章) kills people.
Or, for those performing the "mud-and-ash fasts" (塗炭齋),
they smear their faces with yellow earth,
hang their heads in donkey dung and mud, tied to a pole.
They are beaten until thoroughly soaked.
From the Yìxī (義熙) era of the Jìn (晉) dynasty,
the Dàoshì (道士) Wáng Gōngqī (王公期) abolished the beating method.
Yet, Lù Xiūjìng (陸修靜) still smeared his forehead with yellow earth,
and was bound backwards and hung by his head.
Such illicit sacrifices are ridiculed by all who witness them.
Also, concerning the Hàn Jiéyú (漢婕妤),
the emperor suspected her of cursing.
She replied,
"If ghosts and gods are sentient,
they would not accept an unreasonable curse.
If they are insentient,
what benefit is there in cursing them?
Therefore, I do not do this."
Based on this reasoning,
even an ordinary person's wisdom can comprehend this.
How much more so would ghosts, if they possess spiritual intelligence, be discerning and righteous, and not accept foolish resentment?
This has never happened.
Now, looking at this text,
its words and meaning are without merit,
like the tunes of vulgar shamans performing incantations.
How can the Great Dào (大道)
tolerate such things and not condemn them?
Are they not indulging in dregs and liquor, intoxicated all year round?
Reasoning sincerely,
how could this be so?
According to the "Ten Precepts, Fourteen Sustaining Body Sutra" (十誡十四持身經), it says,
"Bow once to the north.
The north is the beginning.
Then face east and circle the ten directions,
visualizing the true form of Tàishàng (太上)."
Your humble servant smiled and said,
The "Wénshǐ Chuán" (文始傳) says,
"Lǎozǐ (老子) and Yǐn Xǐ (尹喜) traveled in the heavens.
Xǐ (喜) wished to see Tàishàng (太上).
Lǎo (老) said,
'Tàishàng (太上) is in the Tàiluó Tiān Yùjīng (大羅天玉京).
The mountain is extremely remote.
You can pay respects to the palace from afar.'
So, he did not see him and returned."
Based on this,
Xuándū Yùjīng (玄都玉京), where Tàishàng (太上) resides,
is now in the upper reaches.
Why not take the upper direction as primary,
but instead foolishly bow to the north?
However, the Dào (道) was born in the eastern Yang (陽) region.
Why not take the east as the beginning?
The Buddha was born in the western Yin (陰) region.
The north is also Yin (陰).
Previously, it was scorned.
Now, it is revered and bowed to first?
Also, the "Chapter on the Root of Sin" says,
"Dàshàng Dàojūn (大上道君) bowed respectfully to Yuánshǐ Tiānzūn (元始天尊) in the Yángguǎn (陽館) and asked about the Ten Virtues and other practices."
These precepts were preached by Tiānzūn (天尊).
Why not bow to Tiānzūn (天尊),
but instead visualize Tàishàng (太上)?
Forsaking the root to pursue the branches,
whose fault is this?
Lǎozǐ's (老子) "Ice Melting Sutra" (消氷經) says,
"Lǎozǐ (老子) said to Yǐn Xǐ (尹喜),
'If you seek to learn the Dào (道),
first abandon the five attachments:
one, parents;
two, wife and children;
three, sexual desire;
four, wealth and treasures;
five, official positions and titles.
If you can eliminate these, then travel west with me.'
Xǐ (喜) was zealous and sharp.
He then cut off the heads of seven people and brought them.
Lǎo (老) smiled and said,
'I was testing your heart.
This cannot be done.
Those you killed were not your relatives, but merely birds and beasts.'
He looked down to see the seven heads were seven treasures,
and the seven corpses were seven birds.
Xǐ (喜) doubted and returned home,
where his seven relatives were all alive."
Also, the "Record of Creating Heaven and Earth" (造立天地記) says,
"Lǎozǐ (老子) transformed the Hú (胡) barbarians.
The Hú (胡) king did not submit.
Lǎozǐ (老子) killed him,
his seven sons, and a portion of his people."
Your humble servant smiled and said,
The Sān Yuán Jiè (三元誡) says,
"Those who study the Dào (道) must not harbor evil thoughts,
be unfilial to parents,
or not love wife and children."
Counting the parents killed by Xǐ (喜),
if he knew it was an illusion,
how could he have doubted and looked back?
If he sincerely harbored evil thoughts according to the precepts, he would have committed a grave sin.
How much more so for severing the heads of one's parents?
Also, the Hú (胡) king did not submit,
so his seven sons were killed.
This is also too extreme.
Moreover, to kill a portion of the people,
how profound is this lack of benevolence?
If this were to become a law for later generations,
it would cause all seekers of the Dào (道) to kill their parents and wife and children.
Also, how can one, because a single king did not submit, indiscriminately execute half the people of his country?
Considering this from various angles,
it is laughable and bizarre.
The Sān Yuán Pǐn (三元品) says,
"The Zǐwēi Gōng (紫微宮) Qīng Yánshēng Fú (青延生符) is written in the eight directions, and the eight qì (氣) respond, then a person is formed.
If the talisman is destroyed by burning,
the person follows the smoke and transforms into qì (氣).
This text appears once every forty thousand kalpas."
Your humble servant smiled and said,
The "Wénshǐ Chuán" (文始傳) says,
"Every myriad myriad myriad years, there is a great flood.
Kūnlún (崑崙) floats.
Immortals fly to welcome the Heavenly Kings and good people,
settling them on the mountains.
And even before that, for myriad myriad years,
heaven and earth were chaotic like a chicken's yolk,
called a kalpa."
According to this, on the day of the great flood, celestial beings do not die.
They should not need to be welcomed onto the mountains.
Also, the Jìkǔ Jīng (濟苦經).
After the Qúnkūn Dòngrán (乾坤洞然),
it was completely empty and desolate.
Calculating the time of one kalpa,
no people or things existed.
Its Yánshēng Fú (延生符) only appeared after forty thousand kalpas.
How could there be no celestial beings for forty thousand kalpas?
So dim and dark,
how distant it is!
Also, ten thousand times ten thousand is only one hundred million (yì).
One hundred million times one hundred million is only one trillion (zhào).
To speak only of one hundred million trillion years and say
"ten thousand times one hundred million times ten thousand times one hundred million" (wàn yì wàn yì),
is because the new scholars who composed the sūtras
do not know the magnitude of numbers.
The Dòngxuán Dōngfāng Qīngdì Sòng (洞玄東方青帝頌) says:
"The Nine-Five (Jiǔwǔ) does not permanently reside;
Heaven and Earth are subject to decline and danger.
A great kalpa ends a Tūn (椿) tree;
One hundred and six cycles return with the cosmic movement."
Your servant laughs and says:
"After the great flood has swept everything away,
Kūnlún (崑崙) floats;
then there is a great fire,
melting metal and iron, leaving the earth without grass.
Even after billions of years,
Heaven and Earth are like a chicken's egg yolk.
This is generally called one kalpa.
However, the Tūn (椿) is a worldly tree;
if burned by worldly fire, it turns to ash.
If it encounters kalpic fire, it will surely be extinguished.
To say that a great kalpa is as long as a Tūn tree,
how absurd is that!
It is also laughable.
As the Dùmìng Miàojīng (度命妙經) says:
'When a great kalpa reaches its cycle,
Heaven collapses and Earth sinks,
and the realm of desire (yùjiè) is extinguished and ceases to exist.'
The Tàipíng Dàojīng (太平道經) and the Buddhist Fǎhuá (法華) and its major and minor sections,
which circulate through the eighteen heavens above and below,
are within the realm of form (sèjiè) until a great kalpa cycle,
at which point their texts vanish.
The authentic texts and jade characters of the Sāndòng Shénjīng (三洞神經) of the Yùqīng Shàngdào (玉清上道),
which originated from Yuánshǐ (元始),
are in the Twenty-Eight Heavens (Èrshíbā Tiān), above the formless realm (wúsèjiè), in the Dàluó Yùjīng Shān Xuántái (大羅玉京山玄臺), where calamities cannot reach.
Therefore, these natural texts
are born and extinguished with the cosmic movement.
Those who reverently uphold them will enable their seven generations of ancestors to ascend to heaven,
and the Cakravartin (zhuǎnlún shèngwáng) will continue for generations without end."
Your servant laughs and says:
"The Dùrén Běnxíng Jīng (度人本行經) says:
'The Dao says, since Yuánshǐ (元始) first emitted light,
in the first year of Chìmíng (赤明),
after more than nine thousand billion kalpas,
a number of sentient beings like the sands of the Ganges (héngshā) were saved.
Thereafter, until the first year of Shànghuáng (上皇),
countless people were saved.
I follow the kalpas through life and death,
never ceasing through generations,
always appearing simultaneously with Língbǎo (靈寶).'
It further says: 'After enduring many kalpas and exhausting the nine qi,
I changed my destiny and took form in the womb.
The Hóng (洪) clan accumulated over three thousand years.
Until Chìmíng (赤明) was opened in the Jǐazǐ (甲子) year,

In the spring of the second year of Chéngguāng of Qí, Dōngpíng Gāoshì
summoned the former great monks of outstanding virtue to assemble at the palace.
The Emperor ascended his throne and expounded on the meaning of abolishing and establishing religions, saying:
"I have received the mandate of Heaven and brought peace to the realm.
For generations, the three teachings have been propagated, their influence reaching ever wider.
Upon careful examination, the ultimate truths contain many flaws in their civilizing influence.
Therefore, all of them must now be abolished.
However, the six Classics and the Rújiào [Confucian teaching] have profound writings on political arts,
and their rites, righteousness, loyalty, and filial piety are beneficial to the world.
Therefore, they must be preserved.
As for the true Buddha, there is no image; one reveres it from afar to express one's heart.
Buddhist sūtras widely extol the construction of magnificent images and stūpas.
The grand and beautiful constructions are said to bring immense blessings.
These are truly inanimate objects; how can they bestow grace?
Ignorant people believe in them, emptying their precious wealth, merely incurring expenses.
Therefore, they must be eliminated.
Hence, all sūtras and images must be destroyed.
Parents' kindness is profound, yet the Shāmén do not show respect.
This is extreme perversity, intolerable by the laws of the state.
All of them must return to their homes to uphold filial piety and governance.
This is My intention.
What do you, venerable monks, think of this reasoning?"
At that time, over five hundred Shāmén, including Dàtǒng,
all felt that the Emperor's authority was overwhelming and that dissuasion would be difficult to follow.
The abolition in Guānnèi had already been carried out, so their position was not isolated.
The assembly fell silent, and an imperial decree urged them to answer.
They all looked at each other, drained of color,
bowed their heads, and shed tears.
There was the Fǎshī Huìyuǎn,
renowned and esteemed.
He pondered to himself,
"The Dharma is entrusted to the four assemblies.
How can I be silent and claim to understand the principle?"
So he stepped forward and replied,
"Your Majesty governs a great domain and holds a revered position.
You adapt to the customs and establish the three teachings as a model.
The edict says,
'The true Buddha has no image.'
This is indeed as Your Majesty states.
However, sentient beings rely on the sūtras to hear of the Buddha and on images to manifest the truth for their eyes and ears.
If they are now abolished, there will be no means to inspire reverence."
The Emperor said,
"Everyone knows the true Buddha in the void.
There is no need for sūtras or images."
Yuǎn replied,
"Before the time of Hàn Míng, sūtras and images had not arrived.
Why then did sentient beings in this land not know the true Buddha in the void?"
The Emperor had no answer then.
Yuǎn said,
"If one can know the Dharma without relying on sūtras and teachings,
then before the Three Sovereigns, when there was no writing,
people should have naturally known the five constants and other principles.
Why, then, at that time, did people only know their mothers but not their fathers,
just like animals?"
The Emperor again had no answer.
Yuǎn said,
"If images are inanimate
and worshipping them brings no blessings, hence they must be abolished,
then are the images in the state's seven ancestral temples
sentient, that they are wantonly honored and served?"
The Emperor did not answer this challenge,
but said,
"Buddhist sūtras are foreign doctrines.
This country does not need them.
Abolish them and do not use them.
The seven ancestral temples were established by earlier generations.
I do not consider them correct either.
They will be abolished together."
Yuǎn said,
"If foreign sūtras are not to be used here,
then what Zhòngní [Confucius] said, originating from the state of Lǔ, and the lands of Qín and Jìn,
should also be abolished and not practiced.
Furthermore, if you consider the seven ancestral temples incorrect and intend to abolish them,
then you are not honoring your ancestors.
If ancestors are not honored, then the order of generations is lost.
If the order of generations is lost, then the five Classics are useless.
What is the meaning of preserving Rújiào earlier?
If so, then the three teachings would be abolished together.
How then would you govern the state?"
The Emperor said,
"The states of Lǔ, Qín, and Jìn, though their territories differ,
all belong to the one civilization of the monarch.
Therefore, they are not comparable to the difficulty concerning Buddhist sūtras and the seven ancestral temples."
The Emperor had no way to explain.
Yuǎn said,
"If Qín and Lǔ both follow one civilization,
and their teachings can circulate,
then Zhèndàn [China] and Tiānzhú [India], though their national borders differ,
are both within the four seas of Jambudvīpa, under the one civilization of the Cakravartin king.
Why then can they not both follow Buddhist sūtras, and now only they are to be abolished?"
The Emperor again had no answer.
Yuǎn said,
"The edict states,
'Return monks to their homes to cultivate filial piety.'
The Confucian Classics also say,
'Establish oneself and practice the Way to bring glory to one's parents.'
This is filial conduct.
Why must they return home?"
The Emperor said,
"Parents' kindness is profound; they rely on their children for care and support.
Abandoning one's kin for strangers is not ultimate filial piety."
Yuǎn said,
"If that is the case,
Your Majesty's attendants all have parents.
Why do you not release them?
Instead, you make them serve for years, unable to see their parents."
The Emperor said,
"I too, according to my rotation, can return home to attend to them."
Yuǎn said,
"The Buddha also permits monks to travel and cultivate the Way in winter and summer,
and return home in spring and autumn to attend to their parents.
Thus, Mùlián begged for food to offer to his mother,
and the Tathāgata carried a coffin to attend a funeral.
This principle is widely accepted.
It cannot be uniquely abolished."
The Emperor again had no answer.
Yuǎn raised his voice and said,
"Your Majesty now relies on royal power to arbitrarily destroy the Three Jewels.
You are a person of wrong view.
Avīci Hell does not discriminate between the noble and the humble.
How can Your Majesty not be afraid?"
The Emperor flushed with anger,
stared directly at Yuǎn, and said,
"As long as the common people can attain happiness,
I will not shrink from the sufferings of hell."
Yuǎn said,
"Your Majesty uses evil dharma to transform people,
planting karmic suffering in this life.
You will go to Avīci Hell together with Your Majesty.
Where can happiness be found?"
The Emperor, his argument defeated,
and his initial plans and intentions overwhelming, had nothing more to say.
He only said,
"Monks, you may return for now."
The officials recorded the names of the debating monks.
The Emperor had already carried out his persecution for three years.
The Buddhadharma in Guānlǒng was almost completely eradicated.
Upon conquering the Qí territory, he similarly destroyed it.
At that time, in Wèi, Qí, and the eastern regions of Chuān, Buddhadharma was flourishing.
There were over forty thousand existing temples.
All were bestowed upon princes and dukes as residences.
The five assemblies of Buddhist disciples, numbering less than three million,
were all returned to civilian and military status, reverting to registered households.
Buddhist images were melted down and sūtras were burned.
The wealth of the Three Jewels was confiscated by the government.
It was immediately awarded and distributed, completely exhausted.
The Emperor thought he had achieved his ambitions in the world.
Less than a year later,
a plague festered within him, and sores erupted on his body.
Evil omens were manifest.
There was no repentance to dissolve it.
He then retreated to Yúnyáng Gōng.
After only seven days, he suddenly collapsed and died.
Tiānyuán succeeded to the throne.
In the eastern and western capitals, Zhìhù Sì were established.
He punished the Bodhisattva monks to initiate the propagation of Buddhism.
Not long after, the Emperor died, the national destiny shifted, and it was not until Suí Gāozǔ that Buddhism greatly flourished.
This will be shown later.
Recently, I saw in Dà Táng Lìbù Shàngshū Táng Lín's Míngbào Jì,
that his maternal grandfather, Suí Wén Púshè Qí Gōng,
personally saw Emperor Wén asking a person who had died and returned to life.
This person said that upon first dying, he saw Zhōu Wǔdì, who said,
"Please convey this to the Son of Heaven of Great Suí.
Formerly, we shared food from the granaries, and the jade and silk
were also stored by me.
I am now suffering greatly for destroying the Buddhadharma.
Please perform meritorious deeds for me."
Emperor Wén issued an edict,
making it universal throughout the land,
for everyone to contribute one coin to pray for his well-being.
On the fourth day of the eleventh month of Jiàndé 6 (577 CE) of Zhōu.
The Emperor visited the new palace hall in Yè.
The Nèishǐ, Yǔwén Áng, and the Shàngshì, Lǐ Délín,
received the memorials from those presenting them.
At that time, Rèn Dàolín presented a memorial.
The Shàngshì looked at the memorial and said,
“You are of the two teachings.
The sagely sovereign’s keen debating skill is exceptionally difficult to counter.
You should consider it carefully.”
He replied,
“Your Majesty’s sharp debate is renowned throughout the ten directions.
I, Lín, have long heard of it.
Precisely because I have heard of your debating skill, I have come.
If I can debate, there will be no failure.” And so forth.
Then he was led in.
He ascended the steps and stood west of the imperial seat.
The Emperor decreed,
“Since you have presented a memorial to assist in guiding governance,
I greatly praise and value it.
You may state your points separately and clearly.
Do not be verbose.”
Then Lín presented a memorial on pacifying the remnants of Qí and reducing taxes and labor services.
The Emperor accepted it fully.
He then said,
“I, Lín, originally vowed to propagate the Buddha-dharma.
Just now, I exclusively discussed worldly politics,
which might seem like an attempt to flatter the ruler.
But in reality, it is the will of Heaven to protect the Dharma.
Since the propagation of Śākya’s teachings,
the provisional responses have been immeasurable, and the wisdom and methods extraordinarily profound.
They widely proclaim the true Dharma,
saving these five defilements and specially liberating the three existences.
Among humans and in the heavens, in the six paths and four births,
there are none who do not take refuge, turn towards it, and receive its enlightenment.
From the Hàn dynasty until now,
over five hundred years have passed.
Kings, dukes, ministers, and gentry have revered and transmitted it.
But upon the arrival of the great Zhōu, it has been suddenly abolished.
Your Majesty’s reign inherits that of former kings, and your transforming influence succeeds that of later emperors.
How can you exclusively target Buddhism and alone not follow ancient precedents?
If it were not good, the former sages would have long ago extinguished it.
If it is said to be beneficial, Your Majesty
may proceed with the meaning of abolishing Buddhism.
This is what your servant does not understand.”
The Emperor decreed,
“The Buddha was born in the Western Regions and his teachings were transmitted to Eastern Xià.
Its customs and teachings were originally very different from those of Zhōngguó.
During the Hàn, Wèi, and Jìn eras, it seemed to exist and yet not exist.
It was during the chaos of the Wǔ Hú that its influence flourished.
I am not one of the Wǔ Hú and have no reverence for it.
Since it is not a righteous teaching, I have abolished it.”
Rèn Dàolín memorialized,
“Buddhism has been transmitted to the East for over seven generations.
