Indeed, the Dao does not propagate itself.
Its propagation must come through people.
The common folk do not awaken by themselves.
Their awakening must await a master artisan.
Awaiting a master artisan, the world experiences periods of profound awakening.
Coming through people, the Dao has opportunities for modest achievements.
When opportunities are for modest achievements, the spiritual current ceases to flow.
When periods are for profound awakening, the mysterious cutting edge can be reached.
However, when a benevolent one has been absent for a thousand years, and contemporary teachers harbor perverse thoughts, right and wrong contend.
This causes the spiritual principles to quietly vanish and the subtle threads to be nearly disrupted.
At this time, there was Dharma Master Shí,
who was indeed a descendant of the earlier awakened ones.
He concentrated his thoughts on the great Dharma, his mind soaring to a high perspective.
He deeply examined the decline of the Dao
and grieved for the destitution of all living beings.
Thus, he roused his spiritual presence
and manifested himself in these degenerate times.
He inherited the grand lineage
and served as a bulwark for the era.
When the world was peacefully slumbering, he awakened it with a great voice.
When the times were nearing daytime darkness, he illuminated them with the sun of wisdom.
He sought to mend the decaying fabric in an age when the Dao was fading,
and gather the scattered threads in a time of decline.
Therefore, he seized the opportune moment to correct errors and rectify wrongs.
One strike, and the age had no dissenting voices.
A second strike, and the misguided returned to benevolence.
At this time,
the carriages of sheep and deer had their wheels broken.
The chariots of the six teachers were overturned.
The profundity of the two thoughts became clear,
and the subtlety of the one vehicle also became manifest.
Thus, he sat serenely east of the mountains, his reputation echoing across the eight directions.
He contentedly promulgated the teachings, and the nine streams of thought desired to follow.
Therefore, the two Heavenly Kings Fú and Yáo of Great Qín, with their armies and retinues, invited him.
These two kings
wandered in their minds through the gate of great enlightenment,
while their forms governed over myriad transformations.
Outwardly, they propagated the customs of Xī Hé;
inwardly, they advanced the art of propagating the Dharma.
Their Dao converged and their spirits mingled, humbly receiving the transmission in physical form.
He publicly stated that if the patriarch was not held in high esteem, then his Dao would not be honored.
Therefore, he concealed his spiritual treasures, acting only when moved by a suitable response.
From the time he manifested his presence in Qínchuān,
like the divine light of Zhú Lóng shining,
he expanded the great lineage like Xī Hé emerging from Fúsāng.
He integrated the constant Dao, exhausting the wonders of profound mystery.
He eliminated evil and awakened the common folk, perfecting the beauty of conventional teachings.
His words were timely, and his principles met with universal accord.
Thus, his debates were not futile,
and his propagation of the Dao was not in vain.
This was the Dharma drum resounding again in Yánfú,
and the Dharma wheel turning once more in the lands north of heaven.
Apart from one whose station transcends cultivation and attainment, whose essence is refined through a hundred trials, and whose actions and withdrawals are timely,
who else could achieve this?
In summary,
his propagation was as grand as the spring sun,
and his removal of calamities was as severe as autumn frost.
Thus, how majestic, how vast,
his boundless noble resonance!
However, due to a confined destiny and hidden circumstances,
it was as if dusk fell upon this person.
In the Guǐchǒu year,
at the age of seventy,
on the thirteenth day of the fourth month, he passed away at the Great Temple.
Alas, how sorrowful!
The master artisan of the Dao leans westward,
the spiritual axis crumbles eastward.
The morning sun sets,
the precious peak collapses.
The six directions are plunged into daytime darkness,
the confused carriages turn back nine times.
The divine gate is heavily shut,
the three evil paths eagerly open.
The night light is lamentable,
the blind children are pitiable.
Boundless sorrow,
a hundred hearts share the grief.
Therefore, a lament is made, saying:
The former awakened one ascended to the distant,
the spiritual wind is remote and vast.
The enlightened immortal secretly abides,
the true respondent is aloof and serene.
Clustering are the nine streams,
right and wrong contend.
Long suffering are the blind children,
their divine roots sunken and drowned.
When there is no guide for the times,
who will know the path through the darkness?
The great man, having far-reaching awareness,
his profound thoughts uniquely awakened.
Calm, detached, quiet, and silent,
he embraced this profound purity.
Responding to the opportune moment and riding the current of destiny,
he soared on wings along the heavenly path.
Since he responded to destiny,
he was worthy of the era's admiration.
Born with advantage,
his form bore extraordinary characteristics.
In swaddling clothes, he was outstanding and far-reaching,
in childhood, he had exceptional measure.
His thoughts did not require repetition,
his awakening did not await a master artisan.
He set foot upon the eight paths,
his spirit roamed in the three directions.
His mysterious roots stood out magnificently, his grand voice resonated far.
Moreover, he upheld his integrity,
suddenly abandoning worldly glory.
He leisurely entered the gate of the Dao,
honoring simplicity and purity.
When there were scriptures, he sought them out;
when there were wonders, he recorded them.
His propagation had no equal,
his lineage had no comparable clan.
Frost formed like ice,
his spirit was as stable as a mountain.
Outwardly aloof, he grew ever higher;
inwardly clear, he was ever more complete.
How grand, his noble resonance,
a model to imitate, a cause to follow.
How serene, his detached virtue,
truly wondrous, truly genuine.
In stillness, he communicated with the mysterious;
in action, he responded to people.
His words were a treasure for the world,
his silence a jewel for the times.
When the splendid customs were established,
the two teachings also became subservient.
Who says the Dao declines?
The mysterious transformation was just beginning.
Since his awakening,
the Dao was thoroughly propagated.
The spiritual wind fanned far and wide,
its lofty echoes soared high.
He broadened this great Dharma,
kindling this lamp of wisdom.
When the voice of the Dao first sang,
the net of worldly desires collapsed.
The roots of delusion were utterly uprooted,
the highest good greatly increased.
People's dwelling in the world,
their paths were limitless.
He integrated these myriad beings,
and mended this decaying fabric.
He acted in accordance with the four gratitudes,
and descended with the frost of wisdom.
Like that Vimalakīrti,
his traces mingled in the city streets.
Though his form perfectly responded,
his spirit soared in the Emperor's land.
Though the incoming teachings were subtle,
how could they be preserved?
How magnificent, the great man,
who uplifted perfect virtue.
He manifested these characteristics,
and revealed that profound tranquility.
He was enlightened through myriad wonders,
and restrained by mysterious principles.
He greatly promoted Prajñā
to respond to the lands north of heaven.
How could destiny be so adverse,
a hidden ending in the silent realm?
Who will now connect the heavenly path?
Who will block the three evil paths?
Alas, how sorrowful!
The perfect person acts without doing,
yet there is nothing left undone.
His expedient net reached far and wide,
his long snare bound from afar.
Pure grace cast its hook below,
wayfarers were caught above.
How earnest his good guidance,
how swift his sweeping influence.
The Dao could change customs,
the transformation could shift the times.
How could the vast heaven
destroy this spiritual rule?
Since the ultimate truth has departed,
the one Dao can no longer be spread.
Heaven and humanity weep,
grieving for the spiritual deities.
Alas, how sorrowful!
His passing,
was during the time of hundred-six.
The master artisan of the Dao sheathed his axe,
the Dharma wheel broke its axle.
The morning sun's light faded,
the jade peak toppled.
The universe was plunged into daytime darkness,
the times lost their eye of the Dao.
Pitiable, pitiable all living beings,
who will comfort, who will nurture them?
The whole world feels sorrow,
my grief is amplified.
Alas, how sorrowful!
Once, at a certain time,
I traveled through the river of benevolence.
Following its lingering waves,
I inherited its profound mystery.
Using it, there is no end;
delving into it, it becomes ever more solid.
Radiant, he abandoned worldly dust.
I reflect on the passing of many years.
My subtle feelings remain untold.
Already they have followed the transformative flow.
If only it could be redeemed,
I would trade a thousand for it.
Time cannot be awaited.
Life cannot be prolonged.
Neither self nor others
Had anything to rely on, no connections.
My thoughts race boundlessly,
My heart grieves to the vast heavens.
Alas, how mournful!
In the eleventh year of Yuánjiā, winter, eleventh month, Xīnwèi day,
Fǎgāng Fǎshī passed away.
Alas, how mournful!
Indeed, standing tall and rigidly upright causes harm in general service,
while being humbly compliant and agreeable compromises integrity.
Dwelling in the mountains brings the drawback of severe hardship;
residing in towns invites the troubles of noise and congestion.
The Fǎshī was one who weighed these two situations and chose between these two paths.
In his youth, he traveled in Huájīng, and in his later years, he dwelled in secluded foothills.
He found joy in going forth and returning, following his feelings in coming and going.
Disgusted by the human throng, he sought leisure among trees and rocks.
In the silent, deep valleys, he sought understanding among all things.
People thought he lacked unique principles,
but I saw that his principles were indeed true.
His nature was quick-witted and astute, gradually imbued with refined taste.
He calmly explored principles and appreciated and entrusted himself to literary meanings.
His friendships were sincere and honorable, ending in deep companionship.
His ambition was to emulate the eternal Way of Fùyǒng.
He managed his body according to the Dharma robes,
early severing the ties of official life (zhuóyīng).
He set foot in the divine realm,
having long ago settled the impediment of the crimson palace steps (dānchí).
How much more so the traces of the Sangmen's corrective actions,
which merely hover between coming and going!
In the past, by chance encounter, we became friends (qīnggài zhuójiāo).
Together we cast off worldly attachments.
We were friends among friends, sharing our thoughts and easing our frustrations,
thereby giving expression to those bygone years.
Then we journeyed hand in hand to Liáng, and perched wing to wing in Dèng.
We breathed the wind in the tranquil caves and plumbed the profound spring of the Way.
Our shared joy was like a banquet for a thousand years, a unique moment.
Since the woods were emptied and the birds scattered, a full cycle has passed in an instant.
You perched on a high branch, while I sank into the mud.
I always hoped for an opportunity to visit you in your secluded dwelling,
but it turned into the vast separation of Mount Liáng and the sea.
The eastern currents do not return, the western sun cannot be held back.
He reached the end of his journey by river, and his bones returned to Zēngqiū.
Alas, how mournful!
The elegy says: His clan was numerous and prominent,
indeed, a descendant of Tāng.
His illustrious name slightly declined in the middle,
but the source and flow remained clear.
Young, he suffered misfortune,
with no kin to wear mourning.
His compassionate aunt managed everything,
entrusting herself to his upbringing and care.
When he reached his mid-twenties,
his intelligence and grace were exceptionally outstanding.
Two extraordinary talents rivaled in brilliance,
a pair of equally gifted individuals.
He disdained the mundane world,
and yearned to ascend to the divine realm.
He shed the ties of mortal life,
and was devoted to eternal connections.
Having followed the profound path,
he fully understood its essence.
Beyond benevolence and righteousness,
he was not attached to worldly concerns.
He desired no worldly success,
and found contentment in tranquility.
He did not rely on grand residences,
but chose his dwelling among cliffs and walls.
He came without getting his feet wet,
and left without breaking his wings.
He soared and gathered,
advancing and retreating with gain and loss.
I detested drifting on the waves,
while you could grasp the mind itself.
We soared together in the swamp of the Way,
and gathered together in the forest of virtue.
We brushed against the harmonious wind together,
and listened to the profound sound together.
From palace to country,
in sight and in mind.
The past transformation is distant and vague,
my lingering thoughts are in a mournful reverie.
And then we parted,
the heavenly path clearly attested.
You left the old mountain,
I returned to a distant land.
We hoped to ride the harmonious current,
and share the shade and rest together.
The cold ashes emitted no smoke,
the falling leaves scattered.
Our shared wish could not be fulfilled,
you departed this world.
When a person passes away,
sentiments are veiled in sorrow.
Alas, how mournful!
The deep winter is piercingly cold.
The river banks are desolate.
Cold wind flutters the curtains,
flying sleet enters the boat.
Life has a near end,
the homeward journey is still long.
His life is ending with sorrow,
silently, mournful cries.
A solitary journey, like a duckweed.
The transformation is equal, with no praise.
Alas, how mournful!
I cherish the memory of our travels to Hǔqiū,
and mourn the passing of Lúlǐng.
I recall our shared selections in Zhōngjīng,
and think of our mutual support in Fānjìng.
My feelings drift to the twin peaks,
my thoughts linger on the two provinces.
How intimate and boundless!
What my heart holds, fills my chest.
I have witnessed the severe winter depart,
and the scorching summer has subsided.
The four seasons revolve in confusion,
but our longed-for bond is hidden forever.
If our future connection is not extinguished,
I think of his life, which increases my sorrow.
Alas, how mournful!
In the eleventh year of Yuánjiā, winter, tenth month, Gēngzǐ day,
Dàoshēng Fǎshī passed away on Mount Lú.
Alas, how mournful!
When a good person comes to an end,
those who grieve are not shallow.
When reason itself vanishes,
those who regret are even deeper.
The Fǎshī's original surname was Wèi.
He was from Péngchéng.
His father was the magistrate of Guǎngqī County.
As a child, he was extraordinary.
He was brought to Fǎtài Fǎshī,
changed his attire, and became a disciple.
His natural intelligence was keen, and his understanding was exceptional from an early age.
In his student years, he already ascended the lecturing platform.
At that time, renowned monks and celebrated scholars
all exhausted their words and humbled their thoughts, convinced by his profound insight.
Lǔlián's defeat of Tiánbā,
Xiàngtuō's challenge to Kǒngsǒu,
scarcely surpassed him.
Furthermore, his nature was calm yet firm and resolute.
His temperament was harmonious and easy to follow.
He guided others with joy and generosity,
thus his influence grew greater.
In middle age, he traveled to study, extensively gathering unusual knowledge.
From Yáng to Qín, he ascended Lú and trod Huò.
The profound essence of Ròushí's Mahayana,
the crucial points of Dípó's Hinayana,
he thoroughly understood their meanings and completely grasped their profundities.
What he heard daily excelled, what he saw surpassed the abstruse.
Then he awakened, saying:
“Symbols are merely borrowed for principle;
clinging to symbols leads to迷失去principle.
Teachings are what transformation relies on;
being bound by teachings obscures transformation.
Thus, seeking reality by scrutinizing names
is confused by虛誕.
Seeking the mind to respond to affairs
blurs profound maxims.
From the transmission from Hú to the learning inherited in Zhōnghuá,
no one has been able to transcend this realm.”
So he collected his stray thoughts and moved uniquely, preserving and practicing the traces of the past.
Thereupon, all the sutras unfolded like clouds, and all doubts melted like ice.
Śākyamuni's profound meaning became clear and discoverable.
All strange and marvelous sayings became common discourse.
Dānzhōu's exposition of the name-teaching,
Xiùbì's grasp of the profound mind,
were easy for him.
Things are wary of brilliance, people fault integrity and transcendence.
Resentment arose among his peers, and he preferred to break away from group excursions.
So he lowered his wings and drew back his feet,
concealing his presence in mountain caves, following the Way of obscurity.
He cast his lot with the path of Yúgōng, who embarked on a boat.
There was going but no returning; his life ended at the foot of the mountain.
Sorrow arose throughout the land.
Alas, how mournful!
The clarity of the Sì Bìan rivers,
the steepness of Lǚ Liáng.
It is this auspicious spirit
that nurtured this brilliant talent.
Like orchids among grasses,
like jades among stones.
It was not said to be nurtured or carved,
yet it formed this fragrant splendor.
From his early studies,
he absorbed profound doctrines.
What he heard, he understood in his heart;
he analyzed texts and formulated strategies.
While young, he ascended the讲 (jiǎng) platform,
no chapter went unanalyzed.
He excelled in concise speech,
not valuing ornate words.
Those with insight admired and received him,
weary of convoluted arguments.
In middle age, he scrutinized teachings,
but his understanding was not yet complete.
Therefore, he traveled far and wide,
seeking out hidden depths.
Although he encountered diverse doctrines,
he felt them to be even more similar.
When his path reached its end with no return,
he turned his chariot and changed his course.
He pruned away superficial names,
and expounded on the essence of things.
What obstruction did not flow away?
What obscurity did not become clear?
It was like the sun rising from the east,
its light shining brightly.
The four fruits and ten stages of Bodhisattva-hood
were used to inspire and uplift.
The oxen and horses of the Yì Jīng,
the fish and birds of Zhuāng Zǐ—
who could verify their reality
without losing their way from this path?
He lingered in this awakening,
and gave me instructive words.
The Way truly lies here,
and all who listened were enlightened.
Not only did he stand firm,
but he also refuted those who disparaged extensive learning.
I said it was harmless,
and encouraged its propagation.
His understanding accorded with true sincerity,
his teachings transcended frivolous clamor.
Silently, he shielded the great,
and quelled malicious gossip.
He fostered those who secluded themselves or were outstanding,
exceeding the bamboo groves and thickets.
His thoughts retreated to the springs,
unhindered by rivers or mountains.
He wished to entrust himself to leisure,
saying, "The benevolent live long."
But fate has its limitations,
it cannot be eternal. Orchids and irises quickly wither;
spirit is harmed by companionship.
Alas, how sorrowful!
I recall our first parting,
three autumns ago, at dusk.
The wind was bleak, the stream clear,
the clouds high, the forest bare.
We bade farewell at Nán Pǔ,
clasped hands and went our separate ways.
Vast and distant was his departure,
sad and lingering was my gaze. Who remains hidden and obscure?
Each followed their own path.
Grieved by this long separation,
our destinies were forever divergent.
Alas, how sorrowful!
Recalling the wind that came,
its fading echo bade him farewell.
The clouds had no cause.
Three winters have already passed,
and the New Year brings this spring.
Hearing the joyful birds of spring,
beholding the warm, hazy aura.
Remembering the schools in this month,
truly a propitious time for learning.
Feeling the emptiness of the silent lecture hall,
grieving the void of the high seat.
Sighing that reason must be restrained by circumstance,
grieving that emotions lead to missing people.
Alas, how sorrowful!
The Way of Heaven is vast and obscure, yet its order can be inferred.
Truth does not perish, perhaps all will return to it.
The transient can be overlooked, but affection can be pursued.
This short composition is not for display, but merely to express my grief.
Alas, how sorrowful!
Indeed, in formulating theories that accord with reason,
no hundred schools have ever found them to be completely correct.
Understanding things from one's own mind,
one does not worry about stumbling.
Yet, in the end, they could not discern from each other.
If we all sigh and lament, and if fallen ones are ultimately saved, who would know?
He hoped that if his actions were established, good and evil would not need verification.
He wished that if his reputation spread, fragrant and foul would cease together.
However, his intention was not something that his body could hinder,
his aspiration transcended the limits of fate.
What my eyes personally witnessed and saw in this person was:
His benevolent heart and bright intellect emerged in childhood.
He was born with inherent brilliance, his family wealthy.
Furthermore, he was skilled in horsemanship and understood music.
Those who frequented the beautiful scenes on main roads,
and played musical instruments in grand markets,
were not merely those who spent days, months, or years.
Indeed, he was like Zhào and Lǐ in Xián Yáng,
Chéng and Zhèng in Lín Qióng.
Afterwards, during a long night, he suddenly awakened,
and sighed during his drink, saying,
"Alas, joy and aversion come alternately, eventually leading to sorrow and suffering.
If one does not block their root, how can one transcend them?
Moreover, the three realms endlessly sink and all heavens swiftly pass.
How much more so with Qí Jǐng on Niú Shān and Suí Wǔ at Qǐ Yīn!
The seasons hurry, frost and dew press close.
Considering this wish, how can it last long?"
With a sigh, he resolved to abandon worldly splendor and benefit both himself and others.
His mother pitied his heart,
his sisters affirmed his resolve.
So they agreed,
that he would leave home to seek the Way, his own person having left, the entire family departed from the world.
Wife and children would forever be separated from joy, forever bid farewell.
Not only was there no pleasure before,
but in his prime, he definitively severed the eternal bonds of love. Now they were divorced.
His travel boat sailed south, casting its shadow upon Lú Yuè.
Once he ascended Shí Mén and Xiāng Lú Fēng,
he did not descend the peak for six years.
The monks could not endure his profound asceticism,
but the Dharma Master did not change his resolve.
His compassion for beings did not allow him to remain in seclusion.
When his fellow student fell ill,
he shook his staff and traveled thousands of miles to rescue him.
At that time, I was recovering from illness on Dōng Shān,
and admired him from afar.
How could I expect him to seek me, rather than being drawn by the mountains?
When the Dharma Master arrived, I, a humble person, was burdened with tasks.
The previous poem already briefly recorded this,
so I will not repeat it.
Later, he returned to the mountain and completed his discourse.
His sincere efforts were finally rewarded.
Connecting eaves on precipitous cliffs, all drawing from the winding stream.
Eating ganoderma and atractylodes together as medicine,
studying Dharma words from the same scroll.
We passed two more years of cold and heat.
It was not merely that Shān Yáng had no expression of joy or anger, or that the Magistrate had only one look of contentment.
Truly, he illuminated the subtle and profound, cleansed away near attachments.
Washing away superficial impurities, daily forgetting his ailments.
We hoped to live together until old age, but separation had no form.
Sincerity and faith found no return, what reason was there for gathering?
In his later years, he encountered misfortunes, and from afar, sought me out.
Upon arrival, he was hindered by obstacles, and communication was almost cut off.
He fell ill during the summer,
and passed away within ten days.
Truly, life and death are fated.
This journey indeed had its reasons.
Hearing of the tragedy, I felt profound pain,
which is a common human emotion. How much time on paper and ink?
It is not for seeking fame,
but out of admiration for his integrity and a deep remembrance of his life.
I could not keep silent,
so I poured out my feelings and took up my brush.
Its words are:
I look up to investigate form and consciousness.
I look down to explore principle and category.
I gather sounds to understand rhythm.
I pull up mallows to behold their clusters.
Things are distinguished by their spiritual uniqueness.
People are valued for their wisdom.
This is divine insight,
and what observation and discernment signify.
From early childhood,
a benevolent heart was keenly perceptive.
Breathing in and out the fragrance of flowers,
embracing the sun and moon.
Like a garden of orchids,
a breeze passes, and their fragrance wafts forth.
Like the celestial boundary,
clouds part, and light shines.
Seeking fame constrains the self,
regulating conduct binds oneself.
If one is ignorant of the world,
one has never even come close.
Life is made serene by intention;
intention governs life.
Who experiences this joy and comfort?
Chéng Zhèng, Zhào Lǐ.
Their homes possess gold and silk,
their talents are honed, their skills perfected.
They raise their heads and spend lavishly,
with many strings playing exquisite melodies.
Wine flows freely, tunes are quickened,
intentions are beautiful, clothes extravagant.
Morning presses upon dusk,
evening dreads the stars' movement.
Long are the white days,
chill are the good nights.
Years pass, joys flow away,
weariness comes, feelings are abandoned.
Bitterness and joy cycle,
eventually succeeding each other.
Discarded and then renewed,
life is swift, fame is borrowed.
Who can alter or take it away?
What art can shift it?
The subtle and the coarse are mingled and complete,
good and evil are disparate.
The mind itself has limits,
in principle, it cannot be regulated.
Let us examine the multitude of teachings,
perhaps gaining some insight.
Daoists stumble near the goal,
other schools fall short of the distant one.
Who consistently adopts a false name?
How can one deviate from righteousness?
Only by forgetting both
does the mind become good.
Grieving for beings lost in delusion,
envying those who are liberated.
Changing clothes in the capital,
shaking a staff on the peak of Lúshān.
Long bidding farewell to hopes of glory,
eternally resting in the secluded ridge.
Abandoning splendor to adopt simplicity,
forsaking complexity to embrace conciseness.
People suffer its difficulty,
the master takes its tranquility.
From the perspective of darkness, light
immediately turns foolishness into transcendence.
When wisdom holds affection,
in confronting principle, it is nirvāṇa.
Since avarice is not removed,
how can attachment be pulled out?
The master, in his compassion,
for your sake endured bitter discipline.
The discipline's bitterness was for himself,
its beneficial rectitude remained for others.
With light, he departed darkness;
with compassion, he endured transmigration.
To rescue others,
one must first save oneself.
Initially, his feelings conflicted,
but ultimately, his principle was right.
Liáng Hóng carried his wife,
and with a bamboo basket saw his son.
He welcomed guests with chicken and millet,
and conveyed his thoughts through song.
In the world, he was called noble;
in the Dao, truly rustic.
How much more so the Fǎshī,
uniquely transcending divine principles!
Physical life is easily exhausted,
promises are hard to judge.
Riding on the mind, one transforms;
abandoning the body, one does not lament.
Embracing the Dao, he became more resolute;
his fated life was already late.
Compassionate towards beings, he left the mountain,
finally resting in the traveler's lodge.
Alas, how sad!
His spirit followed him.
Yánlíng had already understood,
the kite and the ant are treated alike.
What the Qīyuán understood,
leaving one's skeleton in the empty wilderness,
how is it different or contrived?
Fortunately, there is something left over,
just enough to feed insects and birds.
Alas, how sad!
Remembering his life,
sharing seclusion and profundity.
We led each other in initiating things,
together ascended and overlooked.
Opening rocks to connect valleys,
clearing branches to thin forests.
Gazing far upon overlapping peaks,
looking near at rugged mountains.
With few affairs and a quiet place,
we sought the subtle and explored the abstruse.
What sentence was not analyzed?
What doubt was not resolved?
Scrolls unrolled and rolled up,
kept and taken out, paper folded.
Questions came and answers went,
making the day seem longer than the evening.
Jǔ Nì tilled together,
Yí Qí shared ferns.
Their traces were similar, their hearts joyful;
their deeds differed, their intentions contrary.
Bearing illness with burning pain,
hearing of his death with deep sorrow.
Who would say it doesn't hurt?
Tears stream down, moistening clothes.
Alas, how sad!
Time passes, seasons change;
borders shift, spirits transform.
Late autumn, mid-winter;
passing Guì to reach the sea.
Forever remembering that person,
thoughts deepen, feelings multiply.
Looking down, I feel ashamed before ordinary people;
looking up, I feel unworthy, having no one to rely on.
Alas, how sad!
The Dao maintains its unity,
therefore different eras shine with the same glory.
Virtue aligns with profound principle,
therefore different regions achieve the same goal.
Shì Gōng spread the profound dharma in Guānyòu,
Fǎshī inherited the flowing current in Jiāngzuǒ.
Hearing the wind, the four seas rejoiced and returned to the same path.
Thus, embracing benevolence, he lived as a recluse in the mountains and forests, seeking his aspiration.
Thereupon, many monks gathered like clouds, diligently cultivating pure practices.
Sharing the dharma, they "ate the wind" and lingered at the gate of the Dao.
It can be said that in the last age of the five hundred years, he looked up and honored the customs of Shèwèi,
and on the peak of Lúshān, he looked down and transmitted the sound of Língjiù.
How grand and never before heard!
In my years of devoted study, I hoped to be among the last of his disciples.
Alas, my sincere wish was not fulfilled,
I am forever parted from this world.
He lived to be eighty-four years old.
He passed away on the sixth day of the eighth month of autumn in the thirteenth year of Yìxī.
His years surpassed the stage of following his heart's desires;
his work accomplished, his body gone.
Having a beginning and an end, his light will shine for a thousand years.
Alas, how sad!
Now I compose this eulogy.
In times of old, Ān Gōng.
His Daoist virtues were truly widespread.
When the Great Dharma was nearing its end,
The faltering order was entrusted to him.
His body was serene, his movements ceased,
He embraced truth and rectified falsehood.
He served his teacher with filial piety,
And nurtured his disciples with righteousness.
Looking up, he propagated the Tathāgata's teachings,
Proclaiming the Dharma rain.
Looking down, he instructed the Dharma Masters,
Their solemn deportment truly exemplary.
He learned without peering through windows,
His discernment extended beyond his door.
Though fine grain was his sustenance,
He alone was like a *chángchǔ* (a humble plant).
Bright and spacious was his high hall,
Serene and quiet was his Dharma court.
Both solemn and tranquil,
The higher, the purer it became.
His words and intentions were composed,
His demeanor elegant and graceful.
He broadly extended compassion,
Benefiting all sentient beings.
How grand was his bearing,
How assiduous his nature.
When still a child, he tasted the Dao,
Leaving his parents to follow his teacher.
He made offerings to the Three Jewels,
Analyzing subtleties and resolving doubts.
His flourishing transformation was abundant,
His benevolent virtue was gentle and pleasant.
Here, one sought the Dao,
The four seas embraced his influence.
Those with heart galloped forth,
Bowing with reverence to his precepts and virtues.
His revered name continued to resonate,
Though the five defilements temporarily prevailed.
He propagated the Dao and sang its praises,
Penetrating the vast and the subtle.
Like the sixteen princes,
Children who were enlightened beforehand.
When Gōng became a monk,
His years had not yet reached the age of learning.
Like that Dènglín,
Moistened by sweet dew.
Like that Qióngyáo,
Both ground and carved.
The great congregation gathered,
The assembly convened like dragons.
They came to find a dwelling,
Where could a spiritual temple be established?
The old masters delved into subtle mechanisms,
The new students diligently practiced.
Gōng encouraged them,
Harmonizing and compiling.
He cultivated a relationship with Shí Gōng,
Whose esteemed reputation blended with his own.
He invited Chan practitioners,
Personally receiving the Samādhi.
All virtues merged into one stream,
Sustainable and great.
His august morality,
Transcended gain and loss.
When the six directions were in decline,
Mountains crumbled and seas dried up.
Sun and moon dimmed their light,
The three luminaries ceased to shine clearly.
All peaks broke their branches,
Continuous waves became congealed.
His grand transformation left a legacy,
His subtle influence never fading.
Alas, how mournful!
His life was of pure simplicity,
His death increased our sorrow and grief.
A lone cicada in an earthen tomb,
Appearing like a gathered skeleton.
Heaven and humanity felt withered,
Indra grieved in his heart.
His pervasive lingering influence,
His gentle remaining sadness.
Alas, the Dharma Master,
Has finally found his resting place.
The room has no lingering echoes,
The courtyard has a wide path.
Alas, how mournful!
Duānmù mourned Ní,
Grieving for six full years.
Looking up, he admired Zhūsì,
Looking down, he was wary of the *tíjuān*.
Now your disciples,
Truly share this difficulty.
In the morning, they sweep the empty room,
In the evening, they weep in the desolate mountains.
Alas, Dharma Master,
When will you return?
Wind whistles through bamboos and cypresses,
Clouds shroud the mountain peaks.
Valleys are like hills,
Forests change their appearance.
From of old, hearing of his reputation,
I desired to take refuge.
Mountains and rivers made the road distant,
My heart yearned, but my body could not go.
From beginning to end, I held regret,
My past karmic affinity being slight.
There is hope in Ānyǎng,
But none in Yánfú.
Alas, how mournful!
Waiting for things to engage, to utilize them to generate external paths to come from my embrace with joy.
Therefore, he concealed his treasure and kept his uncarved jade,
Guiding carriages to emerge from Wèi.
A *luán* escaping its cloudy thread,
How could it increase a chariot to enter Wèi?
Thus, a scholar who scorns the mundane values his solitary Dao,
A dweller in seclusion feels no vexation in his lofty solitude.
Each time I proclaimed the scriptures, they illuminated brightly in the past.
Therefore, I have already affixed my feelings in verse,
My body and mind are insufficient.
If such is the rhyme of solitary detachment, lofty already in youth,
The spirit of the absolute peak, early in ambition, can reach afar.
He first rested his carriage at Lúshān when his years were just past youth,
His boundless ambition already extended a thousand *lǐ*.
Then he sought to shave his head and enter the Dao, forgetting his home and joining the Dharma.
At that time, the Shāmen Shì Huìyuǎn,
Though extremely lofty,
Because he was still young, did not permit it.
Thereupon, he ascended Kǒng Jiànshǒu Tàiyáng Lín, a perilous place where he threw himself to the ground,
Exchanging his body for his ambition.
The Dharma Master then marveled and accepted him.
He soared with a noble lineage, his karma accumulating from his pure conduct.
Before the harsh dew became severe, he practiced asceticism with an early ambition.
Fellow students could not endure its hardship,
But this person did not change his principles.
At that time, the sūtra treasury was just arriving in the East,
His studies flourishing in the Central Plains.
So he journeyed thousands of *lǐ*,
Repeatedly traveling to Hán and Luò.
Discernment and wisdom enlightened each other, their utility diminishing daily.
After Luóshí died,
Yuǎn Gōng retreated from the world.
Then he returned to the secluded gate, living in a hidden valley,
His unwillingness to emerge, like those of Yéshān, has been for over twenty years now.
My uncle, suffering from illness, returned to seclusion,
His thoughts tranquil like the wind.
The Dharma Master, moved by inspiration, came to visit,
Accumulating evenings of conversation.
In the clear pavilion, the words concluded, parting without saying goodbye.
Thus, silent communication reached mutual understanding, and movement and stillness were truly complete.
The hermit Dài Yóng's refined temperament was clear and simple,
Their spiritual abodes together, their characters harmonizing.
So he leaned on the peaks to form a pavilion, paused by the woods to open a hall.
Here, beyond human society, he met friends through shared mind.
Xīhé's waves surged, Dōngshān had already crumbled.
When wind and clouds have passed, grass and trees remain in sorrow; my heart is grieved,
Tears flow incessantly.
Alas, how mournful!
