Securely abiding in the unmoving realm and nation. Prostrate and reverently bow to the Eternally Abiding Three Jewels (Cháng Zhù Sān Bǎo).
Disciple of the Bodhisattva Precepts (Pú Sà Jiè Dì Zǐ) prostrates and bows in reverence to the Three Jewels (Sān Bǎo).
I humbly submit that the Buddha-lands (fó chà tǔ) are ineffable.
The titles of the Tathāgatas (Rú Lái) are boundless.
Some are past, some are present,
sharing the surname "Pó Luó" (Pāla).
Some existing simultaneously in different eras,
all bearing the name "Shì Jiā" (Śākya).
Some are ten billion enlightened kings (míng wáng).
Some are thirty thousand Dīpaṅkara Buddhas (Rán Dēng).
Coming and going through the three realms (sān jiè), pervading the ten directions.
Those who hear their names depart from defilements.
Those who uphold them attain the Way.
Their merits are difficult to ponder or conceive.
Śākyamuni Tathāgata (Shì Jiā Rú Lái), with unhindered power, traveled the pure path of Sāla (Suō Luó).
And rested on the auspicious blessed land.
From the jeweled pond, transformed beings spontaneously emerged.
Expounding the *Dà Tōng Fāng Guǎng* (Great Universal Extensive Sūtra).
Bringing forth the names of the Three Jewels (Sān Bǎo).
Just like the Six Heavens (liù tiān) all returning to the One Vehicle (yī chéng).
Your disciple, with a heart of compassion,
cultivates the karma of equality.
Always taking responsibility for the sins of all nations upon myself.
The unrest of the four types of birth (sì shēng) is truly a heavy responsibility.
Therefore, I diligently cultivate myself from dawn to dusk, forgetting toil.
With diligence in my heart, I do not rest even in the dead of night.
I vow to uphold all practices of Bodhisattvas (Pú Sà).
May all Dharma gates (fǎ mén) of the Buddhas be as expounded.
Wishing for all under heaven
to be free from the dust of fear.
May crawling and flying creatures
forever find a place of refuge.
Now, solemnly following the Sūtra teachings, in a certain place, establishing a certain number of monks for a certain number of days, performing the *Fāng Guǎng Chàn Huǐ* (Extensive Repentance).
Reciting it a hundred times, circumambulating clockwise seven times.
Applying incense paste and powdered incense,
exhausting all aspects of adornment.
With right mindfulness (zhèng niàn) and right contemplation (zhèng guān),
pouring out a heart of utmost sincerity.

Before the assembled multitude, I reverently prostrate with utmost sincerity to the fundamental teacher, Śākyamuni Tathāgata (Shì Jiā Rú Lái), and pay homage to the names of the Three Jewels (Sān Bǎo) mentioned in the *Fāng Guǎng Jīng* (Extensive Sūtra).
May all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas (Pú Sà) respond to my call.
Emit pure bright light to illuminate all darkness and defilement.
Bestow cool water to extinguish this thirst of craving.
Board the boat of the six perfections (liù dù) and enter the ocean of samādhi (sān mèi).
Uniting all existence and realizing Suchness (zhēn rú).
Equaling the three realms (sān jiè) and ascending to the true Dharma.
Prostrate and reverently bow to the Eternally Abiding Three Jewels (Cháng Zhù Sān Bǎo).
I humbly submit that
Bodhisattvas (Pú Sà) for sentient beings
are a great reliance.
Observing the nature and characteristics, they save and liberate according to capacity; if even one person is not yet delivered, they will not attain the fruit of the Way.
From past to present, their vows and actions are consistent.
And Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva (Xū Kōng Zàng Pú Sà) is most supreme.
He is the banner king among the multitude.
He is the venerable lord of great illumination.
Possessing the wisdom of all Buddhas.
Attaining the secrets of the Tathāgata (Rú Lái).
Even in dreams, his form can be seen, manifesting appearances according to circumstances.
Upon hearing his title,
water and fire cannot burn or drown.
With a single mind invoking his name,
swords and staffs cannot harm.
Wishes for longevity and wealth
will surely be fulfilled when thought of.
Needs for forms, sounds, tastes, and touches
will all be granted when sought.
Physical and mental afflictions are treated with compassion.
Fears of prisons are resolved with skillful means.
This is following worldly Dharma to bring peace and joy to sentient beings.
And when his divine form changes, going to the realm of fragrance accumulation,
he emits pure bright light, coming to Jambudvīpa (Yán Fú zhī Jiè).
Entering samādhi (sān mèi) concentration to remove the heat of afflictions.
Expounding Dhāraṇī (tuó luó ní) to break through evil karmic obstacles.
The evil world of the five defilements (wǔ zhuó) becomes cool and refreshing at once.
The five cardinal sins (wǔ gēn běn zuì) are all liberated.
This is the eye of the world,
showing the path to Nirvāṇa (Niè Pán).
Your disciple receives the teachings of the Tathāgata (Rú Lái).
Inherits the compassionate land of all Buddhas.
Adorned with the merits of Bodhisattvas (Pú Sà).
And performs the deeds of a Great Being (dà shì).
I now vow that all Buddha-lands (chà tǔ) in the ten directions will have the One Vehicle (yī chéng).
May sentient beings in the ten directions all cultivate the ten stages (shí dì).
Now, solemnly in a certain place, establishing a certain number of monks for a certain number of days for the *Xū Kōng Zàng Pú Sà Chàn* (Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva Repentance).
Before the assembled multitude, I reverently prostrate with utmost sincerity to the fundamental teacher, Śākyamuni Buddha (Shì Jiā Wén Fó).
I prostrate to Tathāgata Vimalapuṣpālayagarbha (Shèng Huā Fū Zàng Rú Lái).
I prostrate to the divine Dhāraṇī (tuó luó ní) mantras.
I prostrate to Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva (Xū Kōng Zàng Pú Sà).
May Ākāśagarbha Bodhisattva (Xū Kōng Zàng Pú Sà)
respond immediately to our call.
Manifest divine powers and open the light of wisdom.
Travel to all lands in various forms.
Deliver and liberate sentient beings, not deviating from his vows.
Prostrate and reverently bow to the Eternally Abiding Three Jewels (Cháng Zhù Sān Bǎo).
I humbly consider that
the Buddhas of the three worlds, by the power of their vows,
and the Tathāgatas of the ten directions, by their wisdom and skillful means,
unfold unimpeded eloquence
and open endless doors.
The streams of Dharma diverge, their sources infinite.
The roots of Dharma scatter, their branches boundless.
It is not only the Mahāprajñā that has eighty-four thousand [teachings];
even the Dhāraṇī-gates number ninety-two billion.
Everywhere, they preach with various names,
their merits immeasurable, their divine power unfathomable.
Just as Vasu rescued from hell,
Pāpīyas (Pāpīyan) awakened Bodhi,
Huājù attained supernatural powers,
and Léiyīn escaped concealment—
none of them did so without relying on these chapters and verses, and without receiving this karmic power.
There are also disciples of the four divisions and sentient beings of the ten directions,
who, hearing a single phrase, arouse the Bodhi-mind;
listening to a single discourse, awaken to the Way.
Thus, it is known that all Dharmas are nothing but true wonders.
Your disciple earnestly cultivates the practice.
What he learns is Bodhi.
Eating late and rising early,
what he practices is salvation.
With the power of one mind, he gathers sentient beings.
In the space of a single thought, he pervades all Dharma-forms.
He wishes to uphold all the comprehensive wisdom of the Tathāgata,
and desires to disseminate all the merits of the Buddhas.
Now, diligently following the scriptures of the Dharma canon,
I, before the great assembly, sincerely bow to Shìjiāmóuní Fó.
I bow to the chapters and verses of Dhāraṇī.
I bow to Bhikṣu Léiyīn.
I bow to Bodhisattva Huājù.
May I, by this merit, tame sentient beings,
extinguish the three poisons of the mind, and break the ten evil karmas.
May the four hundred vexations naturally become pure,
and the eighty-four thousand dust-like defilements be liberated at once.
May I obtain the power of divine incantations,
and possess the goodness of the Dharma seal.
May I enter the Dhāraṇī-gate,
and contemplate the realms of all Buddhas.
May the fires of hell be extinguished forever, without remainder.
I prostrate and respectfully bow to the eternally abiding Three Jewels.
I humbly consider that
all formations are impermanent, all are defiling Dharmas.
All phenomena in inversion become the root of suffering.
Like burning flames and mirror images,
we perceive the ceaseless flux of change.
Like floating grass and burning spears,
we witness the swiftness of arising and ceasing.
Following the winds of karma, we enter the sea of suffering;
pursued by karmic obstructions, we hasten to dark paths.
Coming and going in the three realms,
we have not found a place of rest.
Revolving in the five paths of transmigration, there is no end to the cycle, not even for a moment.
Yàoshī Rúlái has great vows,
to guide all beings and protect sentient creatures.
He directs the hundred rivers of existence
to return to the one taste of the Dharma stream.
He is also able to bestow flower gardens and follow worldly customs,
so that they may attain peace and be without fear.
As for
the eight difficulties, nine calamities, five defilements, and three disasters;
flood, fire, thieves, epidemics, and famine;
enemies, creditors, royal laws, and local officials—
the forces of oppression are manifold, the methods of destruction are countless.
He can transform calamity into fortune, and change danger into safety.
Furthermore, for those who seek wealth and nobility, official positions, prolonged life, and many children—
the great desires of the people,
the urgent necessities of the world—
none are not satisfied naturally, in accordance with their minds and thoughts.
Thus, it is known that the skillful means of the Buddhas are beyond calculation.
Your disciple, though overseeing affairs, lacks proper methods, and his achievements are not yet numerous.
He relies on Yàoshī’s original vow to perfect sentient beings.
Now, diligently following the scriptures, at a certain place, he holds a Yàoshī fast and repentance for a certain number of monks for a certain number of days.
May the great assembly present here sincerely bow to our original teacher Shìjiā Rúlái.
Bow to Yàoshī Rúlái.
His compassion broadly covers all, not straying from his original vow, not abandoning the world.
He raises the clouds of the four immeasurables and showers the rain of the six perfections,
extinguishing the fire of birth and death, removing the arrows of vexation.
The worlds of the ten directions
are illuminated as by revolving lamps.
The seven hundred ghost-spirits
seek out strands of thread and respond to the call.
Obstructions vanish as incense burns, calamities no longer exist.
Life is extended by banners, gradually ascending to the eternal abode.
May we wander in the profound Dharma-nature,
and enter peerless perfect enlightenment.
May our vows and practices be perfected like Yàoshī Rúlái.
Upon reflection, true liberation is fundamentally unarisen.
True wisdom is also without extinction in the present.
Thus, it is known that the changing colors of the Crane Grove
are not a text of impermanence.
The Vulture Peak's eternal presence
is truly a Dharma of permanence.
However, worlds are not uniform,
hence the responses are inexhaustible.
Sentient beings are boundless,
hence skillful means are limitless.
In accordance with thoughts and attachments, various Dharma-gates appear.
Due to karma and mind, each manifests differently.
Sometimes, the form of sitting in meditation for eighty small kalpas remains unchanged;
in a period of eight thousand years, the time of extinction has already arrived.
By the Hīraṇyavatī River,
the morning light suddenly brightens.
Among the Sala trees,
the sound of midnight suddenly stills.
The final merit is on this very day.
Your disciple, having karmic connections in Jambudvīpa, bears a heavy responsibility.
He pities the delusion of sentient beings,
and laments the ignorance and confusion of all creatures.
He constantly wishes to build the boat of the six perfections,
to ferry them to the other shore.
He drives the vehicle of the One Vehicle,
to guide them to the Middle Way.
Now, diligently, in the Tàijí Diàn, he establishes an unimpeded grand assembly, a Sāluó grand fast for a hundred monks for one night.
May the rain of Dharma and clouds of Dharma
cool the fires of the three realms.
May the lamps of wisdom and torches of wisdom
illuminate the chambers of a hundred years.
May the two characters "eternal abiding" be heard by humans and gods alike.
May the three dots of the "ī" character be understood by both ordinary beings and sages.
There is no need for Kasyapa's question,
nor for Subhadra's doubt.
All-encompassing wisdom serves as the root,
immeasurable merits adorn oneself.
The mind-tree blossoms with flowers of liberation,
the body-field contains the water of samādhi and wisdom.
Residing in an auspicious place,
reclining on a field of blessings.
Ever pure, along with the two forces (Yin and Yang);
receiving blessings through the four seasons.
The sun and moon lords
shine like a perfect pair across the great chiliocosm.
The star-palaces
scatter like a string of pearls across billions of worlds.
The light rain of compassion
flies together with auspicious winds.
The precious clouds of Bodhi
come together with flying mist.
The six directions and four seas are no longer troubled by defilements.
The six paths and four kinds of birth are all imbued with purity.
I humbly observe that
in profound ancient pronouncements,
kings declare words of "the responsibility being mine."
In canonical rites and exemplary codes,
sages express their self-reproach.
Therefore, sacrificing oneself to benefit others
is the constant heart of the benevolent.
Overcoming oneself to benefit people
is the constant virtue of the noble person.
Furthermore, for Bodhisattvas and Mahāsattvas, their fundamental practice
is to respond to the three realms and embrace the four kinds of birth.
They manifest the immeasurable four immeasurable minds,
and cultivate the equal six perfections.
Though cities, wives, and children suffer greatly and are in distress,
carrying on the great enterprise of ancestors,
struggling and gasping for breath,
bearing the heavy responsibility of all under heaven.
When the common people are not well governed, and achievements are not flourishing,
he "treads on rotten wood and walks on thin ice," never forgetting vigilance and diligence.
Moreover, seeing worldly phenomena as bubbles and shadows, as temporary as dew and lightning,
the river of craving rushes, the sea of desire surges.
Beings with consciousness are consumed together, all living beings drown together.
Wearing jade pendants and relying on precious stones,
one still realizes that the ten thousand chariots are not venerable.
Sitting on the throne, facing the screen,
one instead finds the myriad affairs to be a burden.
Vigilant every night as if in peril, thinking of widely leading and guiding, never ceasing each morning.
Respectfully, for the holy spirits of the seven ancestral temples;
respectfully, for the holy person of the Empress Dowager;

respectfully, for the devas, nāgas, ghosts, and spirits, the hidden and the manifest, the empty and the existent, the three realms, four kinds of birth, five paths, six destinies; whether with form or with thought, whether enemies or relatives, or neither enemies nor relatives—pervading empty space, filling the Dharma-realm, exhaustively past, completely future, immeasurable names and consciousnesses, all kinds of beings, with equal great generosity.
He gives away your disciple's own person, as well as his imperial carriage and ceremonial robes,
the five grades of ceremonial robes, his imperial chariot, the six crowns, and dragon insignia,
his jade table, black fur robes, golden wheels, and dark blue horses,
his pearl necklaces, precious ornaments, and splendid embellishments.
Whatever he uses or relies upon,
whatever he enjoyed in his life—
all are given as offerings to the Three Jewels.
Now, diligently, in the front hall, an unimpeded grand assembly is established,
to fulfill the vows made,
and all merits are enumerated before you.
May all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, the hidden and manifest in space, all arrive to bear witness.
May they open the sun of wisdom and reflect the clouds of compassion,
erect precious banners in the great chiliocosm,
and strike Dharma drums in billions of worlds.
May they shake the world and awaken all sentient beings,
emit the pure light of samādhi,
and pour forth the one-flavored rain of Dharma.
May they lead the ignorant out of the pit of fire,
and pull the afflicted out of the thorny forest.
May they exit the river of transmigration and reach the shore of non-arising.

Edict of Táng Tàizōng for setting up a fast and performing rites for those who died in battle. Edict of Táng Tàizōng for ordaining monks throughout the empire. Imperial order of Táng Tàizōng prohibiting the sale of Buddha images. Letter to Vinaya Master Xiān and others. Edict of Táng Tàizōng converting his old residence into a temple. Memorial by Táng Tàizōng for accumulating merits for Empress Mù. Inscription on the bell of the two teachings by Zhōu Wǔdì. Inscription on the bell of Dàxīngshàn Temple by Táng Tàizōng. Inscription on the bell of Xīmíng Temple by Crown Prince Táng Dōnggōng.
The **Guǎng Hóngmíng Jí** (Expanded Collection of Propagating and Illuminating).
This refers to its vast propagation and protection of the Dharma, enlightening those with understanding.
From the previous nine chapters, which revealed the rational paths of deliberation as appropriate to their times,
their connections were quite thorough.
However, the full extent of the aspirations was
not yet thoroughly examined.
If not displayed and praised, to whom would the songs be dedicated?
Therefore, this section is compiled for the lessons it offers far and wide.
Moreover, when the Dharma King ruled the land, songs of praise were sung from the beginning.
Brahmā kings, heavenly lords, Śrāvakas, and Bodhisattvas
all offered verses of praise to express their profound sincerity.
There is no scripture that does not manifest this to sight and hearing.
In the Eastern lands, kings and officials were not confused by this path, attempting to emulate it.
The imperial nation's beauty was universally extolled.
Thus, the expression and emotions, all falling into a general disarray,
reside here.
However, since the **Jìn** and **Sòng** dynasties,
several hundred collections by various authors
showed great reverence for the Buddhist gate, all presenting their brief statements.
Yet, when trying to gather them, hardly one in a hundred remained.
Let me list a few items to add to the broad observation.
I have always loved mountains and waters, with a heart for hills and valleys.
My body, bound by worldly nets, could not fulfill its aspirations.
My solitary actions were thwarted, and my desire for freedom was thwarted.
Because of this, I was appointed to office to serve the king.
The times were full of troubles, and the world's path was difficult.
I was involved in military affairs, with scarcely a year of peace.
The government above was dark and tyrannical, and the villains below caused chaos.
The way of the gentlemen diminished, and the way of the small-minded people prospered.
Those who wielded power and responded to imperial edicts included **Méi Chóng'ér** and **Rú** (or **Rú Shòu**).
**Fǎzhēn**, **Yú Língyùn**, and **Fēng Yǒngzhī**.
And many others like these.
These are what **Zhì Gōng** called the "chaotically crowned."
**Zhì Gōng** was the Bhikkhu **Bǎo Zhì**.
His attire was inconsistent, and his manifestations were boundless.
At that time, the multitude of small-minded people suspected his divine strangeness.
So they confined him to the outer chamber of **Huálín**.
**Gōng** also angrily said:
"Chaotically crowned! Chaotically crowned!
Each seizes the axis of power, issuing commands.
Their authority and blessings are self-determined, life and death are at their word.
Loyal and good people suffer slaughter and execution.
Meritorious officials receive undeserved punishments.
Their garments are similar, but they are divided and driven separately.
All claim to be the emperor, calling themselves supreme.
They use their trickery to confuse the minds of the people.
They come and go, reveling, unmindful of dawn or dusk.
They clear out the capital, without rest day or night.
Those on their deathbed run out of breath by the roadside.
Sons do not have time to mourn.
Those about to give birth deliver by the roadside.
Mothers do not get to hold their babies.
The common people trembled as if their horns were breaking off.
**Chángshā Xuānwǔ Wáng**
had rendered great service to the nation.
The rewards of rites were unfulfilled, and cruel harm suddenly befell him.
Even his younger brothers and nephews suffered the same misfortune.
Then **Huán Shén** and **Dù Bófú**, along with six or seven light envoys, were dispatched
to **Yōngzhōu**.
They sought to conspire with the various military advisors to harm him.
But the hearts of the people were not with them, so the plan failed.
Later, **Liú Shānyáng** was dispatched.
He openly sought out brave warriors like **Chūhǔ**.
Their weaponry was sharp and formidable.
There was no defense from rulers or relatives.
They simply wished to bind themselves and await execution.
Such tyranny originated from the small-minded people.
They feared being submerged and drowned without pity.
How much more so the treacherous villains!
If one were to silently accept death,
one would be laughed at by the world.
Soon after, **Shānyáng** reached **Jīngzhōu**,
where he was captured by **Xiāo Yǐngwèi**.
Immediately, a post horse was dispatched to **Yōngzhōu**.
Then a great roar was heard.
Banners were erected, and flags were raised.
The four directions were of one mind,
responding like an echo.
In the first month of the second year of **Qí Yǒngyuán** (500 CE),
they set out from **Xiāngyáng**.
The righteous and brave were like clouds, and their ships covered the sky.
**Jìnglíng** Grand Administrator **Cáo Zōng**, cavalry commander **Yīn Chāng**, and others,
each led cavalry and infantry to welcome them along both banks.
The waves flowed against the current for forty **lǐ**.
They stopped when they reached the boat I was riding.
A pair of white fish leaped into the front of the boat.
This omen was like the **Mèngjīn** incident, a divine response.
Clouds moved, the sky changed, thunder rumbled, and winds raced.
**Yǐngchéng** was captured, and **Jiāngzhōu** surrendered.
The armored forces of **Gūshú** retreated at the mere rumor.
Layman **Lǐ** of **Xīntíng** bowed and submitted.
With the tyrant eliminated, the common people revived.
I then wished to return to gardens and forests, to live freely in the wilderness.
But constrained by the people's will below and fearing Heaven's mandate above,
I had no choice but to assume the great throne.
It was like standing on the edge of a deep abyss, treading on thin ice.
I still wished to avoid the position and await a capable person.
But if I had yielded, the situation would have collapsed again.
Not only would my body have died and my name been disgraced,
but I would also have burdened the seen and unseen realms.
So I composed a poem that said:
"Day and night I constantly ponder,
the cycle has reached its end.
In the end, one may find release,
but release will surely not last."
Facing the court, with the imperial crown for all four seas,
I diligently worked from dawn to dusk, vigilant as if in danger.
To drive six horses with a rotten rope
cannot compare to this.
Worldly commentators compare me to **Tāng** and **Wǔ**.
However, I cannot be compared to **Tāng** and **Wǔ**.
Nor can **Tāng** and **Wǔ** be compared to me.
**Tāng** and **Wǔ** were sages.
I am a common person.
Thus, I cannot be compared to **Tāng** and **Wǔ**.
But the loyalty between **Tāng** and **Wǔ** and their rulers had not been severed
when the incident of the white flag at **Náncháo** occurred.
The loyalty between my ruler and me had already been severed.
Only then did I pacify the tyrant and remove the suffering from the world.
Because of these two paths, we cannot be compared.
When I was a commoner,
I only knew rites and righteousness, not faith and devotion.
I cooked and butchered living beings to entertain guests.
I ate meat according to what was available, not knowing the taste of vegetables.
But when I became emperor, possessing the entire realm,
exotic delicacies from distant lands were continuously offered as tribute.
All kinds of rare foods from within the four seas invariably arrived.
My table was full, and a hundred flavors filled the platters.
It was then that I stopped eating, put down my chopsticks, and wept before the table.
I regretted not being able to provide daily offerings to my parents during their lives.
How could I alone enjoy such fine meals?
Because of this, I became a vegetarian, no longer eating fish or meat.
Although this was my internal practice, I did not let it be known externally.
When hosting banquets for my officials,
the dishes were served as usual.
Not being accustomed to vegetarian food, my body became excessively thin and yellow.
Gradually, some in the court began to notice.
**Xiè Fěi**, **Kǒng Yàn'yǐng**, and others
repeatedly urged me to resume eating meat.
Their loyalty was utmost.
But they did not understand my heart.
I also reflected:
possessing the world was never my original ambition.
**Dù Shù** said:
"To cut out one's heart and throw it on the ground, it is but a few pieces of meat."
What I rely on is clarity and understanding.
A gentleman clarifies his original intention.
Who knows that I do not covet the world?
I must only do what others cannot do,
so that the world may understand my heart.
I also ceased cohabiting with women,
not staying in the same room as my concubines and attendants.
This has been for over forty years.
At that time, my body felt slightly unwell.
I asked the imperial physicians **Liú Chéngzhī** and **Yáo Pútí** about my condition.
**Liú Chéngzhī** said,
"**Chéngzhī** knows this is caused by excessive eating and drinking."
I replied to **Liú Chéngzhī**,
"I was a commoner, indulging in rich foods freely."
**Liú Chéngzhī** said,
"How can what Your Majesty ate in the past
compare to what you eat today?"
**Yáo Pútí** smiled and shook his head, saying,
"Only **Pútí** knows.
Your Majesty's excessive sexual activity
is the cause."
At that time, I had long stopped eating fish and meat,
and also ceased sexual activity.
Since their wisdom was not like **Hé** and **Huǎn** (famous physicians),
and their skill was not like **Biǎn** and **Huà** (also famous physicians),
I remained silent,
not questioning them further.
I still allowed them to treat me.
**Liú Chéngzhī** prescribed wine,
and **Yáo Pútí** prescribed pills.
After taking them, my illness worsened.
Because they knew nothing,
I stopped taking their medicine.
Since then, when ill, I always prescribed for myself,
not taking medicine.
This has also been for over forty years.
I was not inherently diligent.
But since I stopped eating living beings,
there was no more killing.
Since the obstacles were not driven by internal desires,
there were no more obstacles of desire and aversion.
With these two obstacles removed, my consciousness gradually became clear.
I could then understand both internal and external scriptures upon reading them.
From then on, I began to truly understand the path.
The **Lǐ Jì** (Book of Rites) says:
"Human beings are born tranquil; this is the nature of Heaven.
They are moved by external things; this is the desire of nature."
With movement, the mind is defiled.
With stillness, the mind is pure.
When external movements ceased, the inner mind also became clear.
I began to truly awaken,
realizing that suffering and burdens have no origin.
Thus, I composed the **Jìngyè Fù** (Ode on Pure Karma).
Observing the innate nature of human life,
embracing subtle qi and being pure and tranquil.
Moved by external things, desires are stirred;
the mind clings and thus misfortunes arise.
Faults constantly arise from external dust,
and burdens must result from previous circumstances.
Like an empty valley responding to sound,
it resembles a wandering form having a shadow.
Harboring greedy thoughts without satiety,
indulging inner intentions to run wild.
The eyes change with colors,
the gaze shifts with appearances.
Observing the mysterious yellow of the five colors, playing with the dazzling splendor of the seven treasures.
Clinging to the charming beauty of slender forms,
indulging in the captivating allure of graceful figures.
They remain in one's waking and sleeping, never forsaken,
and day and night, fatigue is forgotten.
Like a flourishing plum tree being plucked,
like a swift horse wearing a bridle.
Resembling the bright sun illuminating the sky,
thus for years it does not wane.
Observing the ear-consciousness's love for sound,
it is also like birds returning to the forest.
Already lingering over strings and flutes,
also bustling with the five notes.
Through dusk and dawn, it does not cease,
through the four seasons, they seek each other.
Sometimes disturbing emotions and confusing thoughts,
also blocking the ears and stopping the heart.
As for fragrant scents that arise, touching the nose and activating consciousness,
they linger and follow, indistinct and endless.
Orchids and musk fly together like two wings of a bird,
like drinking poison when thirsty, like wearing thorns when cold.
The tongue discerns flavors, and among all dusts, none exist,
great bitterness, saltiness, sourness – none are unpalatable.
Devouring living beings, oppressing flying and walking creatures,
only saying it is not enough, drinking wine through the long night.
Rebelling against clear actions, heedless of hidden faults.
The body receives touch to find peace and comfort.
Beautiful eyes, clear and bright, charming smiles, elegant eyebrows.
Slender waist, delicate hands, fragile bones, plump flesh.
The body attached to fragrance and purity, touching the body like grease.
A mad mind deluded, self-deceiving with inverted thoughts.
As for consciousness clinging,
endless chaotic thoughts, no good thoughts are cherished,
all give rise to evil snares.
Thus, the six dusts together obstruct the good path,
like purple overwhelming crimson, like wind flattening grass.
Embracing delusion and being born, growing old with it,
following ignorance, all are afflictions.
Reincarnating in the burning house, sinking in the sea of suffering,
clinging stubbornly through the long night, ultimately unable to change.
Distress and stagnation follow each other, calamities and anomalies arise in turn.
Internally harboring perverse beliefs, externally indulging in licentious sacrifices.
Falsely exhausting fate, unjustly dying a violent death.
Falsely creating divine blessings to invite fortune.
The front wheel breaks its axle, the rear cart overturns its track.
Bringing calamity to the state, disaster to the family, destroying oneself and ending one's lineage.
At first, one does not inwardly examine, blame oneself, and reflect.
Heaven has no favorites, it only assists the good.
Externally purify the eye's realm, internally cleanse the mind's dust.
Do not contaminate, do not grasp, do not love, do not anger.
Like jade having luster, like bamboo having skin.
Like a lotus in a pond,
like fragrant orchids blooming in spring.
Mud cannot defile its body,
deep darkness cannot cover its truth.
Mist and dew gather, and pearls flow,
bright wind stirs, and fragrance arises.
Doing much good accumulates years,
bright actions renew the day.
Always accompanying virtue,
constantly neighboring the Way.
Seeing the beloved fruit of pure karma,
with non-killing as the cause.
Departing from desires and evil, cultivating oneself,
thus there is no obstruction to the spirit.
Troubles and burdens are removed, obstacles are also purified.
Like long-clarified water, like a newly polished mirror.
Externally illuminating many forms, internally seeing various ailments.
Having removed external dust, returning to one's true nature.
The three evil paths are forever estranged, the eight difficulties are eternally extinguished.
The highest good is cultivated, good without blemish.
The single path of purity has no different tracks.
Only a wise person can unveil their heart.
Like a stone thrown into water, nothing contradicts the heart.
The heart is pure and cool like ice,
the will is bright and clear like snow.
Entanglements and burdens are already removed,
worries and fears are also extinguished.
Long separated from attachment and love,
forever parted from birth and death.
Beholding the outstanding talents of today,
imagining the brilliant youths of the future.
Harboring the 荊Jīng jade yet uncarved,
possessing divine artifacts within oneself.
Cultivating sacred practices ceaselessly,
trusting in the endless accumulation of good.
For eternal eons, their good name will be praised,
for ten thousand generations, their pure fame will flow.
How can one submit to power and claim bravery?
It is the triumph of the Way that makes one a hero.
Thoughts arise from emotions, emotions arise from thoughts.
Things respond to each other, so it is thus.
Every time I read biographies of filial sons,
I never fail to finish the scroll, stop reading, feel sorrow and regret, clutch my heart, and choke with sobs.
Before the age of pigtails,
I internally lost my support.
With my remaining breath, I struggled with my aged grandmother to raise each other.
When my teeth had passed the age of capping,
I externally lost my protector.
My official duties limited me to 荊Jīng Mán, causing me to miss morning and evening attendance.
The journey along the river was distant, and there was no news from home.
It seemed as if I was on the road.
My late father's body was unwell.
During the day I would stop eating, at night I would forgo sleep.
My heart was in turmoil, nowhere to find rest.
So I resigned from office to follow the road home.
At that time, 齊Qí 隨郡Suí Jùn Prince 子隆Zǐlóng,
鎮Zhèn Fǔ 陝西Shǎnxī, repeatedly sent urgent messages,
ordering me to stay one night.
The next morning, I should depart early to the riverbank for a farewell.
My mind was too anxious, I could not comply with the order.
I only managed to get a small boat and set off by starlight.
At night, I braved wind and waves, with no time to rest.
On the way, at 定陵Dìnglíng, the boat was again damaged.
At that time, the guest 周仲連Zhōu Zhònglián,
who was the commander of 鵲頭戌Quètóuxū,
lent a boat, and I traveled day and night.
I repeatedly encountered dangers and barely managed to cross.
By the time I arrived, it was already too late to catch him.
My inner organs were torn apart, my liver and heart shattered.
I immediately wished to retreat to the mountainside and dedicate my life to the tomb.
My elder brother took pity on me and did not allow me to go alone.
Subsequently, the cunning barbarians of the north gate raided the border.
The imperial court, remembering my late father's benevolence towards the people,
all remembered his former subordinates, of whom there were still several thousand.
武慶宗Wǔ Qìngzōng led them to stay and defend.
At that time, there was an imperial decree from that garrison,
ordering to defend 壽春Shòuchūn, and as it was a matter of royal service, there was no room to refuse.
The provincial governor 崔慧景Cuī Huìjǐng,
whose intentions were volatile,
far and wide summoned fugitives and gathered many ruffians and heroes.
Great villains and fierce scoundrels all gathered like clouds.
Such as 彭盆Péng Pén, 韓元孫Hán Yuánsūn, and others,
too numerous to count.
They doubled their march, rushing like lightning, reaching the 淮Huái and 淝Féi rivers unexpectedly.
The fierce thugs were surprised and frightened, scattering and dispersing.
The imperial army commanders 徐玄慶Xú Xuánqìng, 房伯玉Fáng Bóyù, and others,
wishing to attack and capture 慧景Huìjǐng,
instead firmly confined him.
Only then did the situation subside.
That year, when 齊明Qímíng acted as prime minister, the deliberations were undecided.
A secret memorial was dispatched, urging to summon 慧景Huìjǐng.
It was believed that a simple summons would not be refused.
Immediately, he was heavily dispatched back to reassure his heart.
Once the villainous leader departed, there was no worry along the 㳂Yín border.
Within ten days to a month, 慧景Huìjǐng returned to the garrison.
Then he immediately removed his armor and returned to the capital.
After that, I was constantly on the move, unable to rest.
Repeatedly encountering times of great upheaval, when the moment was like thunder and lightning.
Bringing order out of chaos and restoring government, thus embracing the four seas.
Recalling 子路Zǐlù's meeting with 孔丘Kǒngqiū, who said:
"When 由Yóu served his two parents,
he often ate coarse vegetables.
He carried rice for his parents a hundred li away.
After his parents passed away,
he traveled south to 楚Chǔ.
He was followed by a hundred chariots and accumulated ten thousand *zhong* of grain.
He sat on layers of cushions and ate from rows of tripods.
I wish I could eat coarse vegetables and carry rice for my parents
but it is no longer possible."
Every time I am moved by these words,
though alive, it is as if I am dead.
How can the kindness of parents be repaid?
Their compassion is like rivers and seas, filial piety is like a drop of dust.
Today, being the ruler of the world, yet unable to provide for them.
It is like having seven treasures in a famine year:
one cannot eat when hungry, one cannot wear them when cold.
Longing and crying, how can this sorrow be resolved?
So I built the 大愛敬寺Dà Àijìng Sì at the foot of 鍾山Zhōngshān,
and established the 大智度寺Dà Zhìdù Sì by the side of 青溪Qīngxī,
to express my boundless feelings,
and convey my mind of remembering the distant past.
Unable to forget the sorrow of 蓼莪Liǎo'é,
I again built the 至敬殿Zhìjìng Diàn within the palace.
Exhausting the skills of artisans,
using all the wonders of the secular world.
Water and rocks flowed around, fragrant trees were dense.
Limited by state affairs,
I was again unable to attend to them morning and evening.
Only on the first and fifteenth of the month could I personally offer food and libations.
Although I could offer delicacies, I had no one to look up to.
My inner heart collapsed, as if burned, as if scorched.
My feelings were intense within, expressed in words.
Thus, I composed the "賦Fù of Filial Thought."
I feel the changes and transformations of the four seasons.
I see the evolution and completion of all things.
Receiving the harmony of Heaven, our destinies differ.
Endowed with the virtue of Earth, we all flourish.
I observe the mayfly on a mosquito's eyebrow.
I behold the Kūn-Péng in the Northern Míng.
All possess consciousness, yet their perceptions differ.
All have forms, yet their shapes are distinct.
Though the myriad creatures are numerous,
only humans are the most spiritual.
Propriety and righteousness distinguish us from birds and beasts.
Speech differs us from parrots and orangutans.
I recall the swiftness of time, like a fish darting through a crevice.
I grieve that the flowing river never stops.
Treading on frost and dew, I feel sorrowful.
Remembering the grain burnt for sacrifice, tears fall.
Though I cover this grief, it does not depart.
Nor is there a day I do not dwell on it.
Zhòng Yóu remembered the dried fish and yearned eternally.
Qiū Wú was moved by the wind-swept trees and grieved long.
Though one might offer one's life at a single instance,
when can one serve one's two parents?
Thought arises from emotion,
and emotion arises from thought.
Guiding the source of emotion to flow abundantly,
leading the mind of thought without cease.
Having harbored sorrow throughout life,
I also bear grief until death.
Often, in solitary repose, I contemplate eternally.
Touching my breast, I injure myself.
In vain I ascend the mountain where my father is buried, with nothing to see.
Fruitlessly I climb the mountain where my mother is buried, what hope is there?
Tears stream down vertically and horizontally.
Blood boils up and wets my clothes.
Reflecting on Earth's principles, I blame myself.
I fear the perversion of nature, deviating from the proper path.
Gazing up at the Great Ultimate, I feel an enduring grief.
Thus I proclaim my sorrow to the vast Heaven.
I hope that the August Heaven will be moved;
yet how vast and distant is its recompense?
By day, my heart is shattered a hundred times at the Wèi Quē.
By night, it breaks into ten thousand pieces within my gut.
My heart and heart are continuously linked.
My thoughts and thoughts are endless.
In the morning, sitting alone, worries intertwine.
In the evening, dwelling alone, I pace restlessly.
My breath is obstructed, sorrow like choking.
My accumulated thoughts are like madness.
It is like when the new year emits its radiance, and spring days bring forth the sun.
Trees scatter a hundred blossoms, grasses arrange myriad fragrances.
Facing the joyful season, I have no happiness.
Instead, every sight brings sadness and grief.
Zhū Míng initiates its season, the bright sun shines daily.
Trees lower sweet fruits, branches meet to form cool shade.
No joy is felt in my breast.
Only endless sorrow entwines my heart.
Reeds are lush and green, white dew turns to frost.
Cool air penetrates clothes, chill winds stir garments.
My heart, without turning back, wounds itself.
My emotions, without external stimulus, grieve alone.
As for when cold ice has formed and cold branches have snapped,
forests shed yellow leaves, mountains accumulate white snow.
Migratory geese cry mournfully.
Northern winds blow fiercely.
My eyes meet things and my heart shatters.
My mind, moved by feelings, breaks.
Not a single moment allows a lessening of thought.
With the four seasons, my pain is ever keen.
Years pass swiftly and do not return.
Time flashes like lightning.
I imagine my kind face from the past,
grieving that it cannot be seen again.
I lament that the kindness of birth goes unanswered,
looking back, there is not a shred of repayment.
Sorrow and regret arise together.
Tears mixed with blood fall like hail.
Swallows arrive in early spring, unevenly spaced.
Wild geese soar in late autumn.
Their coming and going await the seasonal changes.
Their flying and crying respond to Yin and Yang.
Why am I not like them?
Opposed and at odds with the two vital forces.
Constantly enduring bitterness in cycles,
I never forget, day and night.
I see red turn into green,
and white turn into yellow.
Disturbing my nature and emotions, overturning them.
Confusing my spiritual thoughts and making them lost and wild.
Thinking of the calling cranes, my soul breaks.
Listening to the lonely young bird, my heart dies.
I grieve that throughout life, I have no support.
I cry out that throughout my life, I have no one to rely on.
Observing Xiū Tú's Rì Dī,
how could it be due to the teachings of righteousness?
Seeing the portrait at Gān Quán,
I often bow down and shed tears.
Suddenly, my heart stirred with unease.
Immediately, I entered the emperor's chamber to serve.
When Hé Luó caused trouble,
I blocked him with a zither.
Surpassing the renown of royal ministers,
crowned as unparalleled in sincerity and bravery.
His many ways of conducting himself.
Seeing Shí Tā's authority,
though his body died, his name was proclaimed.
Thus, loyalty and filial piety were both complete.
Consider Dīng Lán, what kind of person was he?
His home was in Yě Wáng, in Hé Nèi.
When he was old enough to dance with elephant masks,
his parents died as he reached adulthood.
He carved wooden images of his mother to serve,
always by his side morning and evening.
Liú Zhèn was busy providing for his parents and had no leisure.
He often fetched water from afar, and his strength was meager.
His bitter devotion moved the unseen spirits,
and sweet spring water emerged from beneath his stove.
Consider the ancient origins of Dào Shǐ in Lín Xiāng of Cháng Shā.
At that time, his father had died but was not yet buried.
A neighboring fire suddenly broke out.
He then prostrated himself on the coffin and cried out loudly.
A torrential rain arrived, and the fire died.
And Hé Qí was also like that.
His coffin remained entirely preserved in the house.
As for Wáng Xiáng, a yellow sparrow entered his curtain.
Kuí Tōng's transverse stone rose specially.
Shèng Yàn Zhī's mother's eyes opened.
Xíng Qú's father's teeth grew back.
Examining these numerous events,
it is also difficult to record them all completely.
The spiritual snake brings pearls to repay kindness.
The compassionate crow regurgitates food to nourish its parents.
If it is still so for insects and birds,
how much more so for humans, the pinnacle of the Three Powers?
The root of governance returns to the Three Greats.
The people are perfected by the Five Filialities.
Placing Heaven and Earth, virtue overflows.
Traversing the four seas, it is unyielding.
If one walks this path but does not practice it,
alas, what does the school of Kǒng mean by teaching?
These mountains and rivers are vast and boundless.
The sky is high and the air is still.
The roads are spacious and adorned with clear splendor.
The land is secluded and uniquely prominent.
It exhausts the ultimate peaks of the western Zhèjiāng region,
reaching the most scenic spots within the whole world.
Following the pleasant order, we ascend and traverse,
lingering leisurely and soaring freely.
We fully indulge in the elegant pleasures of climbing,
delighting in the temporary shielding from clamor.
Thus, we link our chariot shafts and harness our teams, lining up our curtained carriages and sailing our square boats.
Ten thousand horsemen arrayed in unison, a thousand oars contended in floating.
All are outstanding figures from the southeast,
and precious jade-like spheres from Yǔxué.
Dispersed, we gather companions; at ease, we lead our fellows.
There are no horses for hire in the alleys, few abandoned carriages on the roads.
We exhaust our efforts in a complete tour,
fully enjoying ourselves in leisurely excursions.
Then, alongside the forest, we emerge, and light skiffs ascend upstream.
We pass through the old paths of Qín Wáng,
and follow the ancient roads by Yuèchí.
We gaze at Túshān, circling it obliquely,
and cross Nánhú by winding passage.
It connects the splendid peaks of Tiāntái,
and draws in the long flow of Ruòyé.
Sometimes we float leisurely and gaze afar,
or perhaps climb the peaks for a quick look.
Thereupon, we pass through LèLín and ascend south,
climbing Fǎhuá and looking west.
There are the gurgling sounds of a rushing stream,
and then the winding course of a long creek.
It is both clear and bright like a mirror,
and also transparent to the bottom with no mud.
The path is steep and precipitous,
the ascent like a ladder.
We both climb vines and pull on kudzu,
and also rely on companions to help each other up.
We traverse the winding sheep-intestine paths,
reaching the highs and lows of the horse-ridge.
The fog is dim and vast,
the wind is whistling and chilly.
Looking at the great river, it is like a belt;
gazing at the vast sea, it is like a jade tablet.
Here, jade and silk were held,
and all the feudal lords gathered for accounting.
I imagine the lush leaves of Shūhé,
and recall the bewilderment of Dàgǔ.
Great beauty is transmitted on this mountain,
and lasting examples are spread among the people.
Then, we gaze upon the ancient traces of past worthies,
admiring the lingering customs of the highly esteemed.
We tread upon overgrown paths where grass has withered,
and push aside thickets that densely cover everything.
Renowned peaks stand majestic and towering,
deep valleys are distant and empty.
The spring forests are verdant and all green,
the autumn pools are clear as empty space.
They are continuously connected and intertwined,
and also vast and endless.
Indeed, it is a dwelling place for heroes and extraordinary individuals,
truly a cherished gathering ground for the soaring.
Beside high mountains, temples are built;
also, along the ridges, palaces are formed.
Divine spirits frequently appear and respond,
immortals and sages interact with each other.
Misty mountain air rises and forms clouds,
trees spread out and sprout in clusters.
Beautiful plants grow before and behind them,
auspicious herbs are planted to their west and east.
We gaze at the resplendent vermilion doors,
and look at the exquisitely carved treasure halls.
They resemble the exquisite monasteries of Dàlín,
and are equal to the lecture halls of Chonggé.
They are both bright and elevated Zen sanctuaries,
and also prominent and splendid chambers.
They span winding streams to form rooms,
and encircle rugged hills with long walls.
Evening clouds rise from windows,
the morning sun shines on eaves and beams.
Indeed, beauty is formed from curving crevices,
and light is generated by reflecting the scenery.
Clear Buddhist chants flow melodiously,
the sounds of wooden fish and chimes clang.
The construction is intricate, gorgeous beyond measure.
Clear streams encircle on all sides, spouting long trickles.
Winding corridors and pavilions, steep steps and moats.
Water mills rival those of Jīngǔ,
flying towers resemble Jiànzhāng.
As for their followers, some wander, some reside, some are virtuous, some are enlightened.
All are dedicated to ascetic practice,
and diligently committed to rigorous discipline.
They compete to nap briefly and recite scriptures,
all rising early with piety and reverence.
They recognize the swift flow of suffering and emptiness,
and value the fleeting nature of morning's shadow.
They delve into deep caves to achieve profound understanding,
and seclude themselves in neglected wilds to cultivate righteousness.
Some burn their bodies as an act of merit,
or incinerate their bodies to enter samādhi.
The fragrance of excellent incense wafts,
all carrying their tin staffs, reflecting each other.
Some flick their fly whisks and engage in lofty discourse,
others reside in solitude and sit listening.
The Zen practitioners are likened to lacquered wood (unmoving),
the wise scholars are like hanging mirrors (reflecting clearly).
As the Buddhist teachings flourished,
so the Wheel of Dharma was proclaimed greatly.
The temples were built relying on the mountains,
and the mountains also, due to the temples, had their spirit.
Indeed, it is where auspicious omens arrive,
and also where extraordinary individuals emerge.
Dragon-swords are produced from its ancient streams,
and the remaining arts of deer-machine (daoist practices) are practiced.
Xiè Fènglái came and lingered at ease,
Zhèng Fēngfǎn returned, sighing sorrowfully.
There are both ripples in clear streams,
and also overflowing gushes from flying waterfalls.
Strange trees grow luxuriantly to form forests,
rare fruits flourish and are not singular.
Mountain and sea pomegranates are planted in pairs,
two tangerine trees of Danlú are sown.
Plum blossoms are bright like frost,
yellow sweet oranges gleam like the sun.
Some bloom brilliantly in summer,
and bear fruit abundantly in winter.
The mountains abound with treasures, the land yields rare gems.
Gold and jade are born on its sunny side,
and coarse stones emerge from its shady side.
Divine rocks stand majestically and independently,
immortal dots gleam brightly and appear in isolation.
Who knows the abundance or scarcity of the year?
Seeing black and white, all believe.
Carved stones record the virtue of Yíng,
diagrams reveal the heart of Yǔ.
Cliffs a hundred zhàng high, peaks a thousand xún soaring.
How lofty and vast!
How rugged and precipitous!
Trees are tall and towering, rocks are steep,
springs flow rapidly, waters are deep.
Looking up, its vastness increases;
gazing sideways, its profundity is seen.
So distant and boundless!
So remote and endless!
Distant mountains emerge towering and interspersed,
nearby trees are dense and intertwined.
Cliffs are about to fall but have not yet,
peaks enter the sky but still hang.
They appear ceaselessly connected, obscuring the sun;
they look vast and open, touching the sky.
There is the strange form of a stone sail,
resembling a flying waterfall.
Indeed, it meets rocks and gathers mist,
and touches stones to form smoke.
It is both majestic and overshadowing,
and also towering and continuously extended.
It extends far to the rivers and seas,
and also connects closely to villages and fields.
Looking back at cities and towns, gazing sideways at markets.
It is called the guardian peak of Shénzhōu,
truly a famous river of the world.
As for Pénglái, it is known for sacred traces;
Wūxiù is noted for immortals.
Héngyáng is heard of in the tributes of Xià,
Sōngyuè is revered in the Odes of Zhōu.
How can they compare in beauty? How can they be as lovely as this?
Moreover, there is a wonderfully unique divine well,
clear and still for ten thousand years.
It is drawn from but never exhausted,
added to but never overflows.
Though frequently disturbed, it does not become turbid;
though repeatedly stirred, it always remains clear.
Through deep winter it is warm,
through scorching summer it is cool.
Different from the flying fire of Chéngdū,
how could it be like the token of sincerity from Shūlè?
It rivals the Sweet Spring in curing ailments,
and is like the Zīshǔi in reflecting forms.
There are also the hermit of Gūtán and夫人 Jiāo Lǐ.
They lived alone, practiced the Dao, completely secluded from friends and guests.
They subsisted on mist for eternal days, sitting in quiet meditation for a thousand springs.
No footsteps on the paths, thorns and brambles grew on the roads.
They diligently pursued the Dao,
and were detached and free from worldly dust.
Sometimes they wandered freely and recited poems,
sometimes they embraced their knees and chanted long.
They resembled Dǒng Shēng's prophecies,
and learned from Liáng Zǐ's insightful maxims.
They would associate with Sōngqiáo,
and be intimate with Yán Wèi.
Their forests and swamps are dense, birds flock to them.
Monkeys link arms and drink below,
birds fly wing to wing in flocks.
Swans and wild geese gather and reflect each other,
white pheasants gleam brilliantly.
They brush their luxuriant frosty feathers,
and beat their pure white wings, flying dense and thick.
There are also strange birds and fierce beasts,
resting in the river bends.
Tigers harbor benevolence and do not harm,
bears hide in the woods and grow fat.
Giant elephants several blades (long); male serpents ten *wéi* (in circumference).
Does and deer easily attach; tame rabbits all cling.
Like the immortal chamber of Péng Kēng,
but unlike the sea bird's awareness of omens.
Medicinal herbs grow in clusters, dispelling illness and halting old age.
The land produces longevity, the ruins abound with long-lived ones.
Similar to the valleys of Mount Nánshān,
comparable to buried treasure in a well.
Sending off Liú Wǔqí, how is it different from the Four Hoaries?
Furthermore, there are *niúxī*, *jīcháng*, *quètóu*, *yàncǎo*, *gānjú*, *xīnyí*, *kǔshēn*, *suānzǎo*, *zǐyuàn*, *chìjiàn*, *huángjīng*, *báijí*, *tiānmén*, *dìgǔ*, *ròuzhī*, *shínǎo*.
Shénnóng tasted these; immortal scriptures were created from them.
White rabbits consume them and gain spiritual power;
deer hide is ingested and one attains the Way.
As for fruits, there are *mùguā*, *mùzǎo*, *yángtáo*, *yángméi*.
Vermilion tangerines flourish in winter, yellow *gǒng* bloom in autumn.
Hawthorn and pears stand robustly side-by-side, persimmons and apples contend in beauty.
*Zhǐjù* are planted in rows to form thickets,
brambles brush the grass and wander.
Crabapples are comparable to *píngshí*,
sweet pear trees are likened to the Imperial Terrace.
Red raspberries, *yīngyù*, cherry plums, *hútúi*.
Green plums are offered in winter, purple taros arrive in autumn.
*Bànxià* form beds, planted in groups in spring.
Loquats, pear beans, and chestnut-like fruits are all included.
Some are dazzling red fruits,
some are luxuriant green shoots.
They become more beautiful against fierce winds,
and do not yield to harsh frost.
There are luxuriant *wútóng* trees,
and also elegant, tall bamboos.
Slender bamboo and *jiàn* confuse their forms and types,
*jīnguì* differ in their species and families.
They reflect on eaves and windows, intertwining,
wrapping around rooms and corridors, lush and abundant.
Drawing leaf shade from clear springs,
gathering roots in secluded valleys.
Where spiritual trees naturally grow,
where auspicious birds roost.
Truly a fine place for leisurely enjoyment,
indeed refreshing for the mind and eyes.
As for the cool autumn ninth month, when all plants wither and fall,
the *qì* is chilling and ever strong,
the wind is rustling and ever present.
Sad cicadas cry in the southern fields,
frontier birds sing in the northern courtyard.
Crickets chirp mournfully, heard from afar,
solitary *yuān* howl, making their voices soar.
Cold geese honk honk, resounding at night,
*kūnjī* chirp sorrowfully.
It enhances the freedom and abandon of the recluses,
stirs the lingering emotions of the wandering scholars.
All have the aspiration to go alone,
all rest their hearts on washing their caps.
Indeed, a good gathering for broad-minded people,
truly suitable for extending one's sightseeing.

The Mahāyāna,

It speaks of the freely moving dharma-carriage,

From shallowness to greatness,

If non-non-existence is expressed,
then the vehicle is small.
If existence is made clear,
then the vehicle is great.
Among all gatherings of blessings and good fortune,

Knowing that form is empty, it acts without decay;

Praise is insufficient,
so I compose this fu, saying:
Building the spiritual vehicle of the Mahāyāna,
it shakes the thunderous sound of the dharma-drum.
Removing the canopy of doubt from actions,
one savors the subtle and delights the heart.
The ocean-like enlightenment of the mind is full,

Leveling the broad field of the Eightfold Path,

Settling meditation in Samādhi,
extinguishing form-perceptions in the five aggregates.
Holding the drawn bow of *dǐ luó* (Trilochana),

Breaking the myriad nets that are about to tear,

Like foam that briefly gathers,

Achieving perfect conduct and auspicious departure,

Gathering the empty meaning of *sà yún* (sattva),

Opening the radiant flame of *zhǐguān* (śamatha-vipaśyanā),

Closing the firmly fortified walls,

Ah, the boundless depth of the one reality!
Alas, the countless forms, so complex!
Truth and convention differ, yet their essence is the same.

Inheriting the teachings of mentors and friends,

How dull and ignorant are all living beings,

The nature reaches its deepest point, yet becomes ever clearer;

It is neither emptiness nor existence,

It speaks of secrets to Mílè,
and delights in obscurity with Bóyáng.
Profoundly still, it reaches the ultimate,

Though it is easily obscured by phenomena,

It cannot be revealed by names or words,

The mouth desires to argue, but words are lost;

Therefore, even with the power of a single sound pervading all,

Searching its boundary,

subtly infinite,

reaching without end.
Dispelling doubts, it permeates uniformly;

It encompasses emptiness and existence, yet is profoundly still;
it embraces the cosmos, making all one.
Discussing its function,
one can be many,

It manifests the distinct forms of myriad beings,

It forms the deep roots of the five abodes,
and raises the bonds of the ten fetters.
According to delusion and enlightenment, it opens and obstructs;
following darkness and brightness, it gathers and disperses.
The four currents drift because of it;
the six realms wander idly through it.
The three worthies and ten sages are dim, yet linked in succession;
the two wisdoms and five eyes shine brightly and scatter.
Confusion and clarity, rise and fall, share the same ravine;

Its essence is nothing that is not,
its function is nothing that it does not do.
Like pure gold, it is not separated by rings and bracelets;

Hence, names and functions noisily gather, giving rise to bustling movement.
Phenomena are like ten thousand chariots with different tracks,

Contemplation is unobstructed by conditioned arising;

It is like a jewel suspended in a treasure palace,

Each is different, yet they enter into each other;

Dharma is not fixed in mind and realm;

A dust mote contains the realm of a great chiliocosm;

Last night, in my sleep, my consciousness secretly connected.

Then, I saw an extraordinary guest,

The clear and the turbid flow in different streams; ascension and descent each follow their own path.

The six thieves are gradually subdued; the four serpents are being dispelled.

Who are you?

The guest then replied,
“I have long heard of your noble conduct, but have not had the chance to show my respects.

Please grant me your esteemed reply.
Life is but a temporary loan, a fleeting moment like a throw of dice.
Swift as a red lightning bolt startling the sky,

Why not seize the beautiful prime of one’s years,

Perhaps ride a famous steed on a long path,

Sit in the west garden and summon friends,

As for those whose learning is abundant, whose family thrives, whose virtue is weighty, and whose fame is widespread—
unrivaled in Jiāngdōng (江東), peerless under the sun—
whose mind is a haven of righteousness, whose body a treasury of wisdom; carving gold for the Hàn (漢) court, wearing jade while traveling through Liáng (梁);
riding high chariots drawn by four horses, dwelling in cassia-scented homes and orchid-filled rooms;
having beautiful Yànjī (燕姬) beauties by their side,
and Qínnǚ (秦女) musicians filling their halls;
hearing the clear strains of strings and pipes,
listening to the clanging of silken strings and bamboo flutes—
what is this but the happiness of a lifetime,
whose fragrance will endure for a thousand years?
How can one live in constant unrest, alone with no laughter or conversation,
shaving one’s head and beard, disobeying parents, and turning against one’s lord?
With a haggard appearance, and ragged clothes,
lacking both agriculture and trade,
like countless knots in broken silk,
or a tattered cloak with a thousand patches.
As for the morning dew forming like jade, and the night wind chilling like gold;
old age slowly approaching,
years swiftly drawing to a close, a cold empty bed, a thin single blanket for sleep;
cutting off descendants from the lineage,
and forsaking companions and their joys—
if one takes this as the Way,
how can one attain the immeasurable Way?”
I then laughed joyfully,
and briefly explained the essence of my thoughts.
Slowly, I replied,
“I understand your proud and arrogant words,
which seek to lead me astray.
You wish to discuss greatness with a frog in a well, or a sea-kun,
and contend for light with the sun and moon using a tiny torch.
This is no different from a cicada comparing itself to a roc’s wing,
or a jagged peak matching Kūngāng (崑崗) mountain.
You are already deeply mired in the sleep of birth and death,
and intoxicated by the material world.
You only know how to indulge in wine, lust, towering mansions, and carved walls.
How can you realize the harm of excessive wealth?
How can you believe that possessing a jade disk invites disaster?
Delicious flavors delight the mouth, but rich foods rot the intestines.
Greed and lust lead to calamity; insatiable craving turns into madness.
Life is easily exhausted; the laws of nature are impermanent.
Singing in the morning, weeping in the evening, existing now, gone tomorrow.
Joy is fleeting, but worry and fear extend.
Moreover, the worldly turmoil offers no true tranquility.
Ten thousand sufferings rush in, a hundred anxieties contend to arrive.
Wives and children turn into shackles;
loved ones become like a net.
Private affairs are constantly plagued by difficulties;
royal duties are merely toilsome and burdensome.
Glory and splendor are like water foam;
wealth and eminence are truly like mountain echoes.
Yet, you are fallen and deluded, constantly harboring malice and cruelty.
Undutiful and unkind, without the Way, without virtue.
Your chest is perverse, your mind a den of thieves.
Arrogant and extravagant, your will is harsh and critical.
You do not practice benevolence and righteousness; who cares about principles?
You senselessly kill and injure, greedily taking what is not rightfully yours.
Seeing profit, you contend for it; encountering wealth, you seize it illicitly.
You lose your position and reputation, bringing ruin to your family and nation.
The rope of life is suddenly cut; the city of your body collapses.
Karma seizes your head; demons pierce your ribs.
You approach the icy pool and brave the fiery mountain.
You know your own pain, but who will pity your hidden sorrow?
Then, the forest of knives rises steeply, the mountain of swords towers high.

Layers of iron nets, clusters of ash rivers.

Water and fire rushing to the sky do not frighten them;

They fathom the utmost subtlety of all under heaven;

Thereupon, the gentleman who had approached earlier, hearing these words, pressed his palms together, bowed deeply, lowered his eyebrows, and snapped his fingers.
His spirit fled, his breath trembled, his mind withered, his emotions failed.

“Today I receive your teaching,
and I will respectfully follow your command.”
Jiāng Jiāo, courtesy name Yìnqīng.

To inherit the beautiful traces of lofty conduct,

Alas, my young son!

Therefore, I annotated the Wúwéi Lùn.
There was a young nobleman of an illustrious lineage,

listening to matters of gain and loss, he soared like a dragon.

shaking the jade bits and flashing gold.
He arrived at the gate of Wúwéi Xiānshēng,

"Sir, your wisdom and virtue shine brightly;

no matter has been left unresolved.

Zhuāng Zhōu as a minor official,

and Nífù (Confucius) held a whip without shame.

the noble scholars of their time.

but it is not the supreme principle for governing the world.
Although the rivers and seas consider it an honor,

The Sir smiled gently and replied:

Shēn Shēng and Wǔ Yuán did not achieve their ambitions.

also wandered restlessly, often failing to achieve their goals.
The men you cited,
though their emotions desired it, their will did not act.

hence they can be regarded as followers of the Dao.
Beyond this, what more is there to say?
I have heard that great beings descend,
extensively planting compassion,
breaking the cage of birth and death,
and ascending to the other shore of Nirvāṇa.
They expound the three vehicles to guide sentient beings,
and abandon all distinguishing marks to return to truth.
The wise do not see their coming and going;
the discerning do not know their beginning and end.
Thus, they attain tranquility, eternal abiding, and forever cut off divergent paths.
Without change or shift,
they forever cast away a hundred worries, calmly nourish their spirit,

and all is auspicious and beneficial.
To advance or retreat is natural, to furl or unfurl at will.

What honor is there in it?
What contempt is there in it?
You have gained something;
what have I lost?
Thus, the inner and outer of the world are clarified here."
The young nobleman looked ashamed and embarrassed,

Consoling Letter to Demons, Edict to Demons, Reply to the Edict by the Demon King, Announcement of Victory over Demons, Essay on Pacifying Demons.

An announcement to all sentient beings in the Three Realms and Five Paths:
