His might affects the ignorant below, innocent of suffering.
Leading a host of nine hundred billion, they water their horses at the spiritual ford.
Therefore, an envoy has been commanded to hold the staff of authority,
the general who examines and restores, governor-general of the Nineteen Heavens, the Great King of the Ten Abidings, Wénshūshīlì (Mañjuśrī).
He inherited from distant ancestors, his form shines with three lights.
His body is adamantine, his spirit is lofty and his form grand.
He responds to a thousand paths, with profound calculations and ten thousand strategies.
All beings are moved by his single self,
all anxieties are stilled by his single thought.
He deeply embraces compassion, and his heart encompasses the four gatherings.
Leading a host of sands of Ganges, he soars over this land.
Therefore, an envoy has been commanded to hold the staff of authority,
the general who rectifies teachings, governor-general of the Nineteen Heavens, commander of all demonic armies, colonel of all evils, the King of the Middle Thousand, Guānshìyīn (Avalokiteśvara).
His wisdom and strategy are profound, his axe of wisdom reaches far.
He clearly comprehends the six powers, and brightly observes the three solidities.
Sometimes he manifests among the myriad evils, rising with wondrous sharpness.
Sometimes he provisionally appears in the two nines (eighteen hells), calming their misery.
With a wave of his hand, iron mountains crumble;
with a breath, floating peaks collapse.
He can create unrequested benefits for the ten directions.
Leading a host beyond conception, wind whispers and tigers roar.
Therefore, an envoy has been commanded to hold the staff of authority,
the general who soothes and transforms, governor-general of the ten directions and three realms, the Bodhisattva-in-waiting King, Dàcíshì (Maitreya).
His subtle nature is serene, his heavenly countenance is clear and bright.
His body surpasses vajra, his heart encompasses the dust of the world.
His fierce will pierces the heavens, his axe of wisdom is wielded far.
Non-arising turns within his breast,
provisional wisdom responds beyond affairs.
What he intends to plan, he invariably accomplishes.
His might and grace flow together, truth and convention are spoken in unison.
Leading a host of eight hundred billion,
they are splendidly arrayed, awaiting orders.
The ranks of brave warriors fill the great chiliocosm.
Vajra warriors pervade the eight extremities.
All are eager to assist in the conquest, sweeping across the six directions.
Riding the precious chariots of various perfections,
guarding the rectified path of the eightfold noble path.
Straddling the fine horses of the six powers,
grasping the divine reins of the empty doctrine.
Bending the fine bows of the four dhyānas,
shooting the sharp arrows of provisional wisdom.
The renowned steeds neigh majestically, their light steps are agile.
Waving swords and flying spears,
they long hum, challenging the enemy.
And you, General, your family has been illustrious for generations,
aiding the imperial enterprise, serving the holy court throughout history.
Never has there been a fault.
As for your nobility, you are a Dao master, and five hundred of your disciples,
profoundly discerning the mandate of heaven,
received the king's transforming influence.
The Holy Emperor opened his heart,
bestowing upon all of them titles and ranks, granting them territories, their merits rivaling old retainers.
Their fame covers ten thousand regions.
Yet why do you, my lord, harbor differing views,
stubbornly entrenched in the border wilderness, stubbornly clinging to your ordinary position?
Poison and harm burst forth upon the common people,
disasters flow for eternal kalpas.
How can this not be sorrowful?
How can this not be mistaken?
In the past, you were foolish for a time, deluded and mad by external things.
Your heart turned to falsehood and you fled outwards.
Even a wise and discerning person can err in one of a hundred actions, let alone be lost for a long time.
We thought you would embrace wisdom and return from folly,
confess your faults at the Elephant-and-Wei gate, restrain yourself, and remove your hair ornament,
joining the company of worthies, finding joy in the Dao.
Your honorable name would last from beginning to end.
Yet you still cling to folly and guard your delusion,
stealing comfort in an evil position.
You rely on the mountain of ignorance to exalt yourself,
and depend on the forest of false views to wander in thought.
You indulge in the defiling dust of the six desires,
and amuse your nature with evil delusions.
You erect the high banner of arrogance,
and array the ominous formation of ignorance.
You stride broadly on the long path, lightly playing with divine artifacts.
You steal and usurp the heavenly palace, resisting the sun and moon.
Are you not like one who raises a hand to block the three lights,
or heaps up earth, intending to fill the four seas?
You beat drums, competing in sound with thunder;
you grasp fire, contending in brilliance with lightning.
Though your mind intends this, it is but a futile aim, and the task is difficult to achieve!
However, General, you have cultivated virtue in the profound springs,
your origins extend far back.
Your brilliance and splendor are evident, and your subordinates look up to you.
The foundation of your nobility is easy to ascend,
your past merits are regrettable to lose.
You can change the past and cultivate the future, turn around and submit.
Confess your faults at the Vermilion Gate and be in harmony with the Dao.
Then your family and state will both exist, and your lord and subjects will both be illustrious.
You will gain fame and security, clear-sighted and far-seeing.
Your dependents will be peaceful and content. How wonderful would that be?
The Great Master will certainly accomplish, and the ten thousand directions will flash with lightning.
He holds the conch of Dharma in hand, simultaneously wielding the sword of wisdom.
The axe of Dao radiates brilliance in the vanguard,
the spiritual drums sound in the rear guard.
When the divine bell strikes once, the ten directions overturn.
When ocean waves fly, plains and lands boil.
At that time,
Xūmí (Sumeru) will shrink into a speck of dust,
heaven and earth will shrink into a single grain.
Motionless peace will rest in the left lapel,
and wondrous joy will be held in the right palm.
Such is the divine power.
How can it be withstood?
However, Our Fǎ Wáng is of great benevolence and compassion.
Not wishing to attack immediately,
we temporarily halted all armies and stationed the divine chariots,
sending a letter from the road.
Hopefully, your misguided carriage will turn back.
You should quickly settle on a good plan,
bind yourself and return to the palace, entrusting your life to the royal court.
To enjoy a carefree and tranquil realm, presiding over the highest office,
who but you could do it?
Indeed, the sages, with their supreme wisdom, discern opportunities,
understand responsibility, and avoid misfortune.
To realize one's error and turn back when at one's limit
is what the noble person praises.
This is a high autumn for turning misfortune into blessing,
a good season for achieving merit.
In ancient times, when Xià Jié was without virtue, the Yīn king launched a punitive expedition.
When Shāng Zhòu initiated chaos, Zhōu Wǔ raised an army.
This is the constant rule of ancient and modern times,
a clear warning for generals.
Though our forms differed in those years,
and our lifestyles in the taste of the Way,
with humans and devas arrayed differently,
what can truly separate our thoughts?
Simply follow this letter and surrender your life.
Therefore, I express my deep sorrow in these detailed words.
I do not wish for the fragrant orchid to wither in summer, or its green stem to be broken.
Ponder deeply these sincere words and follow this good plan.
Do not allow your person to be ruined utterly.
Do not let the six heavens be harvested like ripe grain.
Gazing up with quick eyes, my feelings flow freely.
Much is in my heart as I write this letter.
Words cannot fully express my meaning.
Shì Dào'ān respectfully bows.
To the great Mèng Guó,
Chángyè Jùn,
Wèijué Xiàn,
Yìyǔ Lǐ.
From the Liùzìzàizhǔ Tāhuà Huángdì,
a reply to the summons, to the Gāozuò Dàjiāngjūn, Nányánfútí Dàosuífǔ Dàshǐ, Fó Shàngshū, Ānfǎshī Jiéxià.
The news arrived from afar, and I rejoice in this temporary connection.
Upon reviewing the meaning of your words, I am truly pleased.
I can see that the ministers of your great nation possess lofty禮義.
I understand that the general is open-minded and broad, with profound and hidden conduct.
You embrace mountains and rivers, encompassing the universe.
Your thoughts delve deep into ancestral temples, and your worries extend to the populace.
Your excellent spirit reaches a thousand *xún*, your true heart ten thousand *rèn*.
Truly, you are the strong grass in a fierce wind,
a loyal minister in a chaotic age.
I hope that if our paths meet, we will be neighbors,
without separation between us.
I humbly comply with human affairs and offer this reply.
In the past, when the Zhōu dynasty declined, the Six States contended.
When the Hàn dynasty's fortune ended, the world was divided into three.
Sometimes foreign barbarians invaded and poisoned the central plains;
sometimes internal troubles arose, bringing disaster upon the good and innocent.
To rise like a magpie at the opportune moment, to transform like a leopard at the right time,
this has existed since ancient times.
Why is it limited to today?
Only because the common people have accumulated much, Heaven sends down calamities.
Shìjiā Huángdì suddenly ascended to the beyond.
Sorrow entwined his ministers and concubines, grief saturated the entire land.
The Crown Prince Mílè nurtured his virtue in the palace of the mind,
like a full moon resting on a mountain, or a hidden medicine in a deep thicket.
He encountered the age of the hundred and six cycles,
when the succession of the supreme ruler was incomplete.
The feudal lords were cunning and treacherous, living in suspicion.
The eighteen sects' doctrines were uneven.
The ninety-six paths' altars and sacrificial vessels were intertwined.
Wolves gnawed the seashore, owls hooted in the mountain curves.
On the left, words were not recorded; on the right, events were not written down.
The national constitution and court ceremonies
withered and faded like frost and dew.
The imperial seals and jade discs
melted like ice and scattered like leaves.
Ministers resented, the people were angry, the multitude rebelled, and relatives abandoned each other.
They fled without refuge, wandering far away.
I secretly believed that if the times were peaceful, I would bathe in the imperial reforms.
If the times were chaotic, I would save them with weapons.
This is indeed the expedient adaptation of a wise person.
Therefore, I respectfully led a righteous army, forgetting food in my indignation,
climbing mountains to pull tigers, and facing rivers to slay dragons.
I organized military and literary affairs, valuing righteousness above my life.
The altars of soil and grain are not what I covet.
The throne is not what I long for.
It is simply that the mind-city has no master, and evil plays out in the dust of existence,
flowing turbulently.
The source of the mind drifts far away, as if in a great dream,
and prolongs itself with the eternal night.
Thus, by feigning sleep, I lament the people and punish the wicked.
First, I dispatched Jùmò Dàjiāngjūn Huáng Xuán Hóu,
leading the troops of Kōnghuá,
urging on the horses of Yángyán,
to the corner of Gānchéng,
to form the battle array of Fúyún.
Spears and armor gleamed, bows and halberds were arrayed.
Before the blades met, the armed forces were already defeated.
Next, I ordered Jiànxiǎng Dàjiāngjūn Sīzhú Gōng,
leading the multitude of gōngshāng,
to occupy the valley of Chuánshēng,
cutting down as they heard.
Next, I ordered Bǎihé Dàjiāngjūn Lánshè Bó,
leading the troops of Xīnxiāng,
to spread out the formation with the wind, making a thousand *lǐ* cloudless.
Next, I ordered Liùwèi Dàjiāngjūn,
leading the troops of Féiměi,
to be Dūdu of the face-gate,
guarding the mouth of Cāngmíng,
devouring everything without remainder.
Next, I ordered Qīchù Dàjiāngjūn,
leading the multitude of Xìhuá,
whose body-city collapsed as soon as the battle drum was struck.
The five armies advanced and fought, always victorious in a hundred battles.
Heaven indeed aids us, so nothing is left undone.
My concerns are not exhausted, so I personally went to the nests and punished the wicked.
With my military attire ready, I emerged from the empty cave.
I unleashed the wisdom of deep springs,
and stirred the might of mountains.
Relying on the army of delusions,
their numbers swelled to billions.
They concealed their spirits in the sea of consciousness, their shadows in the mountain of the heart.
I commanded the marshals to grasp their swords among the army.
The soldiers were conscripted, holding knives and forming ranks.
They filled the empty space and blocked the distant reaches, smoke flying and mists gathering.
None of them lacked heroic spirit soaring to the sky,
vomiting delusive clouds into the true reality.
Their high wind shook the earth,
startling the dusty waves in the sea of nature.
They struck at the official army of the Dao-stages,
spreading their sheaths on a frosty night.
Once the one mind perished, returning to the source became even more distant.
With the six loves already aflame, the house-fire grew even stronger.
They plundered horizontally and vertically, surrounding and attacking from front and rear.
The six奇 and three略 strategies were already stored in my breast.
Hundred-step, thousand-honor formations originally had no horizontal lines.
Thus, clouds dispersed and mists rolled away,
and Our Way flourished.
Thereupon, I divided offices and assigned duties,
implementing Our transforming influence.
I commanded the Wúlián Piàojì to tiger-crouch on Tānshān,
and Xìsè Jiāngjūn to dragon-coil in Qián Hǎi.
The sympathetic scholars had no refuge on land or water.
I commanded Jìdì Lángjiàng
to establish the office of Yīnyáng.
Qíngchén Fùmǎ observed their marital relations.
The army of love's water temporarily flowed, and the body-city was soaked.
As soon as the fire of desire ignited, the temple of heaven was burned.
Shànxìng Jiāngjūn had already been burned and drowned.
I commanded Páobó Xiàowèi with bow and sword at his side,
and Zhèndú Yīngyáng with halberd in hand.
The stern soldiers strictly guarded the city of bribes,
causing Píngfèn Jiāngjūn to vanish without a trace.
I commanded Zhèngqín Yùshǐ to temporarily halt his supervision.
Suímián Wǔhóu pacified the court's policies.
Profligate ignorance indulged the conditioned.
This caused the single horse of diligence
to cease traveling the path of the four endeavors.
The two arrows of Jiālíu
did not shoot at the gate of the three emptinesses.
Yǒngměng Jiāngjūn's wind and smoke ceased and extinguished.
I decree that Juéguān Dàsīmǎ establish a residence and initially practice meditation.
Xiésīwéi Dūwèi arrays his forces within the Sānyǒu.
The mind's origin is not yet calm, frequently buffeted by wind and waves.
The meditation branches, just about to flourish, again encounter frost and snow.
Ānjìng Jiāngjūn is buried amidst chaos.
I order Wǒjiàn Xínggāo to guard the peak of Tuónà.
The mountains of delusion have ten thousand blades, the fortresses of doubt a hundred layers.
Attacking those who return to delusion, I ask the way to the heavenly road.
I command Guānshēn Shíxiàng to extend like a ram's horn.
The illusory karma from family ties is dense like fish scales.
Therefore, poison moves the mad son, and wine awakens the drunken guest.
The true golden treasure is covered, hidden by rich, greasy grass.
Bótōng Jiāngjūn stands inert, as if drunk.
These are the guests from all corners of the land.
All are my people.
Now, the ten armies are spirited, the five generals heroic.
Seizing the opportunity, they rise to establish the nation's ancestral temple.
I, with a mix of joy and regret, ascended the throne, presided over the court, and inherited the royal enterprise.
Grasping the diagram, I received the mandate.
The weak and struggling wheel is boundless, fit to emulate the golden wheel.
My mind, with its spirited steed, has much to offer.
Let it serve as a dark blue horse.
Attire and caps are unified, chariots and writings are one.
I am about to fan a long wind in the burning house.
To shatter high chariots outside the gate.
To shed armor and helmets, and begin anew with the people.
The generals and soldiers are all lost, their wisdom and strength entirely gone.
The road is exhausted, arrows spent, horses abandoned, boats burned.
The mantis raises its arm.
Truly lamentable!
Truly shameful!
Dàozhí leads his troops to invade and oppress the feudal lords.
Kǒngqiū arrays his forces, sweating as he retreats to his residence.
This is indeed a clear warning from the general.
Huáng Tàizǐ Mílè, as the crown prince, rose like a dragon.
I, with my sweating horse, returned to court.
Bearing my sin before the palace gates.
The general was summoned.
I dared not heed the command.
My feelings are deep, my brush short.
I cannot express much.
I hope to return to the noble gentleman and meet him beyond words.
Bōxún bows his head, guilty unto death.
Guǎngyuán Jiāngjūn, Liúdàng Xiàowèi, Dūdū Liùgēn Zhū Jūnshì, newly appointed Èjiànshàn Wángchén Xīn.
Zhènhuì Jiāngjūn, Shàn Sànzǐ Dūdū Guǎngjì Zhū Jūnshì, Jiānjūn Chén Shī.
Shànxìng Jiāngjūn, Kè Yùjiè Dūdū Shèzhì Zhū Jūnshì, Sīmǎ Chén Jiè.
Píngfèn Jiāngjūn, Dànghuì Hóu Dūdū Hóngyù Zhū Jūnshì, Sīkōng Gōng Chén Rěn.
Yǒngměng Jiāngjūn, Qínxí Bó Dūdū Liùdù Zhū Jūnshì, Xíngtái Chén Jìn. Ānjìng Jiāngjūn, Zhìniàn Dūwèi Dūdū Guānlèi Zhū Jūnshì, Shèsàn Hóu Chén Chán.
BóTōng Jiāngjūn Zhōu Wù greatly.
The Dūdū Tiáo Dá and all his military advisors, Wáng Chén Zhì.
His actions and words were cautious. I, your servant, have heard that
when governance is peaceful and tranquil,
ferocious villains sometimes rise up.
When transformation is pure and killing is abandoned,
rebellious factions then emerge.
This is why Wénmìng, when hunting in the nine regions,
encountered the demon of death at Túshān.
Dǐngshēng, soaring in his chariot across the six directions,
met greedy thieves in the Trāyastriṃśa heaven.
Thus, their bodies were destroyed, their authority scattered, and their souls perished in Mǐnyuè,
wandering in foreign lands and losing their honored positions.
This was due to harboring treachery within and establishing corrupt practices externally.
Rewards were wrongly given for merit, and punishments were misapplied for the evil of officials.
Since Shìzōng Shìjiāmóuní Huángdì passed away in the Gùlín forest
more than a thousand years ago,
Tàizǐ Císhì Āyìduō has been occupied in Tuṣita heaven
and has not yet had leisure to succeed to the throne.
The Dharma-city has been temporarily empty, and the Brahma-wheel without a master.
The dusty realm rebelled externally, and Shāzhōu failed to pay tribute.
This caused the three realms to be alarmed by the wind, and beacon fires to rise in the six heavens.
Heretical followers, with their deceitful doctrines, transformed into strange customs.
The false Zi Zai Tiānzhǔ, the bandit king Bōxún,
was inherently foolish and suspicious, and afflicted by evil influences.
Arrogance resided in his heart, and attachments filled his thoughts.
He usurped the mandate of wisdom and secretly manipulated divine artifacts.
He indulged in the realm of desire and peered into the imperial domain.
Moreover, his governance and teachings declined, and internally and externally contradicted each other.
Sisters engaged in incest, and a thousand sons had divided loyalties.
Three daughters, dissolute and perverse, invited me to the upper palace.
Before their allure could be deployed, they brought about their own decrepitude.
Furthermore, Bōxún delighted in practicing minor ways,
and possessed some talent in debate.
He was stubborn in rejecting advice, adorned his wrongs, and was prone to great anger.
He did not heed the words of obedient sons,
but exclusively followed the schemes of flattering officials.
He watched for weaknesses in the kingdom and seized opportunities to invade.
His false envoys, the great generals and all the Kleshas,
seized the moment when the sacred path declined and the era was in turmoil.
Eight hundred kalpas passed without interruption, and the ten bonds were created.
Thus, he arrayed his army of desire in the sea of craving,
and spurred his horses of doubt on the high plains.
He held the reins in the realm of the two extreme views,
and galloped in the domain of ignorance.
When encountering the sages, he would withdraw his traces and reside in lofty places.
When meeting evil, he would unleash wickedness in the middle region.
He relied on dangerous terrain and multiple passes, setting them up according to the times.
Some sought glory and profit, feigning sleep at powerful gates.
Some, harboring resentment, coerced the masses, engaging solely in harmful acts.
Their spirits were arrogant, firmly holding to their partial views.
They were arrogant and prejudiced, not knowing the correct calendar.
He again dispatched seven envoys by post-carriage,
and three obstacles deceitfully proclaimed six doctrines to attract various customs.
The foolish accepted the teachings and washed their hair,
while the wise abandoned them and drank from the stream.
Soldiers waited in front, and beacon fires were readied for advance.
The false Four Heavenly Great Commanders, the Five Skandhas, etc.,
established their dwelling in the origin of beginninglessness,
and chose to reside within the realm of form.
They floated in the midst of the sea of suffering,
and roamed freely on the banks of the burning house.
They usurped titles for themselves and falsely appointed six offices.
They stole honor for fleeting moments, indulging in temporary pleasure.
Their leaders were few, but their laborers were countless.
Hungry soldiers and envious troops flowed across the fields.
Fearful warriors and sorrowful people filled the mountains and valleys.
Evildoers sought each other out, forming alliances in one region.
Different kinds of beings gathered in hordes, making war in the three realms.
The false provisional government designated birth and death.
The bandit king reviewed his troops in the five paths
and stationed soldiers in the three lower realms.
In life, they defied the mandate; in old age, they became bandits.
The five signs of decay heralded their time, and the four modes of birth responded to the world.
They blocked springs and sources, severing the fleeting flames.
Karmic forces roared,
leading the fragile and perishable to rush forth.
The three poisons wavered,
carrying all beings to their long demise.
Cruelty knows no kin, bringing calamity to nine generations.
Wrath and anger were mutually enacted, killing even the loyal and filial.
Then, they suddenly slighted the sages, slandered the worthy, deceived the true, and wronged the righteous.
They trapped the common people and ensnared all mortals.
They falsely considered suffering and emptiness as their own possession,
with the momentum of a sudden shock,
believing themselves to be as solid as metal and stone.
On the thirtieth day of the first month, at dusk,
there was a person named Shàn, with the courtesy name Zhīshí.
He came from the Daochang and announced,
"The bandits are not far from here.
You should quickly cut them down.
Otherwise, they will become a great calamity."
I, your servant, heard these words but did not fully believe them.
I deeply dug trenches and built barricades, only preparing for myself.
Then, in the latter part of the night, the bandit sent an envoy
who brought many rare treasures,
seeking to establish peace.
I simply drove a sheep cart and moved the army to Huàchéng.
his intelligence and schemes could not surpass mine.
His temperament was wild and unruly, difficult to approach.
I did not speak with him.
He departed, bearing resentment.
He then set up many treacherous devices, intending to invade and press in.
So, on the seventh day of the month,
at dawn, I exited through the gate of skillful means,
at the place of complete liberation.
I dispatched swift couriers to penetrate deeply, gathering confused multitudes from the sea.
I assembled Samādhi to form a single trench,
hoping to sweep away the Five Skandhas and purify all existence.
The bandit, relying on a secure river, resisted the imperial might.
Its waters were vast, deep, and boundless.
Moreover, it encountered a raging vortex,
with hail and sleet pouring down, striking waves and raising billows.
Sea gods competed to surge forth, and seven kinds of miscellaneous creatures,
some flying, some sinking.
Yaksha guarded the paths, and Rakshasa occupied the fords.
Blind and deaf currents drowned good fortune.
Those who wished to swim rarely escaped drowning.
And on the resistant bank,
they built great city walls and ramparts.
The walls stood like cliffs, the moats were deep, and the passes were treacherous.
There was only one gate,
overlooking a dark valley.
One person held a spear, making ten thousand men hesitate.
The Arhats of the Four Fruits were timid, and the Pratyekabuddhas trembled.
So, the crowd gathered and called for insight, hoping to advance.
After a quick assessment of capabilities, they all said,
"Perhaps we can immediately command the soldiers to cross the water."
Therefore, they prepared by collecting various grasses and trees to weave into rafts.
They were made to hold onto these and tread the waves, advancing straight forward.
I and my subordinates held onto floating bags
and went against the current.
Protecting without fail, we ascended to the other shore.
We divided the generals and soldiers, preparing chariots.
With one heart and concerted effort, we drove forth to attack.
Immediately, I dispatched Ānjìng Jiāngjūn,
leading the troops who observe accumulations,
to occupy the plain of scatteredness.
I also sent Píngfèn Jiāngjūn,
leading the soldiers of vast generosity,
to block the mouth of the valley of anger.
Again, I commanded Zhènhuì Jiāngjūn,
leading the multitudes of extensive relief,
to cut off the path of stinginess and greed.
Furthermore, I ordered BóTōng Jiāngjūn,
to organize the enlightened scholars,
to guard the path of madness and delusion.
The commander-in-chief deployed his forces, attacking from all four sides.
Battles accumulated successes, three in less than a month.
The provisional government feared that the troops might encounter unforeseen difficulties and be unable to advance together.
So, they urged on the six armies and stationed them in the realm of Avīci.
And the remaining embers, wandering souls, sought temporary peace in other transformations.
They drove flocks of dogs and sheep, intending to resist the battle.
They falsely assumed the might of tigers and rhinoceroses,
and summoned bears and grizzlies for self-defense.
Those with strange heads and different faces
breathed fire and wind, ready to erupt.
Those who carried mountains and bore trees
gathered like ants, aligning themselves.
We hoped to advance for the imperial house, to receive the mandate and tally.
To open up land for kalpas,
and stack the brilliance of sages, enjoying endless reigns.
When the former emperor ascended to the Dǐnghú,
his deathbed instructions were earnest:
he specifically commanded that from then on, virtue should prevail, and no warfare be permitted.
However, when the military headquarters received the edict,
it acted according to the imperial command.
It merely set up six ingenious strategies and then stopped.
But the mad youths remained boastful, still daring to rebel.
Although Bèiduō was sent to persuade them,
they showed no sign of repentance.
So, I again commanded the great general Dàquán,
and conscripted one hundred thousand soldiers.
Before a short time passed,
he greatly propagated the pure land.
He used fearlessness to adorn his body,
and with myriad wonders, he stood out uniquely. The dragon coiled around the bodhi tree, and the tiger gazed at Sahā.
When the ten titles were proclaimed once, the thirty-two marks responded to the prophecy.
When the teachings were briefly established, the eighteen realms gathered like clouds.
Thus, he beat the drum of extermination and emerged from the three empties.
He erected the banner of compassion, overlooking the eight difficulties.
He conducted military exercises throughout the great chiliocosm, displaying his might in myriad regions.
When his divine spear pointed briefly, the demon hordes lost courage.
When his sword of wisdom waved once, all evil perished.
He manifested his Dao-body to slay the demon of death,
and relied on Prajñā to annihilate the Kleshas.
He crushed Bōxún in the forest of immovability,
and extinguished the Five Skandhas in the realm of conceptual nature.
Afterward, he cornered those who held to their nests and hid in their holes,
those who were everywhere and nowhere,
and those who hid themselves from patrols.
Only one person remained.
He was far gone, at death's door,
beyond the reach of brave force.
So, I banished birth and death to the plain of nirvana,
and cast old age and illness into the realm of permanent joy.
I drove the three obstacles onto the highway of the six supernatural powers,
and threw the seven envoys into the realm of Sarvāstivāda.
The chief culprit was decapitated, and his followers were executed.
The remaining followers were not pursued or questioned.
All those who sincerely and proactively submitted
were commanded to remove their armor and weapons.
They were treated like registered households
and given distant titles,
privately settled in a pleasant land.
Five arrows were extracted,
and their foul diseases were thoroughly cured with good medicine.
Benevolent tonics were dispensed.
At this time, the karma wind ceased to blow, and the six dusts did not arise.
Auspicious clouds spread in all directions, and spiritual birds soared with wings.
They led the eight classes of beings, being inadvertently mistaken.
The twenty-eight constellations were arrayed for protection.
With folded hands, they idled in the hall, doing nothing but that.
Dàjué Tiānwáng and others,
who esteemed the ways and whose ambition was to promote,
cited old plans, earnestly admonishing and debating.
Unable to decline,
they tacitly approved the memorial.
Thereupon, the gate of sweet dew was opened, and the Eightfold Noble Path was brought forth.
With a thousand spokes, clouds revolved, bringing offerings to Lùyuàn.
The Four Heavenly Kings presented vessels on high palms,
and the two merchants offered provisions at the initial invitation.
Therefore, recording merits based on past deeds, Chénrú was enfeoffed first.
Bestowing rewards based on true principles, Yēshè succeeded.
Some kinsmen received honors,
others, brethren, felt the grace.
The cities did not disgrace the first fruit,
proclaiming the virtuous to the Ten Bhūmis.
Following ancient rites, they toured and inspected the four cardinal peaks.
Armies were mobilized in six cities, and troops were marshaled in eight states.
Grievances were settled above the three heavens,
and crimes were investigated beneath the nine earths.
Heroes and exceptional talents were summoned from the ten directions.
All nations convened at Jìuyuè.
Both civilized and wild lands arrived, and extraordinary scholars bravely emerged.
Thereupon, treasure vaults were opened to relieve the poor,
and the three carriages were brought forth to provide for all children.
The common people were comforted, settled, and returned to their occupations.
Thus, the body rested in the one vehicle, and the mind was firm in Pánxī.
Dwelling in the forest and gazing at the water, they proclaimed the imperial grace.
Following established practices, they spoke of freedom, inviting those not yet subject.
Benevolent winds enveloped the universe, and the light of the Way shone far.
Communication flowed in all four directions, and transformation spread without distinction.
Lawsuits were heard in the central regions,
and judgments were made at the place of Baoshan.
Immeasurable majesty shook cities and mountains afar.
Unimpeded wisdom penetrated mountains and rivers.
Hence, the land had no two rules; chariots and books followed one track.
The sun and moon shone with renewed brilliance; heaven and earth were clear and bright.
Six myriad followers
lifted their long sieges and followed the righteous path.
Ten immortals
abandoned the great river to take up their duties.
The steadfast sages, not deterred by a thousand Lǐ,
and the wise ones delighted in the Way, arrived in response to the call.
Laborers offered humble meals in Shīchéng,
and swift beasts presented pots of wine at Chángyuán.
Both internal and external were rectified, inside and out were at peace.
This was truly due to the sound of the Way spreading in all four directions, with its aftereffects instructing the east.
The sovereign was sincere, and his officials were deeply respectful.
Upholding divine precepts, they eradicated these fierce and ugly beings.
This is not something that my wisdom and strength could achieve.
I hope that relying on this one merit, I may gradually hope for more.
I will proceed with the previous plan for the return in triumph on the final day,
and report everything publicly.
Your servants are worthy of death, worthy of death.
Beneath the gate, the foremost divisions, though from the same source, branched into different lineages.
Rise and fall alternated through generations, with a thousand paths of belief and betrayal.
Therefore, the wise and victorious established their doctrine,
rising above the three realms through countless kalpas.
Illumined and enlightened, they initiated teachings,
yet failed to unite for nine periods.
Moreover, heretics and false views
praise the calf of Hèlā Dú from the source of nature,
binding the roots of robbers,
and controlling form and color in a realm of delusion.
With these partial forces, they contend against the middle way.
Thinking of these two or three, I am truly disheartened.
Since the former emperor ascended to heaven,
the treasured reign has been without a master.
The pure customs gradually diminished, and spiritual teachings were diversely established.
False demons seized the opportunity, filling the divine cities.
They falsely assumed true forms, idly speaking of emptiness and existence.
They drove the four kinds of beings, circulating through the six realms.
They rebelled against the heaven of desire, acting like wolves in the land of affection.
Their poison spread to the borderlands, and their cruelty flowed through Huáxià.
Even the invasion of Xiǎnyǔn into Zōngzhōu
and the aggression of the Xiōngnú against Yánhàn
cannot be compared.
I, though divinely obscure and having participated in the profound since childhood,
began governing at weak age.
My name was listed in the year of Dàtōng,
and I campaigned in this Bhadrakalpa.
Bearing the heavy responsibility of a hundred billion,
I am unworthy of the special honor of the three realms.
Humans and devas happily propelled me, leaving nothing to concede.
Thus, I ascended the spiritual altar and received this enfeoffment and sacrifice to heaven.
Reflecting on my many shortcomings, I am ashamed of the affairs of the people.
I labor diligently from dawn, having no time to rest.
I constantly regret that the borders are not yet clear and the true teachings are not unified,
causing all sentient beings to sink into the demonic realm.
Each time I reflect on this, I forgo sleep and food.
Thus, I commanded generals and mobilized troops to pacify the difficulties of the time.
Relying above on practitioners of Samādhi,
and below on masters of the Six Pāramitās,
I control the clear regions and the vast, untamed lands.
Therefore, when the six armies move like thunder, the three existences vanish like clouds.
When compassion spreads like lightning, the four evils are bound hand and foot.
Those who surrendered were like dust, and myriad were captured alive.
Only one, Bōxún,
fled alone on horseback; though a hundred paths cut off his escape, he will soon be tied up.
For now, let the five paths be cleared, and all beyond the cosmos be unified.
I desire to share this blessing and joy with all under heaven.
A great amnesty shall be granted to all under heaven, allowing them to start anew.
The name of the teaching of images shall be changed
to the year of "Becoming True."
From the morning of the eighth day of the second month, all prisoners in nets and snares are to be pardoned and released.
If one was misled by the four Māras,
wandering through the three realms, committing the ten evils and five heinous crimes,
destroying scriptures and defacing images,
all sins committed in the three times,
if they can repent and reform,
their past transgressions shall not be questioned.
However, if one absconds to the mountain of desire, harboring treacherous tools,
and does not surrender after a hundred kalpas,
their punishment shall be as initially prescribed.
Those who kill their fathers, harm their lords, injure their brothers, or commit incest with their mothers
shall be banished at once
to prevent future offenses.
The single Icchantika is not included in this amnesty.
Their罪 should be banished and blamed remotely, and action should be taken with divine speed.
Let this message be swiftly proclaimed throughout the ten directions.
Let those in charge implement it.
On the eighth day of the second month of the first year of Jízhēn.
Declared by the Minister of the Central Secretariat, Bǔchù Wáng Chén Yìduō.
Your servants Wénshū and others say:
We have received the imperial edict as above.
Your servants have heard that slandering the loyal and maligning the good
has happened through a thousand autumns without cease;
and treacherous officials and rebellious sons
have always existed through a hundred generations.
Thus, the Three Overseers spread rumors
and were punished in a enlightened era.
The five hundred turned their backs on the Way
and willingly faced execution in a sacred age.
Therefore, the king's might must shake
and blessings should return to the state of Zhōu.
Changing the teaching for a moment,
fortune returned to Lùgǔ.
We humbly submit that Your Majesty
possesses compassion exceeding a hundred kings and wisdom equal to a thousand sages.
You hold the auspicious spiritual ford and grasp the profound transformation of the diagram.
Your emergence and disappearance affect the great chiliocosm,
and your swift actions respond to all beings.
You take on subtle forms to guide the deluded,
and roar the sound of the Dharma to awaken the deaf world.
You even sacrificed your body for the Way, nailed your body to seek scriptures, broke bones for birds, and offered your life to tame beasts.
You abandoned the precarious body of countless kalpas
to attain the marvelous essence of a single lifetime.
Like a dragon hidden among the Four Heavenly Kings, you were beneficially seen in Jambudvīpa.
You lightly regarded the seven treasures and heavily esteemed the one vehicle.
You removed ornaments from deep palaces and reduced meals by the river.
You shed the precious crown in the bitter forest
and exchanged Dharma robes with a hunter.
Therefore, you were able to master the four Dhyānas and, in due course, traverse the six Pāramitās.
You subdued all evils as easily as turning your hand.
The three realms had no warning of conflagration,
and the four kinds of beings were free from the sorrow of drowning.
You further preserved the intention of loosening the net and the aspiration to pardon transgressions.
Eighteen came back to life, and all nations were exceedingly fortunate.
We respectfully reiterate this submission
and request that it be sent out for implementation.
Respectfully presented.
On the eighth day of the second month of the first year of Jízhēn.
Shìzhōng Chén Wénshūshīlì, Shìzhōng Chén Sàtuópōlún, Huángmén Chén Shīzǐhǒu, Huángmén Chén Shèlìfú, Huángmén Chén Xūpútí.
Prepared for the Weishìdào Xíngjūnfǔ.
Respectfully memorializing on the matter of the fair and public proclamation.

Prepared by the Acting Envoy with Credentials, Equaling the Three Excellencies, concurrently the Grand General of the Twelve Abodes, Marshal of the Weishìdào Xíngjūnfǔ, Senior Pillar of State, Duke of Jìn, Your Servant Bōrě, and others, who state:
Your servants have heard that the four Māras inflict life,
becoming a hindrance through the ages.
Wandering souls in the five abodes
cause suffering for sentient beings.
Therefore, the sacred wise ones of the three insights and the heroic venerated ones of the ten powers
have repeatedly mobilized partial forces and frequently launched minor campaigns.
We humbly submit that
Your Majesty.
Riding on great compassion, you initiated your reign.
Responding to a hidden providence, you arrived at the appointed time.
You swiftly took residence in the divine realm and brilliantly arrived at the Dharma ocean.
You recounted the excellent statutes of former kings.
You expounded myriad wonders in perfect sound.
You examined the profound strategies of past sages.
You gathered all beings into the Pure Land.
Three thousand Pure Lands jointly submitted to your majestic spiritual power.
Billions of continents alike followed your teachings.
Only the false mind-master, Ālíyé Shì,
presumed to use false names and instruments, misappropriating the populace.
He spanned and possessed the *Qiánchéng*, extending through years and sacrifices.
Chasing the utterly deluded into the realm of dreams,
they did not return from the long night.
Indulging in extreme chaos among empty flowers,
they remained as if drunk all year.
He appointed *Pānyuán* as his protective barrier,
and brought in *Xìlùn* as his strategizing minister.
Drowning the common people and causing disturbance with weapons.
Your Majesty, in accord with truth, governs things, regulates customs, and controls the populace.
Pondering these great whales and pitying this suffering,
you thus commanded your servant to raise banners in *Sèyě* and question the crimes in the *Xīntíng*.
Your servant dared to emulate the humble and received your extraordinary strategy.
On the sixteenth day of the fourth month past,
the army reached *Xīnjìng*.
Immediately on the first watch of that night,
met the bandit.
Your servant then secretly deployed strategies, covertly met, and profoundly connected, moving swiftly and imperceptibly.
Gathering warships at the ford of the *Liùdù*,
ordering chariots onto the track of the *Yīchéng*.
Encamped for three months,
displaying pure *Qīngfàn* to assert might.
Lined up formations for ninety days,
striking sounding bells to raise morale.
Ālíyé Shì,
remained stubbornly in deep delusion and could not be enlightened.
Clinging to desperate schemes without wavering.
Like a praying mantis trying to stop a chariot wheel,
like a bee or scorpion carrying venom.
So he dispatched the false Great General of Constant Action, Ātuónà Shì,
leading the sons and younger brothers of *Wúmíng*,
relying on their unscrupulous character.
He firmly defended *Qiánchéng* and resisted your servant.
Furthermore, he dispatched the false Grand Commandant of Self-Nature, Jiāpílúo Xiān, and the false Great General, Jiāzhānyán Zǐ,
recruiting a motley crew and assembling an ant-like rabble.
Shaking the border regions and stirring up a powerful show of force.
Your servant then deployed the various generals and directed the strategies.
Dispatched the Acting Imperial Envoy, Great General of Eradicating Dust, *Báchén*, leading the *Sìniànchù*,
and military affairs, leading the Count of *Dàopǐnxiàn*, founding Duke, your servant Qiúzhī.
Dispatched the Acting Imperial Envoy, Great General of Pacifying Realms, *Níngjìng*, leading the *Bāzhèngdào* and military affairs, Count of *Tōngzhēnxiàn*, founding Duke, your servant Rúshízhī.
Commanding fierce and heroic warriors, moving like shooting stars and turning like lightning.
From the various paths of *Fāngbiàn*,
they pacified the border regions.
Your servant Qiúzhī and others sought out names, discussed meanings, trod on shadows, and pursued traces.
Sometimes moved horizontally between secret chambers,
or engaged in shifting battles in the gaps of *Línxū*.
Affairs were exhausted, principles broken, territories consumed, and paths depleted.
Thus, the *Míngzōng* melted like ice,
the *Shùlùn* philosophy disintegrated like tiles.
Jiāpílúo and others knew that *Dàchéng* existed,
and understood where the profound lineage returned.
Each with several thousand weary soldiers,
all came to beg for their lives.
Your servant pitied their late awakening,
and allowed them to renew themselves.
Immediately ordered the *Cíbēiguān* Daoist Priest, Bìwúyuán, to provide them with comfortable care as appropriate.
The false Grand Master Remonstrant, Zhìdì,
harbored thoughts of surpassing the common crowd,
carried extraordinary world-transcending qualities.
He was about to offer loyalty with the entire state,
and returned as a captive of the perilous body.
On the night of the fifteenth day of this month,
holding the courage of the central army,
capitalizing on the disaffection of the outer enemy.
Wielding weapons in hand, personally leading the soldiers.

Then ordered the Acting Imperial Envoy, Great General of *Dōushuài*, Grand Emissary for Reassurance in the *Suōpó Dào*, Grand Pillar of the State, Count of *Chìtóumò*, founding Duke, your servant Āyìduō.
Acting Imperial Envoy, Great General of *Yánfú*, Grand Commandant of *Tiānzhú*, in charge of all military affairs in *Tiānzhú*, Grand Pillar of the State, Fùlóushā,
founding Duke, your servant Pósǒupándòu.
All of them, with their Dao surpassing the *Sānkōng* and their spirit roaming the *Sìbiàn*,
caused them to herald victory and defeat, clarifying right and wrong.

Also dispatched the Acting Imperial Envoy, Great General of *Píngděng*, concurrently acting as Chief of Military Affairs, Grand Pillar of the State, Count of *Qīngliángxiàn*, founding Duke, your servant Zhèngniàn.
Acting Imperial Envoy, Great General of *Biànmǎn*, concurrently acting as Grand Marshal, Grand Pillar of the State, Count of *Chánglèxiàn*, founding Duke, Zhēnrú.
Along with your servant, they were profoundly united both outwardly and inwardly, responding to each other.
At this time,
the autumn air at the border was crisp, the moon over the frontier was cold.
Banners and flags rose as high as the Milky Way.
Blades and edges were as pure as the frosty sky.
Donning vast vows, riding perfect penetration,
surpassing the *Liǎngguān* and vying to advance.
Breaking through a thousand gates and entering together.
Although birth and death are boundless,
in a single thought, their boundaries were seen.
Though *Chénláo* are numerous,
in an instant, they were seen to collapse.
The false Prime Minister, Chén Xiǎn, and false Grand Minister of State,
found their thoughts and schemes exhausted.
Seeking to survive, they closed their doors and hanged themselves.
The false Minister of Works, Shīzǐkǎi, and the false Minister of Justice, Dámóduōluó,
each rallied their remaining troops and entrenched themselves in deep strongholds.
Suspicion and doubt arose competitively, and distrust began to sprout.
Enduring collapse and peril without being supported,
they were thus doomed to perish and could not be saved.
Ātuónà and his false master,
lacked strong external support and profound internal strategies.
Their army was exhausted, their cities exposed and ruined.
Lord and ministers turned pale, having no means to advance or retreat.
Carrying jade disks, they kowtowed, and brought sacrificial animals, awaiting punishment.
Your servant immediately displayed Tuónà's head,
released Zhìdì, the prisoner.
Deposed that deluded king and established his worthy successor.
Then enabled their ancestral sacrifices to continue without interruption,
forever as a ruler granted territory.
Their virtuous lineage passed down through generations,
constantly performing the rites of tribute.
Thereupon, the ominous atmosphere cleared away,
like a harmonious breeze melting spring ice.
The ugliness and impurity were annihilated,
like a cool wind rolling up autumn bamboo shoots.
The *Liùgēn* were utterly transcended.
No worries of defense posts arose; the *Sānjiè* were desolate.
No longer any alarms of turmoil.
This is due to your majestic radiance extending afar and the unanimous will of the officers and troops.
How could your humble and weak servant have achieved this?
Overwhelmed with joy and relief,
respectfully dispatched the deputy general of the *Hòudéfǔ*, your servant Xízhòngzhī, to deliver this proclamation,
galloping post-haste to report.
The three springs successively departed,
early summer held the crimson brilliance.
Auspiciously, the appointed day was grand;
brightly, the mysterious evening was clear.
The *Púsà*'s spirit was harmonious and colorful,
subtly, born from transformation.
The *Sìwáng* came in due course,
raising their palms to receive the royal form.
Flying devas played delicate silk,
soaring and scattering *Zhīyīng* blossoms.
Along the ripples, dragons bowed their heads,
drifting stamens concealed the flowing chill.
Lotuses nurtured noble blooms,
bending their stems, offering morning glory.
Fragrant dew misted the four directions,
sweet dew condensed in jade bottles.
Precious omens filled the thirty-two,
heaven and earth shone in the purple court.
The sublime response was beyond feeling and thought,
peaceful and undisturbed, with nothing to strive for.
The mysterious root, the spiritual abode of the people,
divine branches displayed form and name.
Perfect light shone brightly like the eastern dawn,
golden form brilliant with the essence of spring.
Containing harmony, embracing all eight tones,
exhaling and inhaling, exuding fragrance.
Traces followed the waves of conditions,
the mind was profound with the great void.
The *Liùdù* enlightened the suffering world,
the *Bājiě* washed away the worldly fetters.
The benefit of wisdom permeated boundlessly,
emptiness and sameness transformed deluded emotions.
The great earth wielded its dark pivot,
clearly, the *Liǎngyí* reflected.
All myriad things were born and flourished,
clearing and solidifying, the profound sage appeared.
Shìjiā rode the spiritual assembly,
perfect spirit manifested the correct mechanism.
Interacting and nourishing, protecting peace and harmony,
spiritual knowledge flowed through nature and life.
In movement, serving as the lower body,
in stillness, being a mirror within nothingness.
The *Zhēnrén* spread divine transformation,
flowing and pausing, truly due to causes.
The dragon hid in *Dōushù Yì*,
his radiance drifted to the shores of *Yánfú Bīn*.
His carriage paused as the three springs departed,
flying reins in the crimson bright season.
The eight directions scattered heavy mist,
the nine heavens dropped fragrant dew.
Mysterious *Xuánqí* offered myriad dances,
*Bānzhē* played harmonious music.
Pure white condensed in the divine cosmos,
orchid springs permeated the physical body.
With each step, the *Sāncái* were at peace,
raising his voice, the *Wǔdào* vanished.
Not acting, therefore noble;
forgetting the marvelous, therefore divinely marvelous.
Distant indeed, the thoughts of profound antiquity,
thoughts entrusted, arising from events.
Together drawing spiritual vessels,
the image resembles that form.
Yellow garments, silk gauze texture,
dark robes trailing crimson and azure.
Spirit bestows grace upon the respectful,
traces move for those who act.
In the empty hall, musical offerings were arranged,
luxuriantly, extraordinary splendor arose.
Doubt and resemblance hung subtly,
I presume the author's feelings.
Thereupon, abandoning what was valued,
the desolate mind solidified into the *Tàiqīng*.
Blazing essence nourishes the moderate qi.
Vermilion li emits condensed yang.
Vast emptiness transforms hidden springs.
Gentle winds ride the harmonious soaring.
Auspicious month initiates the pure fast.
Benevolence moistens boundlessness.
The four sections revere the auspicious period.
Cleansing oneself, one ascends the empty hall.
Quiet peace harmonizes with spring radiance.
Evening vigilance sharpens like autumn frost.
Desolate, one recites in forest and marsh.
Contentment tastes of the city's edge.
Free-spirited composure refines the serene jaw.
Resplendent, gong and shang tones move.
The craftsman grasps the divine standard.
Riding the wind, he blows profound fragrance.
Deep and vast, the Dao's path is profound.
Gently, the principles of transformation grow.
Diligently, Vimalakīrti's spirit.
Virtuous sounds spread far and wide.
Encompassing, wondrously profound.
Ultimate subtlety originates from near concealment.
Briefly, a subtle and simple form.
Eight words resonate the Dao's principles.
Gathering troubles, practicing old phrases.
Facing danger, breaking intricate chapters.
Vast like a startling whirlwind scattered.
Bright like a night glow waved.
Parables, how could they truly represent?
Once the meaning is grasped, the snare is lost.
Permeated, the subtle practice merges.
Subtly, light dust perishes.
Desolate, the window of emotion decays.
Vast and bright, the divine carriage unfurls.
Who says the dark ford is far?
One awakening can withstand it.
I wish to be a master of ocean voyages.
Rowing the rudder, entering the deep blue waves.
Surging waves soak drifting travelers.
Profound return gathers at the Daòchǎng.
Jiān (間) and Hé Piàojì (何驃騎) had an appointment to observe the Eight Precepts Fast.
On the twenty-second day of the tenth month,
those who agreed gathered.
At the foot of Tǔshān (土山) in Wúxiàn (吳縣).
The fast was held for three days, starting early in the morning.
Initially, there were twenty-four Daòshì (道士) in white robes.
Pure, harmonious, solemn, all were peacefully serene.
Until the morning of the fourth day,
all the sages departed.
I, enjoying the solitude of the wilderness hut,
and also having the desire to dig for herbs,
thus stayed alone.
Thereupon, I waved my hand, bidding them farewell.
I had thoughts of the road ahead.
Quietly I clasped my hands in the empty room.
I comprehended the true nature of the external body.
I ascended the mountain, collecting the pleasures of the mountain waters.
Then I picked up my brush, dipping it in ink,
to comfort these few feelings.
I conceived the idea of establishing a Dharma fast.
The virtuous in the village gathered in a bright field.
We made an appointment for an auspicious morning.
Bathing, we went to a quiet mound.
Solemnly ascending the hall were the virtuous.
Brightly cultivating pure minds.
Graceful are the guests of the Eight Precepts.
Without hinges, they intertwine themselves.
Silent and tranquil are the truths of the five skandhas.
Diligently, the rough mind softens.
The Dharma drum initiates three exhortations.
Stirringly, the pure teachings flow.
Sadly, I desire to greatly save.
All in the hall are in the same boat.
Clearly, the sages of the profound outer realm.
Respond to the pleas of the innocent.
Sincerity resides within the inner chambers.
The three realms praise the pure rest.
Auspicious fortune returns to the Prime Minister.
Abundant like a floating propitious cloud.
Three repentances initiated in the former court.
Double confessions extended to midnight.
Singing birds herald the bright dawn.
Fully prepared, the ritual concluded its profound work.
Desolate, the courtyard guests departed.
Drifting, they followed the wind to their destinations.
Hesitating at the corner of the fork in the road.
Waving hands, bidding farewell amidst the departure.
A light carriage speeds across the fields.
Swiftly, like lightning, it dashes.
Calming the mind, I adopt a leisurely pace.
Lightly, I brandish the golden whip.
Stretching my neck, I gaze at the travelers.
Regret and loneliness accumulate.
Alas, my form is not I.
External things are inherently still.
Chanting, I return to my empty room.
Guarding truth, I ponder profound subtleties.
Although not a single continuous journey,
I can find release in leisure.
Quiet and solitary, I conceal myself in my thatched hut.
Softly, I recite "chūjiǔ" (初九).
Vastly, the bamboo thicket is pushed aside.
Gusting winds scatter through the window cracks.
Calmly, distant thoughts soar freely.
Gathering herbs, ascending lofty mounds, windingly climbing a thousand ren.
Desolate, overlooking ten thousand mu.
Gazing at the mountains, I delight in the flourishing pines.
Looking at the marshes, I mourn the plain willows.
Untying my belt at Chánglíng Qí (長陵岐).
Waving gently by the clear river.
Cold wind dispels troubling thoughts.
Cold spring water washes warm hands.
Vast and boundless, my spirit feels refreshed.
Respectfully, like Pán (磐) in spring thickets.
Reaching the essence, I merge with the three powers.
Vaguely, I lose my divine companion.
Roaming and observing the hidden mound.
Ashamed, I lack the elbow that connects to transformation.
Proudly, I ride the plain, uncarved block.
Days pass, months revolve.
Weak and grieving, distressed by wind and waves.
Drifting, wandering, moving with things.
On the way, high rhymes overflow.
Gracefully, I revere profound mystery.
Where is profound mystery?
Gathering truth, wandering among principles.
Simplicity is my nourishment.
Leisure makes me free.
Clear and bright, my mind is lucid.
Containing emptiness, it reflects nature.
Diligently, deep feelings depart.
Resplendent, tranquil thoughts refresh.
Hesitantly, I observe phenomena.
Never yet have I seen a whole ox.
Fur and scales have their value.
What is valued is forgetting the snare.
Sitting upright next to a solitary view.
Vast and obscure, profound thoughts labor.
Proudly, I control the reins of my spirit.
Comprehensively, I summarize famous books.
Traversing Laǒ (老), I sigh at the dual mystery.
Unfolding Zhuāng (莊), I contemplate the primordial beginning.
As I chant, clear winds gather.
Every thought is tranquil and joyful.
Looking down, I admire the flourishing substance and refinement.
Looking up, I lament the departure of the two masters.
Desolately, the Pillar-Keeper is far away.
Silently, Mángyì (濛邑) is empty.
Vast indeed are the deeds of a thousand years.
They dissolve and return to nothingness.
If nothingness, then what sorrow?
Ten thousand differences return to one path.
The Dao's gathering values profound contemplation.
Without form, I retrieve the profound pearl.
Sadly, the turbid water clarifies.
Almost forgetting to reflect in the clear stream.
Reflecting back, it returns to clarity and stillness.
Leisurely, it contains the Dao's talisman.
The mind is intimately linked with principles.
The form is distant from things.
Desolate, human affairs depart.
Alone, I reside with the divine.
Bathed in sun, radiant in the spring garden.
Distantly, I sigh at the passing of time.
Moved by things, I seek where to entrust myself.
Desolately, an ethereal melody ascends.
Still longing for the towering Tiāntái (天台).
As if gazing up at the rock cliffs.
Cold wind sprinkles the orchid forest.
Pipes and flutes play clear sounds.
Sky cliffs nurture spiritual lushness.
Divine sparseness contains moist growth.
Cinnabar reflects the green torrent.
Fragrant ganoderma shines with five refreshing hues.
Lofty and deep are the layered peaks.
Vast and bright is the stone chamber.
Within it is a seeker of transformation.
Detached from the body, released from the worldly net.
Embracing simplicity, firm in intention.
Waving profundity, brushing away thoughts.
Lofty and grand, the body's cliff decays.
Bright and clear, the spiritual abode opens wide.
Winding and turning, without creation or transformation.
Fleetingly, resembling a human image.
I wish to follow in the footsteps of such a person.
Taking lofty steps, shaking my staff.
Idle evil is entrusted to a quiet chamber.
Solitary and empty, yet true.
Wandering thoughts flow to the bends of the mountains.
Dimly, I gaze at the recluse.
Alas, the profound wind is damp.
Brightly, it departs from defiled chaos.
When there's no inquiry into the Dao, one sleeps.
What reason for a walking song?
The spiritual stream has no alarming waves.
The Four Peaks have no dust.
I shall wander its nooks.
Unleash the chariot, pluck the flying wheels.
Fragrant springs replace sweet wine.
Mountain fruits serve as seasonal delicacies.
Through dense forests, light steps freely move.
Stone chambers shelter my humble self.
In profound emptiness, I practice innate illumination.
Diminishing nothingness, I return to my primal spirit.
Vague, old vexatious feelings.
Fresh is the crisp, new qi.
Near, I am not a guest within the realm.
Far, I am not a minister beyond the world.
Calmly, I fear to do nothing.
Lonely indeed, yet I have my own companions.
The foundation of Kūn blossoms with simple elegance.
The light of Qián flows with easy brilliance.
Divine principles are swift yet not hurried.
The Dao's assembly has no overbearing display.
Transcendent indeed is the steadfast person.
Grasping the abstruse, seizing the vital mechanism.
How scattered my life has been!
My lot was not to consult Heaven's endowment.
Deeply, I reached no obscure rhythm.
Changing, I did not manifest brilliant splendor.
Gradually, years pass by, hesitating.
Long and distant, the cycle of transformation is eternal.
I crane my neck, hoping for the profound ford.
Imagining to ascend, but not yet right.
Though the path of life is thirteen stages,
The day has already reached the realm of death.
I wish to obtain the principle of "no body."
The Dao is lofty, tranquil, and serene.
Soaring phoenixes cry on Kūnlún's peaks.
Free will rises to the dark void.
Faintly, the spiritual wings turn back.
On colored shoulders, they perch on the southern nook.
Washing feet, I deplete the flowing current.
Gathering silk, I hold divine simplicity.
Singing loudly, I rinse my mouth with fragrant wine.
Soaring and descending, I ascend the divine parasol tree.
Rustling, I lean on bright wings.
Subtly, I nourish a pure body.
Long I contemplate the smooth flow of the profound.
I incline my head, awaiting the spiritual talisman.
The clearing of the Yellow River can indeed be awaited.
Folding wings causes people toil.
With hair bound in tufts, I upheld the Great Dao.
At twenty, I played with the double mystery.
Hesitantly, I cast off the long net.
With lofty strides, I sought the ancient emperors.
With wondrous humility, I ascended to the profound old ones.
Forgetting concerns, I drifted on Háo and Chuān.
With enlightened perspective, nothing is impossible.
All accumulated troubles are natural.
Examining principles, I loathe the spiritual kindling.
Clearly, the divine fire is passed on.
Joyfully, I find peace in the vast emptiness.
Leisurely, I delight in quietude.
Rich soil has no delightful taste.
Sweet sounds are not elegant melodies.
Broadening my heart, I entrust my form to destiny.
Diligently, I follow transformation.
Distant thoughts dwell on the profound!
How vast is the pure wind!
All things are gathered in glory and splendor.
The paths of life are linked in confusion.
Once the great clarity and truth are lost,
Tempted by things, wisdom scatters.
Once I heard of Páo Dīngzǐ,
Wielding his knife, letting his spirit roam.
If one can inherit the pure sound,
Nourishing life is as easy as pointing to a palm.
Riding amidst these incoming things,
Casting myself into this bright, silent illumination.
Transcending, advancing, unfolding, and retracting.
Forgetting concerns, attaching to the formless.
Intermingled joy fills my breast.
Spiritual communion flows with every movement.
Great harmony encompasses myriad distinctions.
Lushly, it fills the entire net.
A guest's journey, the body's native land entrusted,
Transformation unified with Heaven and Earth.
Sūn Chánglè
Made an image of a Daoist sitting in meditation,
And praised it.
It can be said that by contemplating it, he expressed his sincere heart,
Seeking to participate therein, like the yoke of a carriage,
Depicting the magnificent scenery of cliffs and forests,
Imagining that person to be here.
I admired its craftsmanship,
And praised its beautiful prose.
I could not remain silent.
So, I casually wrote a poem,
To follow on the left.
Its words say:
Cloudy peaks rise to the great wilderness.
Vast and grand, heroic mountains are spread.
Winding valleys hold orchid springs.
Graceful peaks gather beautiful trees.
Lush and dense, with subtle, winding paths.
Lofty and rugged, cutting off roads.
Within, there is a pure, rare person,
Sitting upright, imitating the Great Simplicity.
He strives diligently, like the movement of Heaven.
His weak will desires to have no hindrance.
His jade-like character surpasses wind and frost.
Crisply, he embodies pure interest.
Pointing his heart, he connects with the cold pine.
Closely knit, he understands the year's end.
His heart meets between two breaths.
Continuously, he advances in meditation practice.
Casting off one, he extinguishes sensory knowledge.
Taking hold of two, he is met by the spirit.
Catching cicadas, he stacks precarious pellets.
Stacking ten, also with concentrated focus.
His suspended heart is in a breathless state.
Subtly, he investigates and transforms coarse thoughts.
His profound mind calms shock and surprise.
Calmly, he indulges in profound conduct.
Having climbed the ladder to the Six Purities,
Empty and unified, he eradicates the Seven Abidings.
He departs into emptiness, riding on what is to come.
Forever, he is carried by that which awaits.
The Five Peaks stabilize the divine foundation.
The Four Rivers surge with vast currents.
In movement, he seeks the wisdom of the eyes.
In stillness, he guards the essence of quiet benevolence.
If one does not feast on coming and going,
Entrusting preferences has a constant cause.
Seeking the origin, he preserves antiquity.
Penetrating the past, he thinks of reclusive talents.
Pure as jade, below its cliffs.
With a golden sound, he rinses by the Yí River.
Folding his brilliance, he conceals the myriad mists.
Shaking his robes, he brushes off dust.
His traces follow the Dao, contracting like a silkworm.
His Dao extends like a soaring dragon.
His eminence is not like Dān Bào's punishment.
His lot is not the truth of Shǒuyáng.
He lets out a long whistle, returning to the forest ridge.
Desolately, he submits to Táo Jūn.
Preface says:
What is meant by the term Sānmèi?
It is dedicated thought and tranquil contemplation.
When thought is dedicated, the will is unified and undivided.
When contemplation is tranquil, qi is empty and the spirit is clear.
When qi is empty, wisdom is calm in its illumination.
When the spirit is clear, there is no obscurity that cannot be penetrated.
These two are the subtle symbols of nature,
converging into one to exert their function.
Therefore, one guards idly and reverently,
and thereby senses phenomena and communicates with the numinous.
One controls the mind with rectitude,
and every action must reach the subtle.
This is borrowing cultivation to solidify the spirit,
accumulating merit to transform one's nature.
How much more so for those who, like corpses, sit in oblivion, whose minds are deeply absorbed to the utmost, whose wisdom spans the cosmos, and who silently tread the great path!
Let me speak of its beginning.
When a Púsà first ascends the path,
just peering into the mysterious gate,
their body is still and acts without acting, yet there is nothing they do not do.
When their spiritual transformations occur,
they cause length and shortness to overturn their usual measures,
and great and small to encompass each other.
The three lights turn their reflections to shift their illumination,
and heaven and earth roll up and unfold within their embrace.
Moreover, among the various Sānmèi,
their names are very numerous.
Among those with high merit and easy progress, Nianfó is foremost.
Why? One who exhausts the mysterious and reaches the ultimate tranquility, whose venerable title is Rúlái,
embodies the spirit and unites transformations, responding without fixed patterns.
Therefore, those who enter this state
become oblivious and lose awareness.
They immediately take what is perceived as a mirror.
When clear, inner illumination reflects, and myriad phenomena arise.
It is not reached by the ears and eyes,
yet hearing and seeing occur.
Thereupon, beholding the deeply tranquil and empty mirror-like body,
they awaken to the pure and clear oneness of the numinous root, naturally.
Observing the mysterious sound knocking at the heart's listening,
defilements dissipate, and stagnant emotions melt into clarity.
If it were not for the utmost subtlety under heaven,
who could achieve this?
From this perspective,
the perception of a single glimpse
can unleash the accumulated defilements of long practice,
and dispel the heavy delusion of the ignorant world.
If we were to compare it to the objects of concentration of ordinary people,
we certainly could not speak of their superiority or inferiority.
Its place is known.
Therefore, all the sages who uphold the Dharma contemplate the agreement of the one principle,
feeling the passing shadow of an inch of time,
fearing that future accumulations are not yet amassed.
Thus, they cleanse their minds in the Dharma hall, straighten their collars towards purity,
forgetting sleep at midnight, diligently working from dawn till dusk.
They hope that the merit of their steadfast devotion
will allow them to fulfill the aspirations of the three vehicles,
to cross the ford,
and go forth with the nine kinds of beings.
They look up to aid and leap forward with the rising momentum of "pulling out the mào grass,"
and stoop to guide the weak in progress,
whipping them from behind.
In light of this,
the brushwork of the many chapters
is surely not merely literary composition!
Subtle function lies in the obscure,
traversing being to contemplate non-being.
The spirit penetrates from obscurity,
consciousness illuminates the coarse.
Accumulating the subtle leads naturally,
merit is fundamentally empty due to cause.
Extinguishing those three contemplations,
forgetting this minute remainder, the vast river begins from emptiness.
Principle is profound, penetrating the subtle.
Melting away self-satisfaction,
it expands the spiritual radiance.
The mind's realm is vast and distant,
one attains without treading on the mechanism.
Using it for emptiness,
meeting it with rarity. The spirit relies on heavenly stillness,
its perfect reflection shines like morning clouds.
Responding to transformation and sensing, it forms groups with phenomena.
It responds without fixed patterns,
the recipient naturally receives.
Tranquil like a deep mirror,
golden water and dusty confusion spontaneously arise.
The wisdom and knowledge of past lives
are entrusted to profound individuals.
Hoping to borrow their hidden power,
to transform minute efforts into great merit.
It is deep and measurable.
The thought of reaching the ultimate
focuses the mind on the Western 極.
How subtle are the enlightened ones,
whose merit is profound through former leaves.
Dragons lurk in the nine marshes,
civilization has not yet connected.
Fate brings their convergence,
the spirit makes its tracks sparse.
Dreams and souls intertwine,
inspiring these sages.
Striking echoes pierce the deep mountains,
arousing profound sincerity.
The flowing sound is in the ear,
joyfully embarking on the morning journey.
Obeying the command, they travel by night,
a hundred thoughts merge into the obscure.
Pledges are made from the heart,
and transformation descends as a spirit.
The return path is about to open,
the spiritual gate reopens.
Divine功 is hard to plan,
it waits for diminution to increase.
Believing in the Dao, one forgets form,
joy comes unexpectedly.
If not for such wise people,
who could fathom the mysterious strategy?
The diligent profound craftsmen,
the Dao is profound, numbers are exhausted.
Like that great ocean,
a hundred rivers all flow into it.
The shore does not await a ferry,
the path has no turning back.
The three streams open their sources,
and are extinguished therein together.
How wonderful is true enlightenment,
embodying the spirit through non-being.
Motion does not reach being,
stillness does not approach emptiness.
It transforms yet is not altered,
it images yet is not a copy.
It reflects that true nature,
and mirrors this myriad coarseness.
Heaven is long-lived, but life is short.
The world is fleeting, but the Dao is vast.
The Zen path is wide and far-reaching,
the sea of love churns light boats.
The dust of defilement has never reached its limit,
how can the mind-tree be measured?
Why wash away the dust of emotion?
The water of rectitude has a clear stream.

May we rely on the power of the eight liberations,
forever extinguishing the greed for the six dusts.
Our emperor follows the supreme Way,
setting forth to where it leads.
The traveling carriage turns its vermilion hubs,

Flying bridges connect ravine paths,

Clustered flowers overlook distant steps,
divided streams encircle winding courtyards.
Who says this is not a supreme realm?
Cloud-shrouded mountains stand uniquely here.
Worldly emotions are indeed easy to discard,
the nature of the Way is truly difficult to stain.
Receiving grace and upholding the teachings,

The divine mind contemplates the order of things,

Sparse forests reveal the carriage's shadow,
the wind carries the sound of pipes far away.
Stopping the followers, they rest in the sacred realm,
unhitching the carriage, they halt at the mountain peak.
The year returns, the season is already mid-spring,

Short leaves grow on tall trees,
sparse blossoms unfurl on early branches.
Distant peaks are obscured by clouds,
drifting smoke is mixed with falling rain.
Again, I, the one who fills a humble post,

Once one knows the treasure in the robe,
one laments the abundance of the compassionate land.

Just entering the fragrant mountain path,

Buying a mountain, he stood high above his age,
riding a cup, he crossed the river.
Dharma rain falls from time to time,
fragrant clouds are numerous, piece by piece.
If only he could ascend as an immortal,
to rescue those caught in the worldly net.
Having entered the Way in the Dragon Palace,
he bade farewell to glory in the Phoenix Palace.
The meditation niche is pure with eight contemplations,
the cave of righteousness is light with four dusts.
Fragrant canopies rise as clouds of Dharma,

Naturally forgetting attachment,

The realm of blessings is newly opened,

Willow branches grow into towering trees,

Stone seats respond to morning lectures,
mountain niches imitate night meditation.
This is surely not the city of Shèwèi (舍衛),
where land was sold for gold coins.
The Vulture Peak has a three-storied pagoda,
the hermitage garden has a lecture hall.
Tame crows follow the meal bell,
familiar beasts encircle the meditation couch.
Picking chrysanthemums, the mountain has no wine,
burning pines, the night has fragrance.
Fortunate to be with such noble and excellent ones,
here, the mind-king is polished.
The Emperor, with supreme wisdom, governs the world, shining brilliantly in his reign.
He controls nine generations and drives a hundred kings.
His ultimate virtue reaches above, his profound benevolence flows below.
His awe-inspiring power spreads west, his renown and teachings gradually extend east.
He promulgates policies in the great palace, sets rituals in the great hall.
He performs music in the open fields, holds councils at Miáoshān (苗山).
Heaven does not begrudge treasures, spirits do not hold back gifts.
Fish and birds show forth wonders, mountains and lakes present blessings.
Chinese and barbarians alike follow, the hidden and the manifest are all in order.
The eight governmental policies are well-ordered, the six hexagrams declare peace.
Yet, he rests his aspirations in the profound and mysterious, concentrates his spirit in emptiness and tranquility.
He looks down on the narrow world, considers the lingering forms of existence.
He rescues the pure people from the vessel of suffering,
saves the realm of desire from the perilous city.
His body and mind ascend to the realm of pure joy,
all living beings look up to the power of his regulation and guidance.
The Empress, with profound virtue, sustains the world, her rightful position equals heaven.
Her Way surpasses Shàolíng (邵陵), her achievements exceed Shēnsì (莘姒).
Clouds of wisdom rise in the morning;
all four kinds of sentient beings await their gathering.
Lamps of compassion burn at night;
the nine regions are illuminated by their residual light.
Then, gazing at Cānxū (參墟),
it is truly the ancient land of Táng (唐), with mountains and rivers surrounding it like a collar and belt, majestic and secluded.
In the eastern suburbs, a supreme site, a precious monastery was constructed.
It stands as if transformed and created, dimly emerging as if rising from the earth.
Afterward, as the sun entered the western sector, and the qi was in the middle of Nánlǚ (南呂).
Autumn winds stirred the wilderness, white dew heralded the cold.
The sagely ruler, eloquent and discerning, toured the regions, adapting to the seasons to nurture all beings.
Six dragons advanced the imperial carriage, seven sages rode in unison.
Jade-green plumes raised banners, carved jade wheels moved slowly.
Asking about a hundred years, he halted his chariot;
addressing myriad spirits, he presented his staff of authority.
Those like Xióngqú (熊渠) who joyfully flew,
entered and joined the central guard.
Companions of the tiger hall and golden gate,
gazed afar at the attendant carriages.
Approaching the lower capital, they encountered this pure land.
All delighted in the view of Vulture Peak,
together rejoiced in the visit to the Dragon Palace.
They joined hands, purified their hearts, and extended their sincerity and reverence.
They meditated on emptiness, embraced tranquility, and then composed songs.
Although the act is like striking the chariot shaft, and the meaning is like tapping a horn,
it is also to praise the glorious achievements and commend the excellent beauty.
How can it compare to Gāoshuò's (臯朔) rhetoric, merely presenting male blessings,
or Wánggǔ's (王谷) insect-script, merely likening female embroidery?
